7139 if (nc <= 0x20) {
7140 c = skip_to_action();
7141 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7142 goto done;
7143 nc = static_cast<unsigned char>(c);
7144 }
7145 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(nc == ',')) {
7146 ++p_;
7147 // + 60-A: fused key scan; in_obj = bit1 of cur_state_
7148 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(depth_ > 0 && (cur_state_ & 0b010u))) {
7149 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(p_ < end_)) {
7150 unsigned char fc = static_cast<unsigned char>(*p_);
7151 if (fc <= 0x20) {
7152 fc = static_cast<unsigned char>(skip_to_action());
7153 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7154 goto done;
7155 }
7156 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(fc == '"')) {
7157 char vc = scan_key_colon_next(p_ + 1, nullptr);
7158 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(vc == 0))
7159 goto fail;
7160 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7161 goto done;
7162 c = vc;
7163 continue; // directly to value
7164 }
7165 c = static_cast<char>(fc);
7166 continue;
7167 }
7168 goto done;
7169 }
7170 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(depth_ == 0)) goto done;
7171 c = skip_to_action();
7172 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7173 goto done;
7174 continue; // bypass loop bottom separator logic, go straight to
7175 // next token
7176 }
7177 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(nc == ']' || nc == '}')) {
7178 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(depth_ == 0))
7179 goto fail;
7180 --depth_;
7181 // restore parent state
7182 cur_state_ = cstate_stack_[depth_];
7183 push_end(nc == '}' ? TapeNodeType::ObjectEnd
7184 : TapeNodeType::ArrayEnd,
7185 static_cast<uint32_t>(p_ - data_));
7186 ++p_;
7187 c = skip_to_action();
7188 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7189 goto done;
7190 continue; // End handled inline!
7191 }
7192 }
7193 break;
7194 }
7195 default:
7196 goto fail;
7197 } // switch
7198 if (depth_ == 0) break;
7199
7200 // ── Inline separator + peek-next optimization ─────────
7201 // After each token, consume ':' or ',' inline (no switch iteration).
7202 // After the separator, try a direct *p_ peek before calling
7203 // skip_to_action. For JSON like "key":value or value,"next", the char
7204 // after sep is > 0x20.
7205 c = skip_to_action();
7206 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7207 break;
7208 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(c == ':' || c == ',')) {
7209 ++p_; // consume separator
7210 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7211 break;
7212 // Peek: if next char is already an action byte, skip
7213 // skip_to_action()
7214 unsigned char nc = static_cast<unsigned char>(*p_);
7215 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(nc > 0x20)) {
7216 c = static_cast<char>(nc); // direct dispatch, zero function call
7217 } else {
7218 c = skip_to_action(); // whitespace present, do SWAR skip
7219 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(p_ >= end_))
7220 break;
7221 }
7222 }
7223
7224 } // while
7225
7226 done:
7227 doc_->tape.head = tape_head_;
7228 if (!allow_trailing) {
7229 while (p_ < end_) {
7230 if (static_cast<unsigned char>(*p_) > 0x20)
7231 return false;
7232 ++p_;
7233 }
7234 }
7235 return depth_ == 0 && tape_head_ > doc_->tape.base;
7236
7237 fail:
7238 doc_->tape.head = tape_head_;
7239 return false;
7240 }
7241
7242#if QBUEM_HAS_AVX512 || QBUEM_HAS_NEON
7243 // ── Stage 2 — index-based parse loop ───────────────────────
7244 //
7245 // Key differences from parse():
7246 // • No skip_to_action() calls — structural positions pre-computed by
7247 // Stage 1 • String length = O(1) lookup: close_offset - open_offset - 1
7248 // • No double-pump logic needed — sequential index traversal suffices •
7249 // Same push() / push_end() / cur_state_ as parse() for correctness
7250 //
7251 // Stage 1 guarantees:
7252 // • Every '"' in the index is a real (unescaped) quote
7253 // • After each opening '"', the VERY NEXT index entry is the closing
7254 // '"' • structural chars inside strings are excluded from the index •
7255 // value starts (digit/'-'/'t'/'f'/'n') are marked via vstart
7256 [[gnu::hot]] bool parse_staged(const Stage1Index &s1, bool allow_trailing = false) noexcept {
7257 const uint32_t *pos = s1.positions;
7258 const uint32_t n = s1.count;
7259
7260 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(n == 0)) {
7261 doc_->tape.head = tape_head_;
7262 return false; // empty / all-whitespace JSON is invalid
7263 }
7264
7265 // last_off tracks the byte offset just past the end of the last
7266 // consumed atom. After the for-loop we scan [last_off, end_) for stray
7267 // non- whitespace, which catches things like "nulls" or "true garbage".
7268 uint32_t last_off = 0;
7269
7270 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n;) {
7271 const uint32_t off = pos[i++];
7272 const char c = data_[off];
7273
7274 switch (static_cast<ActionId>(kActionLut[static_cast<uint8_t>(c)])) {
7275
7276 case kActObjOpen: {
7277 // A nested object/array is not a valid object key (RFC 8259 §4) —
7278 // matches parse() so both engines accept/reject identically.
7279 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(cur_state_ & 0b001u))
7280 goto s2_fail;
7281 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(depth_ >= kMaxDepth))
7282 goto s2_fail;
7283 push(TapeNodeType::ObjectStart, 0, off);
7284 // save parent state, init new object context.
7285 cstate_stack_[depth_] = cur_state_;
7286 cur_state_ = 0b011u; // in_obj=1, is_key=1, has_elem=0
7287 ++depth_;
7288 last_off = off + 1;
7289 break;
7290 }
7291
7292 case kActArrOpen: {
7293 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(cur_state_ & 0b001u))
7294 goto s2_fail; // not a valid object key (RFC 8259 §4)
7295 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(depth_ >= kMaxDepth))
7296 goto s2_fail;
7297 push(TapeNodeType::ArrayStart, 0, off);
7298 // save parent state, init new array context.
7299 cstate_stack_[depth_] = cur_state_;
7300 cur_state_ = 0b000u; // in_obj=0, is_key=0, has_elem=0
7301 ++depth_;
7302 last_off = off + 1;
7303 break;
7304 }
7305
7306 case kActClose: {
7307 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(depth_ == 0))
7308 goto s2_fail;
7309 --depth_;
7310 // restore parent state (no mask arithmetic needed).
7311 cur_state_ = cstate_stack_[depth_];
7312 push_end(c == '}' ? TapeNodeType::ObjectEnd : TapeNodeType::ArrayEnd,
7313 off);
7314 last_off = off + 1;
7315 break;
7316 }
7317
7318 case kActString: {
7319 // Stage 1 guarantees: pos[i] is the closing '"' of this string.
7320 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(i >= n))
7321 goto s2_fail;
7322 const uint32_t close_off = pos[i++]; // consume closing '"'
7323 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(close_off - off - 1 > 0xFFFFu))
7324 goto s2_fail; // string longer than 16-bit length field
7325 push(TapeNodeType::StringRaw,
7326 static_cast<uint16_t>(close_off - off - 1),
7327 off + 1); // offset = first char inside string
7328 last_off = close_off + 1;
7329 break;
7330 }
7331
7332 // kActColon / kActComma are no longer emitted by
7333 // stage1_scan_avx512. push() cur_state_ handles key↔value
7334 // alternation internally.
7335
7336 case kActNumber: {
7337 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(cur_state_ & 0b001u))
7338 goto s2_fail; // a number is not a valid object key (RFC 8259 §4)
7339 // Scan integer/float from data_[off]; push raw token.
7340 const char *s = data_ + off;
7341 const char *pn = s;
7342 if (*pn == '-')
7343 ++pn;
7344 // SWAR-8 integer digit scan
7345 while (pn + 8 <= end_) {
7346 uint64_t v;
7347 std::memcpy(&v, pn, 8);
7348 uint64_t shifted = v - 0x3030303030303030ULL;
7349 uint64_t nondigit = (shifted | ((shifted & 0x7F7F7F7F7F7F7F7FULL) +
7350 0x7676767676767676ULL)) &
7351 0x8080808080808080ULL;
7352 if (nondigit) {
7353 pn += QBUEM_CTZ(nondigit) >> 3;
7354 goto s2_num_done;
7355 }
7356 pn += 8;
7357 }
7358 while (pn < end_ && static_cast<unsigned>(*pn - '0') < 10u)
7359 ++pn;
7360 s2_num_done:;
7361 bool flt = false;
7362 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(pn < end_ &&
7363 (*pn == '.' || *pn == 'e' || *pn == 'E'))) {
7364 flt = true;
7365 ++pn;
7366 if (pn < end_ && (*pn == '+' || *pn == '-'))
7367 ++pn;
7368 // SWAR-8 fractional digit scan
7369 while (pn + 8 <= end_) {
7370 uint64_t _v;
7371 std::memcpy(&_v, pn, 8);
7372 uint64_t _s = _v - 0x3030303030303030ULL;
7373 uint64_t _nd =
7374 (_s | ((_s & 0x7F7F7F7F7F7F7F7FULL) + 0x7676767676767676ULL)) &
7375 0x8080808080808080ULL;
7376 if (_nd) {
7377 pn += QBUEM_CTZ(_nd) >> 3;
7378 break;
7379 }
7380 pn += 8;
7381 }
7382 while (pn < end_ && static_cast<unsigned>(*pn - '0') < 10u)
7383 ++pn;
7384 if (pn < end_ && (*pn == 'e' || *pn == 'E')) {
7385 ++pn;
7386 if (pn < end_ && (*pn == '+' || *pn == '-'))
7387 ++pn;
7388 while (pn + 8 <= end_) {
7389 uint64_t _v;
7390 std::memcpy(&_v, pn, 8);
7391 uint64_t _s = _v - 0x3030303030303030ULL;
7392 uint64_t _nd = (_s | ((_s & 0x7F7F7F7F7F7F7F7FULL) +
7393 0x7676767676767676ULL)) &
7394 0x8080808080808080ULL;
7395 if (_nd) {
7396 pn += QBUEM_CTZ(_nd) >> 3;
7397 break;
7398 }
7399 pn += 8;
7400 }
7401 while (pn < end_ && static_cast<unsigned>(*pn - '0') < 10u)
7402 ++pn;
7403 }
7404 }
7405 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(static_cast<size_t>(pn - s) > 0xFFFFu))
7406 goto s2_fail; // number literal longer than 16-bit length field
7407 push(flt ? TapeNodeType::NumberRaw : TapeNodeType::Integer,
7408 static_cast<uint16_t>(pn - s), off);
7409 last_off = static_cast<uint32_t>(pn - data_);
7410 break;
7411 }
7412
7413 case kActTrue:
7414 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY((cur_state_ & 0b001u) ||
7415 off + 4 > static_cast<uint32_t>(end_ - data_) ||
7416 std::memcmp(data_ + off, "true", 4)))
7417 goto s2_fail; // (cur_state_&1): not a valid object key
7418 push(TapeNodeType::BooleanTrue, 4, off);
7419 last_off = off + 4;
7420 break;
7421
7422 case kActFalse:
7423 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY((cur_state_ & 0b001u) ||
7424 off + 5 > static_cast<uint32_t>(end_ - data_) ||
7425 std::memcmp(data_ + off, "false", 5)))
7426 goto s2_fail;
7427 push(TapeNodeType::BooleanFalse, 5, off);
7428 last_off = off + 5;
7429 break;
7430
7431 case kActNull:
7432 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY((cur_state_ & 0b001u) ||
7433 off + 4 > static_cast<uint32_t>(end_ - data_) ||
7434 std::memcmp(data_ + off, "null", 4)))
7435 goto s2_fail;
7436 push(TapeNodeType::Null, 4, off);
7437 last_off = off + 4;
7438 break;
7439
7440 default:
7441 goto s2_fail;
7442 } // switch
7443 if (depth_ == 0) break;
7444 } // for
7445
7446 if (!allow_trailing) {
7447 const char *tail = data_ + last_off;
7448 while (tail < end_) {
7449 if (static_cast<unsigned char>(*tail) > 0x20)
7450 goto s2_fail;
7451 ++tail;
7452 }
7453 }
7454
7455 doc_->tape.head = tape_head_;
7456 // Same empty-tape guard as parse(): require at least one value node.
7457 return depth_ == 0 && tape_head_ > doc_->tape.base;
7458
7459 s2_fail:
7460 doc_->tape.head = tape_head_;
7461 // Record an approximate failure position for diagnostics (offset just past
7462 // the last successfully consumed atom). Failure path only — no hot-loop
7463 // cost. get_p() is otherwise unused on the staged path.
7464 p_ = data_ + last_off;
7465 return false;
7466 }
7467#endif // QBUEM_HAS_AVX512
7468};
7469
7470// Public API
7471
7472// Tape node offsets are 32-bit, so the source must fit in a uint32_t index
7473// space. Inputs >= 4 GiB would wrap the offset and produce wrong/out-of-bounds
7474// slices; reject them up front.
7475inline constexpr size_t kMaxInputSize = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
7476
7477inline Value parse_partial(DocumentView &handle, std::string_view json, size_t* consumed = nullptr) {
7478 DocumentState *doc = handle.state();
7479 if (!doc) return {};
7480 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(json.size() > kMaxInputSize)) return {};
7481 doc->source = json;
7482 doc->mutations_.clear(); doc->deleted_.clear(); doc->additions_.clear(); doc->array_insertions_.clear();
7483 const size_t needed = json.size() + 64;
7484 if (!doc->tape.base || static_cast<size_t>(doc->tape.cap - doc->tape.base) < needed) doc->tape.reserve(needed); else doc->tape.reset();
7485 Parser p(doc);
7486 if (!p.parse(true)) return {};
7487 if (consumed) *consumed = p.get_p() - json.data();
7488 return Value(doc, 0);
7489}
7490// Zero-copy: the returned Value views into `json`. Reject rvalue std::string
7491// at compile time so a temporary buffer cannot become a use-after-free (mirrors
7492// the Document& overloads). Keep an lvalue alive, or use read<T>()/fuse<T>().
7493Value parse_partial(DocumentView &, const ::std::string &&,
7494 size_t * = nullptr) = delete;
7495
7496inline Value parse_reuse(DocumentView &handle, std::string_view json) {
7497 DocumentState *doc = handle.state();
7498 if (!doc)
7499 return {};
7500 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(json.size() > kMaxInputSize))
7501 throw std::runtime_error("qbuem: input exceeds 4 GiB (32-bit offset limit)");
7502 doc->source = json;
7503 // Clear mutation / deletion / addition overlays from any prior parse.
7504 // These maps reference tape indices that are invalidated when the tape is
7505 // reset; stale entries would corrupt dump_changes_() on the next call.
7506 doc->mutations_.clear();
7507 doc->deleted_.clear();
7508 doc->additions_.clear();
7509 doc->array_insertions_.clear();
7510 // Worst-case tape nodes == json.size() (e.g. "[[[...]]]" produces one
7511 // node per character). Use json.size() + 64 as a guaranteed upper bound.
7512 const size_t needed = json.size() + 64;
7513 if (QBUEM_UNLIKELY(!doc->tape.base ||
7514 static_cast<size_t>(doc->tape.cap - doc->tape.base) <
7515 needed)) {
7516 doc->tape.reserve(needed);
7517 } else {
7518 doc->tape.reset(); // hot path: head = base (1 instruction)
7519 }
7520#if QBUEM_HAS_AVX512
7521 // Stage 1+2 is beneficial when the positions array fits in
7522 // L2/L3 cache and the JSON is string-heavy (e.g. twitter.json,
7523 // citm.json). Large number-heavy files (canada.json, gsoc-2018.json) have
7524 // too many positions (~1M+) causing L3 pressure: Stage 1 overhead exceeds
7525 // savings. Threshold: 2 MB — includes twitter(617KB) and citm(1.65MB);
7526 // excludes canada(2.15MB) and gsoc(3.3MB).
7527 static constexpr size_t kStage12MaxSize = 2 * 1024 * 1024; // 2 MB
7528 if (QBUEM_LIKELY(json.size() <= kStage12MaxSize)) {
7529 stage1_scan_avx512(json.data(), json.size(), doc->idx);
7530 Parser parser(doc);
7531 if (!parser.parse_staged(doc->idx))
7532 throw_parse_error("Invalid JSON", parser.get_p(), json);
7533 } else {
7534 Parser parser(doc);
7535 if (!parser.parse())
7536 throw_parse_error("Invalid JSON", parser.get_p(), json);
7537 }
7538#else
7539 Parser parser(doc);
7540 if (!parser.parse())
7541 throw_parse_error("Invalid JSON", parser.get_p(), json);
7542#endif
7543 return Value(doc, 0);
7544}
7545// Zero-copy: the returned Value views into `json`. Reject rvalue std::string at
7546// compile time so a temporary buffer cannot become a use-after-free (mirrors the
7547// Document& overload). Keep an lvalue alive, or use read<T>()/fuse<T>().
7548Value parse_reuse(DocumentView &, const ::std::string &&) = delete;
7549
7550// ── Value::merge_patch() out-of-line (needs parse_reuse) ────────────────────
7551inline void Value::merge_patch(std::string_view patch_json) {
7552 if (!is_object())
7553 return;
7554 DocumentView patch_doc;
7555 Value patch = parse_reuse(patch_doc, patch_json);
7556 merge_patch_impl_(patch);
7557}
7558
7559// ── Value::patch() — RFC 6902 ────────────────────────────────────────────────
7560
7561inline bool Value::patch(std::string_view patch_json) {
7562 DocumentView patch_doc;
7563 Value patch_array = parse_reuse(patch_doc, patch_json);
7564 return patch(patch_array);
7565}
7566
7567inline bool Value::patch(const Value &patch_array) {
7568 if (!patch_array.is_array())
7569 return false;
7570
7571 // Transactional safety: backup current mutation state
7572 auto saved_deleted = doc_->deleted_;
7573 auto saved_additions = doc_->additions_;
7574 auto saved_array_insertions = doc_->array_insertions_;
7575
7576 auto rollback = [&]() {
7577 doc_->deleted_ = std::move(saved_deleted);
7578 doc_->additions_ = std::move(saved_additions);
7579 doc_->array_insertions_ = std::move(saved_array_insertions);
7580 doc_->last_dump_size_ = 0;
7581 return false;
7582 };
7583
7584 for (Value op_obj : patch_array.elements()) {
7585 if (!op_obj.is_object())
7586 return rollback();
7587 std::string op = op_obj["op"] | "";
7588 std::string path = op_obj["path"] | "";
7589 if (op.empty())
7590 return rollback();
7591 if (!path.empty() && path[0] != '/')
7592 return rollback();
7593
7594 if (op == "add") {
7595 Value val = op_obj["value"];
7596 if (!val)
7597 return rollback();
7598 if (path.empty()) {
7599 doc_->mutations_[idx_] = {val.type(), val.dump()};
7600 doc_->last_dump_size_ = 0;
7601 continue;
7602 }
7603 const size_t last_slash = path.find_last_of('/');
7604 std::string parent_path(path.substr(0, last_slash));
7605 std::string key(path.substr(last_slash + 1));
7606 Value parent = at(parent_path);
7607 if (!parent)
7608 return rollback();
7609 if (parent.is_object()) {
7610 parent.erase(key);
7611 parent.insert(key, val);
7612 } else if (parent.is_array()) {
7613 if (key == "-") {
7614 parent.push_back(val);
7615 } else {
7616 size_t p_idx = 0;
7617 auto [ptr, ec] =
7618 std::from_chars(key.data(), key.data() + key.size(), p_idx);
7619 if (ec != std::errc{})
7620 return rollback();
7621 parent.insert(p_idx, val);
7622 }
7623 } else
7624 return rollback();
7625 } else if (op == "remove") {
7626 if (path.empty())
7627 return rollback();
7628 const size_t last_slash = path.find_last_of('/');
7629 std::string parent_path(path.substr(0, last_slash));
7630 std::string key(path.substr(last_slash + 1));
7631 Value parent = at(parent_path);
7632 if (!parent || !parent.erase(key))
7633 return rollback();
7634 } else if (op == "replace") {
7635 Value val = op_obj["value"];
7636 if (!val || !at(path).is_valid())
7637 return rollback();
7638 if (path.empty()) {
7639 doc_->mutations_[idx_] = {val.type(), val.dump()};
7640 doc_->last_dump_size_ = 0;
7641 continue;
7642 }
7643 const size_t last_slash = path.find_last_of('/');
7644 std::string parent_path(path.substr(0, last_slash));
7645 std::string key(path.substr(last_slash + 1));
7646 Value parent = at(parent_path);
7647 if (parent.is_object()) {
7648 if (!parent.erase(key))
7649 return rollback();
7650 parent.insert(key, val);
7651 } else if (parent.is_array()) {
7652 size_t p_idx = 0;
7653 auto [ptr, ec] =
7654 std::from_chars(key.data(), key.data() + key.size(), p_idx);
7655 if (ec != std::errc{} || !parent.erase(p_idx))
7656 return rollback();
7657 parent.insert(p_idx, val);
7658 } else
7659 return rollback();
7660 } else if (op == "move") {
7661 std::string from = op_obj["from"] | "";
7662 Value val = at(from);
7663 if (from.empty() || !val)
7664 return rollback();
7665 std::string json = val.dump();
7666 // Remove from
7667 const size_t f_slash = from.find_last_of('/');
7668 Value f_parent = at(from.substr(0, f_slash));
7669 std::string f_key(from.substr(f_slash + 1));
7670 if (f_parent.is_object()) {
7671 if (!f_parent.erase(f_key))
7672 return rollback();
7673 } else if (f_parent.is_array()) {
7674 size_t idx = 0;
7675 std::from_chars(f_key.data(), f_key.data() + f_key.size(), idx);
7676 if (!f_parent.erase(idx))
7677 return rollback();
7678 } else
7679 return rollback();
7680 // Add to path (recursion-simulated)
7681 DocumentView temp_doc;
7682 Value v_new = parse_reuse(temp_doc, json);
7683 // Re-use 'add' logic manually or create helper
7684 const size_t t_slash = path.find_last_of('/');
7685 Value t_parent = at(path.substr(0, t_slash));
7686 std::string t_key(path.substr(t_slash + 1));
7687 if (t_parent.is_object())
7688 t_parent.insert(t_key, v_new);
7689 else if (t_parent.is_array()) {
7690 if (t_key == "-")
7691 t_parent.push_back(v_new);
7692 else {
7693 size_t idx = 0;
7694 std::from_chars(t_key.data(), t_key.data() + t_key.size(), idx);
7695 t_parent.insert(idx, v_new);
7696 }
7697 } else
7698 return rollback();
7699 } else if (op == "copy") {
7700 std::string from = op_obj["from"] | "";
7701 Value val = at(from);
7702 if (from.empty() || !val)
7703 return rollback();
7704 std::string json = val.dump();
7705 DocumentView temp_doc;
7706 Value v_new = parse_reuse(temp_doc, json);
7707 const size_t t_slash = path.find_last_of('/');
7708 Value t_parent = at(path.substr(0, t_slash));
7709 std::string t_key(path.substr(t_slash + 1));
7710 if (t_parent.is_object())
7711 t_parent.insert(t_key, v_new);
7712 else if (t_parent.is_array()) {
7713 if (t_key == "-")
7714 t_parent.push_back(v_new);
7715 else {
7716 size_t idx = 0;
7717 std::from_chars(t_key.data(), t_key.data() + t_key.size(), idx);
7718 t_parent.insert(idx, v_new);
7719 }
7720 }
7721 } else if (op == "test") {
7722 Value expected = op_obj["value"];
7723 Value actual = at(path);
7724 if (expected.dump() != actual.dump())
7725 return rollback();
7726 } else {
7727 return rollback(); // Unknown operation
7728 }
7729 }
7730 return true;
7731}
7732
7733// SafeValue — optional-propagating chain proxy
7734//
7735// Returned by Value::get(key/idx). Every subsequent operator[] propagates
7736// std::nullopt silently: if any step is absent, the entire chain returns
7737// an empty SafeValue without throwing.
7738//
7739// Read path comparison:
7740// root["user"]["id"].as<int>() ← throws on missing key (fast path)
7741// root.get("user")["id"].as<int>() ← std::optional<int>, never throws
7742// root.get("user")["id"].value_or(-1) ← int with default, never throws
7743//
7744// SafeValue is std::optional<Value>-compatible: has_value(), operator bool,
7745// operator* and operator-> all work, so existing code using optional<Value>
7746// patterns compiles unchanged.
7747
7752class SafeValue {
7753 Value val_; // valid only when has_ == true; default-constructed otherwise
7754 bool has_ = false;
7755
7756public:
7757 SafeValue() noexcept = default;
7758 explicit SafeValue(Value v) noexcept : val_(v), has_(true) {}
7759
7760 // ── std::optional-compatible interface ───────────────────────────────────
7761
7762 bool has_value() const noexcept { return has_; }
7763 explicit operator bool() const noexcept { return has_; }
7764
7765 Value &value() {
7766 if (!has_)
7767 throw std::bad_optional_access{};
7768 return val_;
7769 }
7770 const Value &value() const {
7771 if (!has_)
7772 throw std::bad_optional_access{};
7773 return val_;
7774 }
7775 Value &operator*() { return value(); }
7776 const Value &operator*() const { return value(); }
7777 Value *operator->() { return &value(); }
7778 const Value *operator->() const { return &value(); }
7779
7780 // ── Type checks — false when absent ──────────────────────────────────────
7781
7782 bool is_null() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_null(); }
7783 bool is_bool() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_bool(); }
7784 bool is_int() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_int(); }
7785 bool is_double() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_double(); }
7786 bool is_number() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_number(); }
7787 bool is_string() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_string(); }
7788 bool is_object() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_object(); }
7789 bool is_array() const noexcept { return has_ && val_.is_array(); }
7790
7791 // ── Container size — 0 when absent, never throws ─────────────────────────
7792 //
7793 // Avoids the operator->-then-size() antipattern that throws when absent:
7794 // sv->size() ← throws bad_optional_access if absent
7795 // sv.size() ← returns 0 safely when absent
7796 size_t size() const noexcept { return has_ ? val_.size() : 0; }
7797 bool empty() const noexcept { return size() == 0; }
7798
7799 // ── Chaining — absent propagates forward, never throws ───────────────────
7800
7801 SafeValue operator[](std::string_view key) const noexcept {
7802 if (!has_)
7803 return {};
7804 return val_.get(key); // calls Value::get() defined below
7805 }
7806 SafeValue operator[](const char *key) const noexcept {
7807 return (*this)[std::string_view(key)];
7808 }
7809 SafeValue operator[](size_t idx) const noexcept {
7810 if (!has_)
7811 return {};
7812 return val_.get(idx);
7813 }
7814 SafeValue operator[](int idx) const noexcept {
7815 if (idx < 0 || !has_)
7816 return {};
7817 return val_.get(static_cast<size_t>(idx));
7818 }
7819 // unsigned int overload — resolves ambiguity between int and size_t
7820 SafeValue operator[](unsigned int idx) const noexcept {
7821 return (*this)[static_cast<size_t>(idx)];
7822 }
7823
7824 // Alias for further chaining (same as operator[]):
7825 SafeValue get(std::string_view key) const noexcept { return (*this)[key]; }
7826 SafeValue get(const char *key) const noexcept { return (*this)[key]; }
7827 SafeValue get(size_t idx) const noexcept { return (*this)[idx]; }
7828 SafeValue get(int idx) const noexcept { return (*this)[idx]; }
7829 // unsigned int overload — resolves ambiguity between int and size_t
7830 SafeValue get(unsigned int idx) const noexcept { return (*this)[static_cast<size_t>(idx)]; }
7831
7832 // ── Terminal: typed extraction ────────────────────────────────────────────
7833
7834 // as<T>() — returns std::optional<T>; std::nullopt when absent or wrong type
7835 template <JsonReadable T> std::optional<T> as() const noexcept {
7836 if (!has_)
7837 return std::nullopt;
7838 return val_.try_as<T>();
7839 }
7840
7841 // value_or(default) — direct T with fallback; never throws
7842 template <JsonReadable T> T value_or(T def) const noexcept {
7843 auto r = as<T>();
7844 return r ? *r : def;
7845 }
7846
7847 // dump() — "null" when absent
7848 std::string dump() const { return has_ ? val_.dump() : "null"; }
7849
7850 // ── Pipe fallback on SafeValue: safe_val | default ────────────────────────
7851 //
7852 // Usage:
7853 // int age = root.get("user")["age"] | 0;
7854 // std::string s = root.get("name") | "anon";
7855
7856 template <JsonReadable T>
7857 friend T operator|(const SafeValue &sv, T def) noexcept {
7858 if (!sv.has_)
7859 return def;
7860 auto r = sv.val_.try_as<T>();
7861 return r ? *r : def;
7862 }
7863 friend std::string operator|(const SafeValue &sv, const char *def) noexcept {
7864 if (!sv.has_)
7865 return std::string(def);
7866 auto r = sv.val_.try_as<std::string>();
7867 return r ? *r : std::string(def);
7868 }
7869
7870 // ── Monadic operations ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7871 //
7872 // Inspired by the Monad pattern and C++23 std::optional monadic ops.
7873 // All three propagate the absent state (has_=false) without branching at
7874 // the call site, keeping transformation pipelines free of if-checks.
7875 //
7876 // Example pipeline:
7877 //
7878 // auto price = root["store"]["items"][0]
7879 // .and_then([](const Value& v) -> SafeValue {
7880 // return v.is_number() ? SafeValue{v} : SafeValue{};
7881 // })
7882 // .transform([](const Value& v) { return v.as<double>() * 1.1; })
7883 // .value_or(0.0);
7884
7885 // and_then — flatMap: F(Value) -> SafeValue.
7886 // If absent, returns SafeValue{}. F is only called when has_value().
7887 // Use when the transformation can itself fail (returns SafeValue).
7888 template <std::invocable<const Value &> F>
7889 requires std::same_as<std::invoke_result_t<F, const Value &>, SafeValue>
7890 SafeValue and_then(F &&f) const
7891 noexcept(std::is_nothrow_invocable_v<F, const Value &>) {
7892 if (!has_)
7893 return {};
7894 return std::invoke(std::forward<F>(f), val_);
7895 }
7896
7897 // transform — map: F(Value) -> U, result wrapped in std::optional<U>.
7898 // If absent, returns std::nullopt. Never throws unless F throws.
7899 // Use when the transformation always succeeds given a valid Value.
7900 template <std::invocable<const Value &> F>
7901 auto transform(F &&f) const
7902 noexcept(std::is_nothrow_invocable_v<F, const Value &>)
7903 -> std::optional<std::invoke_result_t<F, const Value &>> {
7904 if (!has_)
7905 return std::nullopt;
7906 return std::invoke(std::forward<F>(f), val_);
7907 }
7908
7909 // or_else — fallback: F() -> SafeValue, called only when absent.
7910 // Use to supply a default SafeValue when the chain is broken.
7911 template <std::invocable F>
7912 requires std::same_as<std::invoke_result_t<F>, SafeValue>
7913 SafeValue or_else(F &&f) const noexcept(std::is_nothrow_invocable_v<F>) {
7914 if (has_)
7915 return *this;
7916 return std::invoke(std::forward<F>(f));
7917 }
7918};
7919
7920// ── DocumentState::get_synthetic out-of-line (Value now complete) ──────────
7921
7922inline DocumentState *
7923DocumentState::get_synthetic(const ::std::string &json_str) const {
7924 auto it = synthetic_docs_.find(json_str);
7925 if (it != synthetic_docs_.end())
7926 return it->second.get();
7927
7928 // Reserve the cache slot first so the map owns a STABLE copy of the key, and
7929 // point the synthetic document's `source` view at that stable key — NOT at
7930 // the `json_str` argument. The argument is typically a reference to a string
7931 // stored in additions_/array_insertions_, which erase_from_additions_/merge()
7932 // can free; since synthetic_docs_ is never invalidated, a source view into
7933 // the freed argument would dangle (use-after-free). unordered_map key
7934 // references are stable across other insert/erase operations.
7935 auto [slot, inserted] = synthetic_docs_.try_emplace(json_str);
7936 const std::string &stable_key = slot->first;
7937
7938 DocumentView synth_handle(std::string_view{stable_key});
7939 // parse_reuse throws on unparseable input. get_synthetic is reached from
7940 // noexcept accessors (operator[], dump helpers), so an escape here would
7941 // call std::terminate. An inserted value can be unparseable when its
7942 // serialized form exceeds the 64KB token limit (e.g. a short string whose
7943 // escaped \uXXXX expansion crosses 65535 bytes) — erase the reserved slot
7944 // and return nullptr so callers produce an invalid Value instead of crashing.
7945 try {
7946 parse_reuse(synth_handle, std::string_view{stable_key});
7947 } catch (...) {
7948 synthetic_docs_.erase(slot);
7949 return nullptr;
7950 }
7951
7952 DocumentState *s = synth_handle.state();
7953 // Transfer ownership to shared_ptr. The handle has 1 ref.
7954 // We want the shared_ptr to own it too.
7955 auto shared = std::shared_ptr<DocumentState>(
7956 s, [](DocumentState *ptr) { ptr->deref(); });
7957 // Increment ref for the shared_ptr so it doesn't delete when handle goes away
7958 s->ref();
7959
7960 slot->second = std::move(shared);
7961 return s;
7962}
7963
7964// ── Value::get() out-of-line definitions (SafeValue now complete) ──────────
7965
7966inline SafeValue Value::get(::std::string_view key) const noexcept {
7967 Value v = this->operator[](key);
7968 if (v.idx_ == 0)
7969 return {};
7970 return SafeValue{v};
7971}
7972
7973inline SafeValue Value::get(const char *key) const noexcept {
7974 return get(::std::string_view(key));
7975}
7976
7977inline SafeValue Value::get(size_t idx) const noexcept {
7978 Value v = this->operator[](idx);
7979 if (v.idx_ == 0)
7980 return {};
7981 return SafeValue{v};
7982}
7983
7984inline SafeValue Value::get(int idx) const noexcept {
7985 if (idx < 0)
7986 return {};
7987 return get(static_cast<size_t>(idx));
7988}

7990// ============================================================================
7991// qbuem::rfc8259 — RFC 8259 strict validator
7992// ============================================================================
7993//
7994// Validates a JSON string against RFC 8259 (the JSON specification).
7995// Throws std::runtime_error with a descriptive message on any violation.
7996//
7997// Differences from the default lenient parser:
7998// • Rejects trailing commas: [1,2,] {\"a\":1,}
7999// • Rejects leading zeros: 01 007 -01
8000// • Rejects trailing decimal: 1.
8001// • Rejects empty exponent: 1e 1e+ 1E-
8002// • Rejects unescaped control chars in strings (U+0000..U+001F)
8003// • Rejects invalid escape sequences: \x \a \z etc.
8004// • Rejects trailing non-whitespace content after the value
8005// • Accepts any JSON value at top level (RFC 8259 §2)
8006//
8007// Usage:
8008// qbuem::Document doc;
8009// qbuem::Value root = qbuem::parse_strict(doc, json); // throws on violation
8010//
8011// // Or just validate without parsing:
8012// qbuem::rfc8259::validate(json); // throws std::runtime_error on violation
8013// ============================================================================
8014
8015namespace rfc8259 {
8016
8017namespace detail_ {
8018
8019[[noreturn]] inline void fail(const char *msg, const char *pos,
8020 const char *begin) {
8021 const size_t off = static_cast<size_t>(pos - begin);
8022 // The prefix [begin, begin+off) is exactly the input up to the failure, so its
8023 // end position is the failure's line/column.
8024 const ::qbuem::json::source_position loc =
8025 ::qbuem::json::compute_source_position(::std::string_view(begin, off), off);
8026 char buf[160];
8027 std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
8028 "RFC 8259 violation at line %zu column %zu (byte offset %zu): %s",
8029 loc.line, loc.column, off, msg);
8030 // parse_error (derived from std::runtime_error) so strict-mode failures carry
8031 // the same typed offset()/line()/column() as the relaxed parser; existing
8032 // catch blocks for std::runtime_error / std::exception are unaffected.
8033 throw ::qbuem::json::parse_error(buf, off, loc.line, loc.column);
8034}
8035
8036struct Validator {
8037 const char *p;
8038 const char *end;
8039 const char *begin;
8040 // Recursive-descent nesting depth. Without a cap, adversarial deeply-nested
8041 // input (e.g. "[[[[…") exhausts the native call stack → SIGSEGV. Mirrors the
8042 // tape Parser's kMaxDepth bound so all engines reject the same inputs.
8043 uint32_t depth = 0;
8044 static constexpr uint32_t kMaxDepth = 1024;
8045
8046 void ws() noexcept {
8047 while (p < end && (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t' || *p == '\n' || *p == '\r'))
8048 ++p;
8049 }
8050
8051 void expect_literal(const char *lit, size_t len) {
8052 if (static_cast<size_t>(end - p) < len || std::memcmp(p, lit, len) != 0)
8053 fail("invalid literal", p, begin);
8054 p += len;
8055 }
8056
8057 void parse_string() {
8058 ++p; // skip '"'
8059 while (p < end) {
8060 unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(*p++);
8061 if (c == '"')
8062 return; // end of string
8063 if (c == '\\') {
8064 if (p >= end)
8065 fail("unterminated escape sequence", p - 1, begin);
8066 unsigned char esc = static_cast<unsigned char>(*p++);
8067 if (esc == 'u') {
8068 if (p + 4 > end)
8069 fail("incomplete \\uXXXX escape", p - 2, begin);
8070 for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
8071 unsigned char h = static_cast<unsigned char>(*p++);
8072 bool hex = (h >= '0' && h <= '9') || (h >= 'a' && h <= 'f') ||
8073 (h >= 'A' && h <= 'F');
8074 if (!hex)
8075 fail("invalid hex digit in \\uXXXX", p - 1, begin);
8076 }
8077 } else if (esc != '"' && esc != '\\' && esc != '/' && esc != 'b' &&
8078 esc != 'f' && esc != 'n' && esc != 'r' && esc != 't') {
8079 fail("invalid escape character", p - 1, begin);
8080 }
8081 } else if (c < 0x20) {
8082 fail("unescaped control character in string", p - 1, begin);
8083 } else if (c >= 0x80) {
8084 // RFC 8259 §8.1: JSON text MUST be valid UTF-8. Validate the multibyte
8085 // sequence against the Unicode "well-formed UTF-8" table (Table 3-7),
8086 // which rejects overlong encodings, UTF-8-encoded surrogates (U+D800..
8087 // U+DFFF), code points > U+10FFFF, lone continuation bytes, and
8088 // truncated sequences. c is the lead byte; p points at the first
8089 // continuation. (Only strict mode validates this — the relaxed parser
8090 // stays byte-transparent for zero-copy.)
8091 int extra; // number of continuation bytes after the lead
8092 unsigned char lo, hi; // allowed range for the FIRST continuation byte
8093 if (c >= 0xC2 && c <= 0xDF) { extra = 1; lo = 0x80; hi = 0xBF; }
8094 else if (c == 0xE0) { extra = 2; lo = 0xA0; hi = 0xBF; }
8095 else if (c >= 0xE1 && c <= 0xEC) { extra = 2; lo = 0x80; hi = 0xBF; }
8096 else if (c == 0xED) { extra = 2; lo = 0x80; hi = 0x9F; }
8097 else if (c >= 0xEE && c <= 0xEF) { extra = 2; lo = 0x80; hi = 0xBF; }
8098 else if (c == 0xF0) { extra = 3; lo = 0x90; hi = 0xBF; }
8099 else if (c >= 0xF1 && c <= 0xF3) { extra = 3; lo = 0x80; hi = 0xBF; }
8100 else if (c == 0xF4) { extra = 3; lo = 0x80; hi = 0x8F; }
8101 else fail("invalid UTF-8 lead byte in string", p - 1, begin); // 80-C1,F5-FF
8102 // First continuation is range-restricted (this is what rejects overlong
8103 // encodings, surrogates, and > U+10FFFF).
8104 if (p >= end || static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) < lo ||
8105 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) > hi)
8106 fail("invalid UTF-8 continuation byte in string", p, begin);
8107 ++p;
8108 // Remaining continuation bytes must each be 0x80..0xBF.
8109 for (int i = 1; i < extra; ++i) {
8110 if (p >= end || static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) < 0x80 ||
8111 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) > 0xBF)
8112 fail("invalid UTF-8 continuation byte in string", p, begin);
8113 ++p;
8114 }
8115 }
8116 }
8117 fail("unterminated string", p, begin);
8118 }
8119
8120 void parse_number() {
8121 // Optional minus
8122 if (*p == '-')
8123 ++p;
8124 if (p >= end)
8125 fail("unexpected end in number", p, begin);
8126
8127 // Integer part
8128 if (*p == '0') {
8129 ++p;
8130 // Leading zero: reject if followed by another digit
8131 if (p < end && static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) >= '0' &&
8132 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) <= '9')
8133 fail("leading zero in number", p - 1, begin);
8134 } else if (static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) >= '1' &&
8135 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) <= '9') {
8136 while (p < end && static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) >= '0' &&
8137 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) <= '9')
8138 ++p;
8139 } else {
8140 fail("invalid number", p, begin);
8141 }
8142
8143 // Optional fractional part
8144 if (p < end && *p == '.') {
8145 ++p;
8146 if (p >= end || static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) < '0' ||
8147 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) > '9')
8148 fail("trailing decimal point or missing digits after '.'", p - 1,
8149 begin);
8150 while (p < end && static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) >= '0' &&
8151 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) <= '9')
8152 ++p;
8153 }
8154
8155 // Optional exponent
8156 if (p < end && (*p == 'e' || *p == 'E')) {
8157 ++p;
8158 if (p < end && (*p == '+' || *p == '-'))
8159 ++p;
8160 if (p >= end || static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) < '0' ||
8161 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) > '9')
8162 fail("missing digits in exponent", p - 1, begin);
8163 while (p < end && static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) >= '0' &&
8164 static_cast<unsigned char>(*p) <= '9')
8165 ++p;
8166 }
8167 }
8168
8169 void parse_array() {
8170 ++p; // skip '['
8171 ws();
8172 if (p < end && *p == ']') {
8173 ++p;
8174 return;
8175 } // empty array
8176 parse_value();
8177 ws();
8178 while (p < end && *p == ',') {
8179 ++p; // skip ','
8180 ws();
8181 if (p < end && *p == ']')
8182 fail("trailing comma in array", p - 1, begin);
8183 parse_value();
8184 ws();
8185 }
8186 if (p >= end || *p != ']')
8187 fail("expected ']'", p, begin);
8188 ++p;
8189 }
8190
8191 void parse_object() {
8192 ++p; // skip '{'
8193 ws();
8194 if (p < end && *p == '}') {
8195 ++p;
8196 return;
8197 } // empty object
8198 if (p >= end || *p != '"')
8199 fail("expected string key", p, begin);
8200 parse_string();
8201 ws();
8202 if (p >= end || *p != ':')
8203 fail("expected ':' after key", p, begin);
8204 ++p;
8205 parse_value();
8206 ws();
8207 while (p < end && *p == ',') {
8208 ++p; // skip ','
8209 ws();
8210 if (p < end && *p == '}')
8211 fail("trailing comma in object", p - 1, begin);
8212 if (p >= end || *p != '"')
8213 fail("expected string key", p, begin);
8214 parse_string();
8215 ws();
8216 if (p >= end || *p != ':')
8217 fail("expected ':' after key", p, begin);
8218 ++p;
8219 parse_value();
8220 ws();
8221 }
8222 if (p >= end || *p != '}')
8223 fail("expected '}'", p, begin);
8224 // RFC 8259 §4 says object names SHOULD (not MUST) be unique, so duplicates
8225 // are valid JSON and are accepted here — rejecting them would make this
8226 // validator non-conformant (JSONTestSuite y_object_duplicated_key). The
8227 // resolution is predictable and documented per engine: relaxed DOM is
8228 // first-wins, Nexus fuse<T> is last-wins. See the note on Value::operator[].
8229 ++p;
8230 }
8231
8232 void parse_value() {
8233 ws();
8234 if (p >= end)
8235 fail("unexpected end of input", p, begin);
8236 char c = *p;
8237 if (c == '"')
8238 parse_string();
8239 else if (c == '{') {
8240 if (++depth > kMaxDepth)
8241 fail("nesting too deep", p, begin);
8242 parse_object();
8243 --depth;
8244 } else if (c == '[') {
8245 if (++depth > kMaxDepth)
8246 fail("nesting too deep", p, begin);
8247 parse_array();
8248 --depth;
8249 } else if (c == 't')
8250 expect_literal("true", 4);
8251 else if (c == 'f')
8252 expect_literal("false", 5);
8253 else if (c == 'n')
8254 expect_literal("null", 4);
8255 else if (c == '-' || (c >= '0' && c <= '9'))
8256 parse_number();
8257 else
8258 fail("unexpected character", p, begin);
8259 }
8260
8261 void run(std::string_view json) {
8262 p = json.data();
8263 end = json.data() + json.size();
8264 begin = p;
8265 parse_value();
8266 ws();
8267 if (p != end)
8268 fail("trailing content after JSON value", p, begin);
8269 }
8270};
8271
8272} // namespace detail_
8273
8276inline void validate(std::string_view json) { detail_::Validator{}.run(json); }
8277
8282inline Value parse_strict(DocumentView &doc, ::std::string_view json) {
8283 rfc8259::validate(json);
8284 return qbuem::json::parse_reuse(doc, json);
8285}
8286// Zero-copy: the returned Value views into `json`. Reject rvalue std::string at
8287// compile time so a temporary buffer cannot become a use-after-free (mirrors the
8288// Document& overload). Keep an lvalue alive, or use read<T>()/fuse<T>().
8289Value parse_strict(DocumentView &, const ::std::string &&) = delete;
8290
8291} // namespace rfc8259
8292
8293// ============================================================================
8294// qbuem::detail — Automatic Serialization / Deserialization Engine
8295// ============================================================================
8296//
8297// Concept-based dispatch: zero user effort for all standard C++ types.
8298//
8299// ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
8300// │ Tier 1 — Built-in (automatic, no code needed) │
8301// │ bool, int, double, float, … → JSON number/bool │
8302// │ std::string, string_view → JSON string (escaped) │
8303// │ std::optional<T> → null or T │
8304// │ std::vector / list / deque <T> → JSON array │
8305// │ std::set / unordered_set <T> → JSON array │
8306// │ std::map / unordered_map <str,V> → JSON object │
8307// │ std::array<T,N> → JSON array (fixed size) │
8308// │ std::pair<A,B>, tuple<Ts…> → JSON array │
8309// │ nullptr_t → null │
8310// ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
8311// │ Tier 2 — One macro line for custom structs │

8325// ── SWAR helpers (used by string serialization and Nexus key scanning) ────────
8326// Returns non-zero if any byte in `v` equals `byte`.
8327QBUEM_INLINE uint64_t swar_has_byte(uint64_t v, uint8_t byte) noexcept {
8328 uint64_t x = v ^ (static_cast<uint64_t>(byte) * 0x0101010101010101ULL);
8329 return (x - 0x0101010101010101ULL) & ~x & 0x8080808080808080ULL;
8330}
8331// Returns non-zero if any byte in `v` is less than `threshold` (0x01..0x7F range safe).
8332QBUEM_INLINE uint64_t swar_has_less(uint64_t v, uint8_t threshold) noexcept {
8333 return (v - static_cast<uint64_t>(threshold) * 0x0101010101010101ULL) & ~v &
8334 0x8080808080808080ULL;
8335}

8337// ── Type trait helpers
8338
8339template <typename T, template <typename...> class U>
8340struct is_specialization_of : std::false_type {};
8341
8342template <template <typename...> class U, typename... Args>
8343struct is_specialization_of<U<Args...>, U> : std::true_type {};

8345// ── Concepts
8346
8347template <typename T>
8348concept JsonDetailBool =
8349 std::is_same_v<T, bool> ||
8350 std::is_same_v<std::remove_cvref_t<T>, std::vector<bool>::reference> ||
8351 std::is_same_v<std::remove_cvref_t<T>, std::vector<bool>::const_reference>;
8352// ── Nexus Core: Pulse Mapping Hashing (FNV-1a)
8353constexpr uint64_t fnv1a_hash(std::string_view s) {
8354 uint64_t hash = 0xcbf29ce484222325ULL;
8355 for (char c : s) {
8356 hash ^= static_cast<uint64_t>(c);
8357 hash *= 0x100000001b3ULL;
8358 }
8359 return hash;
8360}
8361
8362// ── Fast key hash for nexus_pulse field dispatch ─────────────────────────────
8363// ≤8 bytes : raw little-endian bytes loaded as uint64 (single load, no multiply)
8364// 9-16 bytes: XOR first-8 and last-8 bytes, mixed with length
8365// >16 bytes : FNV-1a fallback
8366// Compile-time and runtime versions produce identical values on LE platforms.
8367consteval uint64_t fast_key_hash_ce(const char *s) noexcept {
8368 size_t n = 0; while (s[n]) ++n;
8369 if (n == 0) return 0;
8370 if (n <= 8) {
8371 uint64_t v = 0;
8372 for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
8373 v |= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i])) << (i * 8);
8374 return v;
8375 }
8376 if (n <= 16) {
8377 uint64_t a = 0, b = 0;
8378 for (size_t i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
8379 a |= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i])) << (i * 8);
8380 for (size_t i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
8381 b |= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[n-8+i])) << (i * 8);
8382 return a ^ b ^ (static_cast<uint64_t>(n) << 56);
8383 }
8384 uint64_t h = 0xcbf29ce484222325ULL;
8385 for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
8386 h ^= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i]));
8387 h *= 0x100000001b3ULL;
8388 }
8389 return h;
8390}
8391
8392// string_view consteval variant — for hashing reflected field names, which are
8393// non-null-terminated views into __PRETTY_FUNCTION__. Produces the SAME value as
8394// fast_key_hash_ce(const char*) / fast_key_hash(string_view) for the same bytes.
8395// A separate name (not an overload) so a string-literal argument to the macro's
8396// fast_key_hash_ce(...) stays unambiguous.
8397consteval uint64_t fast_key_hash_ce_sv(std::string_view s) noexcept {
8398 const size_t n = s.size();
8399 if (n == 0) return 0;
8400 if (n <= 8) {
8401 uint64_t v = 0;
8402 for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
8403 v |= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i])) << (i * 8);
8404 return v;
8405 }
8406 if (n <= 16) {
8407 uint64_t a = 0, b = 0;
8408 for (size_t i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
8409 a |= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i])) << (i * 8);
8410 for (size_t i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
8411 b |= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[n - 8 + i])) << (i * 8);
8412 return a ^ b ^ (static_cast<uint64_t>(n) << 56);
8413 }
8414 uint64_t h = 0xcbf29ce484222325ULL;
8415 for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
8416 h ^= static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i]));
8417 h *= 0x100000001b3ULL;
8418 }
8419 return h;
8420}
8421
8422QBUEM_INLINE uint64_t fast_key_hash(std::string_view s) noexcept {
8423 const size_t n = s.size();
8424 if (n == 0) return 0;
8425 if (n <= 8) {
8426 uint64_t v = 0;
8427 std::memcpy(&v, s.data(), n); // LE: byte[0] → LSB (consistent with CE)
8428 return v;
8429 }
8430 if (n <= 16) {
8431 uint64_t a = 0, b = 0;
8432 std::memcpy(&a, s.data(), 8);
8433 std::memcpy(&b, s.data()+n-8, 8);
8434 return a ^ b ^ (static_cast<uint64_t>(n) << 56);
8435 }
8436 return fnv1a_hash(s);
8437}

8439template <typename T>
8440concept JsonDetailArith = std::is_arithmetic_v<T> && !std::is_same_v<T, bool>;
8441
8442template <typename T>
8443concept JsonDetailStrLike =
8444 std::is_same_v<T, std::string> || std::is_same_v<T, std::string_view> ||
8445 std::is_same_v<T, const char *>;
8446
8447template <typename T>
8448concept JsonDetailOptional = is_specialization_of<T, std::optional>::value;
8449
8450// Sequence: has push_back — vector, list, deque (not string)
8451template <typename T>
8452concept JsonDetailSeq = requires(T &t) {
8453 t.push_back(std::declval<typename T::value_type>());
8454} && !JsonDetailStrLike<T>;
8455
8456// Set: has insert, no push_back, no mapped_type — set, unordered_set, multiset
8457template <typename T>
8458concept JsonDetailSet =
8459 requires(T &t) { t.insert(std::declval<typename T::value_type>()); } &&
8460 !JsonDetailStrLike<T> &&
8461 !requires(T &t) { t.push_back(std::declval<typename T::value_type>()); } &&
8462 !requires { typename T::mapped_type; };
8463
8464// Map: has mapped_type with string-compatible key — map, unordered_map
8465template <typename T>
8466concept JsonDetailMap =
8467 requires {
8468 typename T::mapped_type;
8469 typename T::key_type;
8470 } && (std::is_same_v<typename T::key_type, std::string> ||
8471 std::is_convertible_v<std::string, typename T::key_type>);
8472
8473// Fixed array: std::array<T,N> — tuple_size + value_type, no push_back
8474template <typename T>
8475concept JsonDetailFixedArr = requires {
8476 std::tuple_size<T>::value;
8477 typename T::value_type;
8478} && !JsonDetailSeq<T> && !JsonDetailSet<T> && !JsonDetailMap<T>;
8479
8480// Tuple/pair: std::tuple<Ts…> or std::pair<A,B>
8481template <typename T>
8482concept JsonDetailTuple = is_specialization_of<T, std::tuple>::value ||
8483 is_specialization_of<T, std::pair>::value;
8484
8485// ADL hooks (user-defined or via QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS)
8486template <typename T>
8487concept HasFromQbuemJson =
8488 requires(const Value &v, T &t) { from_qbuem_json(v, t); };
8489template <typename T>
8490concept HasToQbuemJson =
8491 requires(Value &v, const T &t) { to_qbuem_json(v, t); };
8492template <typename T>
8493concept HasAppendQbuemJson =
8494 requires(std::string &out, const T &t) { append_qbuem_json(out, t); };
8495template <typename T>
8496concept HasNexusPulse =
8497 requires(std::string_view key, const char *&p, const char *end, T &t) {
8498 nexus_pulse(key, p, end, t);
8499};
8500// Fast variant: dispatch on a pre-computed uint64 key hash (skips runtime hash).
8501// NOTE: the signature here MUST track nexus_pulse_h's real arity — it gained a
8502// string_view `key` parameter (used to byte-verify the hash match against the
8503// field name, defeating hash-collision field spoofing). If this requires-clause
8504// lags behind, the concept silently evaluates false and NexusScanner::fill()
8505// falls back to the slow read_key()+separate-hash path (a ~15% fuse<T> regression
8506// that is functionally correct, so no test catches it).
8507template <typename T>
8508concept HasNexusPulseH = requires(uint64_t h, ::std::string_view key,
8509 const char *&p, const char *end, T &t) {
8510 nexus_pulse_h(h, key, p, end, t);
8511};
8512
8513// ── Enum support ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
8514// Any `enum`/`enum class` serializes out of the box as its underlying integer.
8515// Opt into a string representation with QBUEM_JSON_ENUM(E, A, B, ...): it
8516// generates ADL hooks `qbuem_enum_to_string(E)` / `qbuem_enum_from_string(sv, E&)`
8517// in the enum's namespace, and then the value round-trips as its name across
8518// every engine (DOM, fuse, CBOR). Detection is by ADL (same mechanism as
8519// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS), so the macro is invoked at the enum's namespace scope.
8520template <typename E>
8521concept JsonDetailStringEnum =
8522 std::is_enum_v<E> &&
8523 requires(E e, ::std::string_view s, E &er) {
8524 { qbuem_enum_to_string(e) } -> ::std::convertible_to<::std::string_view>;
8525 qbuem_enum_from_string(s, er);
8526 };
8527
8528// ── Macro-free aggregate reflection (GCC/Clang only) ─────────────────────────
8529// Serialize/deserialize a plain *aggregate* struct with NO QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS
8530// registration: qbuem::write(dto) / read<Dto> just work when Dto is an aggregate
8531// (no private members, no user-declared constructors, no base classes). A
8532// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS / from_qbuem_json registration, if present, always wins — so
8533// this is purely additive. Field *names* are recovered from __PRETTY_FUNCTION__
8534// (works on GCC and Clang; the library is GCC/Clang-only by design, so this needs
8535// no MSVC fallback). Up to kReflectMaxFields fields; beyond that, use the macro.
8536namespace refl {
8537
8538// A defined (inline) instance whose subobject addresses are compile-time
8539// constants; used only to recover field names (never read at runtime). Defining
8540// it — rather than `extern` — makes it work for types with ANY linkage (including
8541// anonymous-namespace and function-local aggregates, which an extern of a
8542// no-linkage type cannot) and for non-constexpr-constructible members (std::map,
8543// etc.). Requires the type be default-constructible (so does read<T>).
8544template <class T> inline const T probe_obj{};
8545
8546// Converts to anything; used only to count fields by aggregate-init probing. The
8547// conversion is named only in unevaluated requires-expressions, so it is never
8548// odr-used and needs no definition; the pragma silences the -Wundefined-inline
8549// note that referencing an undefined inline member would otherwise raise in
8550// consuming translation units.
8551#if defined(__clang__)
8552#pragma clang diagnostic push
8553#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wundefined-inline"
8554#endif
8555struct any_field {
8556 template <class U> constexpr operator U() const noexcept;
8557};
8558#if defined(__clang__)
8559#pragma clang diagnostic pop
8560#endif
8561
8562// Double-braced initializers ({any}{any}...) defeat brace elision, so a nested
8563// aggregate counts as ONE field rather than being flattened into its members.
8564template <class T, class... A>
8565concept brace_initable = requires { T{{A{}}...}; };
8566
8567template <class T, class... A>
8568constexpr ::std::size_t count_fields_() {
8569 if constexpr (brace_initable<T, A..., any_field>)
8570 return count_fields_<T, A..., any_field>();
8571 else
8572 return sizeof...(A);
8573}
8574template <class T>
8575constexpr ::std::size_t field_count() {
8576 return count_fields_<::std::remove_cvref_t<T>>();
8577}
8578
8579inline constexpr ::std::size_t kReflectMaxFields = 32;
8580
8581// One structured-binding ladder: returns a tuple of pointers to each field of the
8582// referenced object. Used both for values (real object) and, via probe_obj, for
8583// names (the pointers are constant expressions usable as template arguments).
8584template <class T>
8585constexpr auto field_ptrs(T &o) {
8586 constexpr ::std::size_t n = field_count<T>();
8587 if constexpr (n == 0) return ::std::make_tuple();
8588 else if constexpr (n == 1) { auto &[ f0] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0); }
8589 else if constexpr (n == 2) { auto &[ f0, f1] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1); }
8590 else if constexpr (n == 3) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2); }
8591 else if constexpr (n == 4) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3); }
8592 else if constexpr (n == 5) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3, f4] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3, &f4); }
8593 else if constexpr (n == 6) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3, &f4, &f5); }
8594 else if constexpr (n == 7) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3, &f4, &f5, &f6); }
8595 else if constexpr (n == 8) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3, &f4, &f5, &f6, &f7); }
8596 else if constexpr (n == 9) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7, f8] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3, &f4, &f5, &f6, &f7, &f8); }
8597 else if constexpr (n == 10) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7, f8, f9] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3, &f4, &f5, &f6, &f7, &f8, &f9); }
8598 else if constexpr (n == 11) { auto &[ f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7, f8, f9, f10] = o; return ::std::make_tuple( &f0, &f1, &f2, &f3, &f4, &f5, &f6, &f7, &f8, &f9, &f10); }

8625template <auto Ptr>
8626constexpr ::std::string_view pretty_ptr_() { return __PRETTY_FUNCTION__; }
8627
8628// The field name is the trailing identifier of the NTTP value:
8629// Clang: "...pretty_ptr_() [Ptr = &probe_obj.id]"
8630// GCC: "...pretty_ptr_() [with auto Ptr = (& probe_obj<Foo>.Foo::id); ...]"
8631// The value ends at the first ';' (GCC alias separator) or the final ']'.
8632constexpr ::std::string_view parse_field_name_(::std::string_view pf) {
8633 ::std::size_t end = pf.find(';');
8634 if (end == ::std::string_view::npos) end = pf.rfind(']');
8635 if (end == ::std::string_view::npos) end = pf.size();
8636 ::std::size_t i = end;
8637 while (i > 0 && (pf[i - 1] == ')' || pf[i - 1] == ' ')) --i;
8638 ::std::size_t e = i;
8639 auto is_id = [](char c) {
8640 return (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') ||
8641 (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_';
8642 };
8643 while (i > 0 && is_id(pf[i - 1])) --i;
8644 return pf.substr(i, e - i);
8645}
8646
8647template <class T, ::std::size_t I>
8648constexpr ::std::string_view field_name() {
8649 constexpr auto ptr = ::std::get<I>(field_ptrs(probe_obj<::std::remove_cvref_t<T>>));
8650 return parse_field_name_(pretty_ptr_<ptr>());
8651}
8652
8653// Invoke fn(field_name, field_ref) for each field, in declaration order.
8654template <class T, class F, ::std::size_t... Is>
8655constexpr void for_each_field_(T &o, F &&fn, ::std::index_sequence<Is...>) {
8656 auto ptrs = field_ptrs(o);
8657 (fn(field_name<T, Is>(), *::std::get<Is>(ptrs)), ...);
8658}
8659template <class T, class F>
8660constexpr void for_each_field(T &o, F &&fn) {
8661 for_each_field_(o, static_cast<F &&>(fn),
8662 ::std::make_index_sequence<field_count<T>()>{});
8663}
8664
8665} // namespace refl
8666
8667// A type qbuem can serialize purely by aggregate reflection: a real aggregate
8668// (so structured bindings work), not an array/scalar/container, with at least one
8669// field and no explicit registration (the macro / from_qbuem_json always wins).
8670template <typename T>
8671concept ReflectableAggregate =
8672 ::std::is_aggregate_v<::std::remove_cvref_t<T>> &&
8673 ::std::is_default_constructible_v<::std::remove_cvref_t<T>> &&
8674 !::std::is_array_v<::std::remove_cvref_t<T>> &&
8675 !::std::is_union_v<::std::remove_cvref_t<T>> &&
8676 // Exclude tuple-like types (std::array / std::tuple / std::pair): they are
8677 // aggregates too, but their structured binding follows the tuple protocol
8678 // (N elements) while field_count sees one member — and they have dedicated
8679 // array/tuple branches. Checked before field_count so it never probes them.
8680 !requires { ::std::tuple_size<::std::remove_cvref_t<T>>::value; } &&
8681 (refl::field_count<T>() >= 1) &&
8682 (refl::field_count<T>() <= refl::kReflectMaxFields);
8683
8684// ── Forward declarations
8685
8686template <typename T> void from_json(const Value &v, T &out);
8687template <typename T> std::string to_json_str(const T &in);
8688template <typename W, typename T> void append_json(W &out, const T &in);
8689template <typename T> void append_json(std::string &out, const T &in);

8691// ── FastWriter forward declarations (full definition later) ──────────────────
8692struct FastWriter;
8693QBUEM_INLINE void json_put(std::string &s, char c) noexcept;
8694QBUEM_INLINE void json_write(std::string &s, const char *p, size_t n) noexcept;
8695QBUEM_INLINE void json_put(FastWriter &w, char c) noexcept;
8696QBUEM_INLINE void json_write(FastWriter &w, const char *p, size_t n) noexcept;
