8698// ── Tuple/pair helpers
8699
8700template <typename Tup> void from_json_tuple_(const Value &v, Tup &out) {
8701 std::vector<Value> elems;
8702 for (const auto &e : v.elements())
8703 elems.push_back(e);
8704 std::apply(
8705 [&](auto &...args) {
8706 size_t i = 0;
8707 ((i < elems.size() ? (from_json(elems[i++], args), void())
8708 : (++i, void())),
8709 ...);
8710 },
8711 out);
8712}
8713
8714template <typename Tup> std::string to_json_str_tuple_(const Tup &in) {
8715 std::string s = "[";
8716 bool first = true;
8717 std::apply(
8718 [&](const auto &...args) {
8719 ((s += (std::exchange(first, false) ? "" : ",") + to_json_str(args)),
8720 ...);
8721 },
8722 in);
8723 return s + ']';
8724}
8725
8726template <typename W, typename Tup>
8727void append_json_tuple_(W &out, const Tup &in) {
8728 json_put(out, '[');
8729 bool first = true;
8730 std::apply(
8731 [&](const auto &...args) {
8732 (((first ? (first = false, void()) : (void)json_put(out, ',')),
8733 append_json(out, args)),
8734 ...);
8735 },
8736 in);
8737 json_put(out, ']');
8738}
8739
8740// ── from_json — concept-dispatched deserialization ───────────────────────────
8741//
8742// Precedence (highest to lowest):
8743// nullptr_t → bool → arithmetic → string → optional → sequence → set →
8744// map → fixed-array → tuple → ADL from_qbuem_json → static_assert
8745
8746template <typename T> void from_json(const Value &v, T &out) {
8747 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::nullptr_t>) {
8748 // nothing — null is null
8749 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailBool<T>) {
8750 out = v.as<bool>();
8751 } else if constexpr (std::is_enum_v<T>) {
8752 if constexpr (JsonDetailStringEnum<T>) {
8753 T tmp{};
8754 if (qbuem_enum_from_string(v.template as<std::string_view>(), tmp)) out = tmp;
8755 } else {
8756 out = static_cast<T>(v.template as<std::underlying_type_t<T>>());
8757 }
8758 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailArith<T>) {
8759 out = v.as<T>();
8760 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::string>) {
8761 out = v.as<std::string>();
8762 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailOptional<T>) {
8763 if (!v.is_valid() || v.is_null()) {
8764 out = std::nullopt;
8765 return;
8766 }
8767 typename T::value_type inner{};
8768 from_json(v, inner);
8769 out = std::move(inner);
8770 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailSeq<T>) {
8771 out.clear();
8772 for (const auto &elem : v.elements()) {
8773 typename T::value_type item{};
8774 from_json(elem, item);
8775 out.push_back(std::move(item));
8776 }
8777 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailSet<T>) {
8778 out.clear();
8779 for (const auto &elem : v.elements()) {
8780 typename T::value_type item{};
8781 from_json(elem, item);
8782 out.insert(std::move(item));
8783 }
8784 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailMap<T>) {
8785 out.clear();
8786 for (const auto &[k, val] : v.items()) {
8787 typename T::mapped_type item{};
8788 from_json(val, item);
8789 out.emplace(std::string(k), std::move(item));
8790 }
8791 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailFixedArr<T>) {
8792 constexpr size_t N = std::tuple_size_v<T>;
8793 size_t i = 0;
8794 for (const auto &elem : v.elements()) {
8795 if (i >= N)
8796 break;
8797 from_json(elem, out[i++]);
8798 }
8799 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailTuple<T>) {
8800 from_json_tuple_(v, out);
8801 } else if constexpr (HasFromQbuemJson<T>) {
8802 from_qbuem_json(v, out); // ADL: user-defined or QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS-generated
8803 } else if constexpr (ReflectableAggregate<T>) {
8804 // Macro-free: match each reflected field name against the object's members.
8805 refl::for_each_field(out, [&](::std::string_view _nm, auto &_f) {
8806 Value _m = v[_nm];
8807 if (_m.is_valid()) from_json(_m, _f);
8808 });
8809 } else {
8810 static_assert(sizeof(T) == 0,
8811 "qbuem::read / from_json: no deserialization for T. "
8812 "Use QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS(Type, field...) or define "
8813 "from_qbuem_json(const qbuem::Value&, T&).");
8814 }
8815}
8816
8817// Strict deserialization (drives qbuem::read_strict). Identical to from_json
8818// except that a *missing required field* — a non-std::optional member of a
8819// reflectable aggregate that is absent from the input — throws parse_error
8820// instead of being left default-constructed. Recurses through the object
8821// structure (aggregates and present optionals) so nested DTOs are checked too;
8822// container elements (vector/map values, array items) fall back to plain
8823// from_json, so a "required" field inside a list element is not enforced.
8824template <typename T> void from_json_strict(const Value &v, T &out) {
8825 if constexpr (ReflectableAggregate<T>) {
8826 if (!v.is_object())
8827 throw ::qbuem::json::parse_error("read_strict: expected a JSON object", 0);
8828 refl::for_each_field(out, [&](::std::string_view _nm, auto &_f) {
8829 Value _m = v[_nm];
8830 if (_m.is_valid()) {
8831 from_json_strict(_m, _f);
8832 } else if constexpr (!JsonDetailOptional<::std::remove_cvref_t<decltype(_f)>>) {
8833 throw ::qbuem::json::parse_error(
8834 ::std::string("read_strict: missing required field '") +
8835 ::std::string(_nm) + "'",
8836 0);
8837 }
8838 });
8839 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailOptional<T>) {
8840 if (!v.is_null()) {
8841 typename T::value_type _tmp{};
8842 from_json_strict(v, _tmp);
8843 out = ::std::move(_tmp);
8844 }
8845 } else {
8846 from_json(v, out); // scalar / string / container leaf — no required concept
8847 }
8848}
8849
8850// ── to_json_str — concept-dispatched serialization ───────────────────────────
8851
8852template <typename T> std::string to_json_str(const T &in) {
8853 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::nullptr_t>) {
8854 return "null";
8855 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailBool<T>) {
8856 return in ? "true" : "false";
8857 } else if constexpr (std::is_enum_v<T>) {
8858 if constexpr (JsonDetailStringEnum<T>)
8859 return to_json_str(std::string_view(qbuem_enum_to_string(in)));
8860 else
8861 return to_json_str(static_cast<std::underlying_type_t<T>>(in));
8862 } else if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<T>) {
8863 char buf[24];
8864 char *p;
8865 if constexpr (std::is_unsigned_v<T>) {
8866 if constexpr (sizeof(T) <= 4) p = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<uint32_t>(in));
8867 else p = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<uint64_t>(in));
8868 } else {
8869 if constexpr (sizeof(T) <= 4) p = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<int32_t>(in));
8870 else p = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<int64_t>(in));
8871 }
8872 return std::string(buf, p);
8873 } else if constexpr (std::is_floating_point_v<T>) {
8874 char buf[40];
8875 // qj_nc::to_chars handles NaN/Inf → "null" internally
8876 char *ep = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<double>(in));
8877 return std::string(buf, ep);
8878 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::string> ||
8879 std::is_same_v<T, std::string_view>) {
8880 std::string r;
8881 r.reserve(in.size() + 2);
8882 r += '"';
8883 const char *s = in.data(), *e = s + in.size();
8884 while (s < e) {
8885 const char *safe = s;
8886 // SWAR: skip 8 bytes at a time when no byte needs escaping
8887 while (safe + 8 <= e) {
8888 uint64_t w; std::memcpy(&w, safe, 8);
8889 if ((swar_has_less(w, 0x20) | swar_has_byte(w, '"') |
8890 swar_has_byte(w, '\\')) == 0) { safe += 8; continue; }
8891 break;
8892 }
8893 while (safe < e) {
8894 unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(*safe);
8895 if (c < 0x20 || c == '"' || c == '\\') break;
8896 ++safe;
8897 }
8898 if (safe > s) r.append(s, safe - s);
8899 s = safe;
8900 if (s < e) {
8901 unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(*s++);
8902 if (c == '"') r.append("\\\"", 2);
8903 else if (c == '\\') r.append("\\\\", 2);
8904 else if (c == '\n') r.append("\\n", 2);
8905 else if (c == '\r') r.append("\\r", 2);
8906 else if (c == '\t') r.append("\\t", 2);
8907 else {
8908 static constexpr char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
8909 char esc[6] = {'\\', 'u', '0', '0', hex[c >> 4], hex[c & 15]};
8910 r.append(esc, 6);
8911 }
8912 }
8913 }
8914 r += '"';
8915 return r;
8916 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, const char *>) {
8917 return to_json_str(std::string_view(in ? in : ""));
8918 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailOptional<T>) {
8919 if (!in.has_value())
8920 return "null";
8921 return to_json_str(*in);
8922 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailSeq<T> || JsonDetailSet<T>) {
8923 std::string s = "[";
8924 bool first = true;
8925 for (const auto &item : in) {
8926 if (!first)
8927 s += ',';
8928 s += to_json_str(item);
8929 first = false;
8930 }
8931 return s + ']';
8932 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailMap<T>) {
8933 std::string s = "{";
8934 bool first = true;
8935 for (const auto &[k, val] : in) {
8936 if (!first)
8937 s += ',';
8938 s += to_json_str(k) + ':' + to_json_str(val);
8939 first = false;
8940 }
8941 return s + '}';
8942 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailFixedArr<T>) {
8943 constexpr size_t N = std::tuple_size_v<T>;
8944 std::string s = "[";
8945 for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
8946 if (i > 0)
8947 s += ',';
8948 s += to_json_str(in[i]);
8949 }
8950 return s + ']';
8951 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailTuple<T>) {
8952 return to_json_str_tuple_(in);
8953 } else if constexpr (HasAppendQbuemJson<T>) {
8954 std::string s;
8955 append_qbuem_json(s, in);
8956 return s;
8957 } else if constexpr (HasToQbuemJson<T>) {
8958 // User-defined: create temp document, call to_qbuem_json, dump
8959 ::std::string src = "{}";
8960 DocumentView doc;
8961 Value root = ::qbuem::json::parse_reuse(doc, src);
8962 to_qbuem_json(root, in); // ADL: user-defined or QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS-generated
8963 return root.dump();
8964 } else if constexpr (ReflectableAggregate<T>) {
8965 std::string s; // macro-free aggregate — delegate to the append_json workhorse
8966 append_json(s, in);
8967 return s;
8968 } else {
8969 static_assert(sizeof(T) == 0,
8970 "qbuem::write / to_json_str: no serialization for T. "
8971 "Use QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS(Type, field...) or define "
8972 "to_qbuem_json(qbuem::Value&, const T&).");
8973 }
8974}
8975
8976// ── FastWriter — direct buffer write (avoids per-call std::string overhead) ─
8977
8978// FastWriter: stack-buffer accumulator — zero pre-init overhead.
8979// Accumulates output in a 1 KB on-stack buffer; flushes to std::string
8980// only on overflow or destruction. For typical structs (< 1 KB JSON),
8981// the destructor flush is the ONLY std::string call.
8982struct FastWriter {
8983 static constexpr size_t kBuf = 1024;
8984 char stack_[kBuf];
8985 size_t pos_;
8986 std::string &s;
8987
8988 explicit FastWriter(std::string &s) noexcept : pos_(0), s(s) {}
8989
8990 // Flush stack to string on destruction (single s.append call).
8991 ~FastWriter() noexcept { if (pos_) s.append(stack_, pos_); }
8992
8993 QBUEM_INLINE void put(char c) noexcept {
8994 if (__builtin_expect(pos_ < kBuf, 1)) { stack_[pos_++] = c; return; }
8995 flush_then_put(c);
8996 }
8997 QBUEM_INLINE void write(const char *src, size_t n) noexcept {
8998 if (__builtin_expect(pos_ + n <= kBuf, 1)) {
8999 std::memcpy(stack_ + pos_, src, n); pos_ += n; return;
9000 }
9001 flush_then_write(src, n);
9002 }
9003 // Overwrite the last written byte (replaces trailing comma with '}'/'}'.
9004 QBUEM_INLINE void set_last(char c) noexcept {
9005 if (__builtin_expect(pos_ > 0, 1)) { stack_[pos_ - 1] = c; return; }
9006 if (!s.empty()) s.back() = c; // after flush, last byte is in s
9007 }
9008
9009 void flush() noexcept { s.append(stack_, pos_); pos_ = 0; }
9010 void flush_then_put(char c) noexcept { flush(); stack_[pos_++] = c; }
9011 void flush_then_write(const char *src, size_t n) noexcept {
9012 flush();
9013 if (__builtin_expect(n <= kBuf, 1)) {
9014 std::memcpy(stack_, src, n); pos_ = n;
9015 } else {
9016 s.append(src, n); // oversized single write: bypass stack
9017 }
9018 }
9019};
9020
9021// Writer-agnostic adapter helpers
9022QBUEM_INLINE void json_put(std::string &s, char c) noexcept { s += c; }
9023QBUEM_INLINE void json_write(std::string &s, const char *p, size_t n) noexcept { s.append(p, n); }
9024
9025QBUEM_INLINE void json_put(FastWriter &w, char c) noexcept { w.put(c); }
9026QBUEM_INLINE void json_write(FastWriter &w, const char *p, size_t n) noexcept { w.write(p, n); }
9027
9028// Concept: anything with json_put/json_write adapters
9029template <typename W>
9030concept JsonWriter = requires(W &w, char c, const char *p, size_t n) {
9031 json_put(w, c);
9032 json_write(w, p, n);
9033};
9034
9035// ── Forward-declare HasQbuemJsonFW concept (satisfied after macro expansion) ─
9036template <typename T, typename W>
9037concept HasQbuemJsonFW = requires(W &w, const T &t) { qbuem_json_append_fw(w, t); };
9038
9039// ── append_json — zero-allocation concept-dispatched streaming ─────────────
9040
9041template <typename W, typename T> void append_json(W &out, const T &in) {
9042 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::nullptr_t>) {
9043 json_write(out, "null", 4);
9044 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailBool<T>) {
9045 if (in) json_write(out, "true", 4); else json_write(out, "false", 5);
9046 } else if constexpr (std::is_enum_v<T>) {
9047 if constexpr (JsonDetailStringEnum<T>)
9048 append_json(out, std::string_view(qbuem_enum_to_string(in)));
9049 else
9050 append_json(out, static_cast<std::underlying_type_t<T>>(in));
9051 } else if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<T>) {
9052 char buf[24];
9053 char *ep;
9054 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<std::remove_cvref_t<T>, bool>) {
9055 // bool is_integral but handled above — unreachable
9056 ep = buf;
9057 } else if constexpr (std::is_unsigned_v<T>) {
9058 if constexpr (sizeof(T) <= 4) ep = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<uint32_t>(in));
9059 else ep = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<uint64_t>(in));
9060 } else {
9061 if constexpr (sizeof(T) <= 4) ep = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<int32_t>(in));
9062 else ep = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<int64_t>(in));
9063 }
9064 json_write(out, buf, static_cast<size_t>(ep - buf));
9065 } else if constexpr (std::is_floating_point_v<T>) {
9066 char buf[40];
9067 // qj_nc::to_chars handles NaN/Inf → "null" internally
9068 char *ep = qj_nc::to_chars(buf, static_cast<double>(in));
9069 json_write(out, buf, static_cast<size_t>(ep - buf));
9070 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::string> ||
9071 std::is_same_v<T, std::string_view>) {
9072 json_put(out, '"');
9073 const char *s = in.data(), *e = s + in.size();
9074 while (s < e) {
9075 const char *safe = s;
9076 // SIMD fast scan: 16 bytes/iter (SSE2 on x86-64, NEON on ARM64)
9077#if defined(QBUEM_ARCH_X86_64)
9078 while (safe + 16 <= e) {
9079 __m128i v = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i *>(safe));
9080 int mask = _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_or_si128(
9081 _mm_or_si128(_mm_cmpeq_epi8(v, _mm_set1_epi8('"')),
9082 _mm_cmpeq_epi8(v, _mm_set1_epi8('\\'))),
9083 _mm_cmplt_epi8(v, _mm_set1_epi8('\x20'))));
9084 if (!mask) { safe += 16; continue; }
9085 safe += __builtin_ctz(mask); break;
9086 }
9087#elif defined(QBUEM_HAS_NEON)
9088 while (safe + 16 <= e) {
9089 uint8x16_t v = vld1q_u8(reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(safe));
9090 uint8x16_t need = vorrq_u8(
9091 vorrq_u8(vceqq_u8(v, vdupq_n_u8('"')),
9092 vceqq_u8(v, vdupq_n_u8('\\'))),
9093 vcltq_u8(v, vdupq_n_u8(0x20)));
9094 uint64_t lo = vgetq_lane_u64(vreinterpretq_u64_u8(need), 0);
9095 uint64_t hi = vgetq_lane_u64(vreinterpretq_u64_u8(need), 1);
9096 if (!(lo | hi)) { safe += 16; continue; }
9097 safe += lo ? (__builtin_ctzll(lo) >> 3) : (8 + (__builtin_ctzll(hi) >> 3));
9098 break;
9099 }
9100#endif
9101 // SWAR-8 for remaining bytes / fallback platforms
9102 while (safe + 8 <= e) {
9103 uint64_t w; std::memcpy(&w, safe, 8);
9104 if ((swar_has_less(w, 0x20) | swar_has_byte(w, '"') |
9105 swar_has_byte(w, '\\')) == 0) { safe += 8; continue; }
9106 break;
9107 }
9108 while (safe < e) {
9109 unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(*safe);
9110 if (c < 0x20 || c == '"' || c == '\\') break;
9111 ++safe;
9112 }
9113 if (safe > s) json_write(out, s, static_cast<size_t>(safe - s));
9114 s = safe;
9115 if (s < e) {
9116 unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(*s++);
9117 if (c == '"') json_write(out, "\\\"", 2);
9118 else if (c == '\\') json_write(out, "\\\\", 2);
9119 else if (c == '\n') json_write(out, "\\n", 2);
9120 else if (c == '\r') json_write(out, "\\r", 2);
9121 else if (c == '\t') json_write(out, "\\t", 2);
9122 else {
9123 static constexpr char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
9124 char esc[6] = {'\\', 'u', '0', '0', hex[c >> 4], hex[c & 15]};
9125 json_write(out, esc, 6);
9126 }
9127 }
9128 }
9129 json_put(out, '"');
9130 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, const char *>) {
9131 append_json(out, std::string_view(in ? in : ""));
9132 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailOptional<T>) {
9133 if (!in.has_value()) { json_write(out, "null", 4); return; }
9134 append_json(out, *in);
9135 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailSeq<T> || JsonDetailSet<T>) {
9136 json_put(out, '[');
9137 bool first = true;
9138 for (const auto &item : in) {
9139 if (!first) json_put(out, ',');
9140 append_json(out, item);
9141 first = false;
9142 }
9143 json_put(out, ']');
9144 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailMap<T>) {
9145 json_put(out, '{');
9146 bool first = true;
9147 for (const auto &[k, val] : in) {
9148 if (!first) json_put(out, ',');
9149 append_json(out, k);
9150 json_put(out, ':');
9151 append_json(out, val);
9152 first = false;
9153 }
9154 json_put(out, '}');
9155 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailFixedArr<T>) {
9156 constexpr size_t N = std::tuple_size_v<T>;
9157 json_put(out, '[');
9158 for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
9159 if (i > 0) json_put(out, ',');
9160 append_json(out, in[i]);
9161 }
9162 json_put(out, ']');
9163 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailTuple<T>) {
9164 append_json_tuple_(out, in);
9165 } else if constexpr (HasQbuemJsonFW<T, W>) {
9166 // Fast path: uses qbuem_json_append_fw (generated by updated macro)
9167 qbuem_json_append_fw(out, in);
9168 } else if constexpr (HasAppendQbuemJson<T>) {
9169 // Legacy path: append_qbuem_json takes std::string
9170 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<std::remove_cvref_t<W>, std::string>) {
9171 append_qbuem_json(out, in);
9172 } else {
9173 // W is FastWriter but type only has legacy append_qbuem_json:
9174 // write to temp string, then bulk-copy into writer
9175 std::string tmp;
9176 append_qbuem_json(tmp, in);
9177 json_write(out, tmp.data(), tmp.size());
9178 }
9179 } else if constexpr (HasToQbuemJson<T>) {
9180 ::std::string src = "{}";
9181 DocumentView doc;
9182 Value root = ::qbuem::json::parse_reuse(doc, src);
9183 to_qbuem_json(root, in);
9184 const std::string ds = root.dump();
9185 json_write(out, ds.data(), ds.size());
9186 } else if constexpr (ReflectableAggregate<T>) {
9187 // Macro-free aggregate: {"field":value,...} from reflected names. Field names
9188 // are C++ identifiers, so they need no JSON escaping.
9189 json_put(out, '{');
9190 bool _first = true;
9191 refl::for_each_field(in, [&](::std::string_view _nm, const auto &_f) {
9192 if (!_first) json_put(out, ',');
9193 _first = false;
9194 json_put(out, '"');
9195 json_write(out, _nm.data(), _nm.size());
9196 json_put(out, '"');
9197 json_put(out, ':');
9198 append_json(out, _f);
9199 });
9200 json_put(out, '}');
9201 } else {
9202 static_assert(sizeof(T) == 0,
9203 "qbuem::write / append_json: no serialization for T. "
9204 "Use QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS(Type, field...) or define "
9205 "append_qbuem_json(std::string&, const T&).");
9206 }
9207}
9208
9209// Backward-compatible std::string overload (called by existing code that
9210// uses the 2-arg form before the W template was introduced)
9211template <typename T> void append_json(std::string &out, const T &in) {
9212 append_json<std::string, T>(out, in);
9213}
9214
9215// ── CBOR (RFC 8259's binary sibling, RFC 8949) ───────────────────────────────
9216// A binary serialization backend that mirrors append_json<W,T> 1:1 and reuses
9217// the SAME type concepts, so any QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS struct serializes to CBOR with
9218// no extra per-struct code. Self-describing → any language decodes it (e.g. the
9219// JS `cbor-x` library) without a shared schema. Output goes through the same
9220// W writer abstraction (json_put / json_write) used by the JSON path.
9221
9222// Forward declaration for nested-struct dispatch (defined by QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS).
9223template <typename T, typename W>
9224concept HasQbuemJsonAppendCbor = requires(W &w, const T &t) {
9225 qbuem_json_append_cbor(w, t);
9226};
9227
9228// Write a CBOR data-item head: major type (0..7) + argument, smallest encoding.
9229// The single-byte case (argument < 24) is the overwhelming common one (small
9230// ints, map/array counts, short string lengths) and stays one append; the
9231// multi-byte cases are assembled in a stack buffer and flushed in one bulk write
9232// rather than 2–9 per-byte appends.
9233template <typename W>
9234QBUEM_INLINE void cbor_head(W &out, uint8_t major, uint64_t val) {
9235 const auto mt = static_cast<uint8_t>(major << 5);
9236 if (val < 24u) {
9237 json_put(out, static_cast<char>(mt | static_cast<uint8_t>(val)));
9238 return;
9239 }
9240 char b[9];
9241 int n;
9242 if (val <= 0xffull) {
9243 b[0] = static_cast<char>(mt | 24); b[1] = static_cast<char>(val); n = 2;
9244 } else if (val <= 0xffffull) {
9245 b[0] = static_cast<char>(mt | 25);
9246 b[1] = static_cast<char>(val >> 8); b[2] = static_cast<char>(val); n = 3;
9247 } else if (val <= 0xffffffffull) {
9248 b[0] = static_cast<char>(mt | 26);
9249 const uint32_t v = __builtin_bswap32(static_cast<uint32_t>(val));
9250 std::memcpy(b + 1, &v, 4); n = 5;
9251 } else {
9252 b[0] = static_cast<char>(mt | 27);
9253 const uint64_t v = __builtin_bswap64(val);
9254 std::memcpy(b + 1, &v, 8); n = 9;
9255 }
9256 json_write(out, b, n);
9257}
9258
9259// Compile-time CBOR-encoded map key (text header + key bytes) so the struct
9260// encoder emits each field name with ONE bulk write — the CBOR analogue of the
9261// JSON FastWriter's precomputed "\"key\":" literal. Field names are short, so the
9262// header is a single byte; the whole blob lives in .rodata.
9263template <std::size_t M>
9264constexpr auto make_cbor_key(const char (&s)[M]) {
9265 constexpr std::size_t N = M - 1; // key length, excluding the NUL terminator
9266 static_assert(N < 256, "CBOR map key (field name) too long for the fast path");
9267 std::array<char, (N < 24 ? 1 : 2) + N> k{};
9268 std::size_t o = 0;
9269 if constexpr (N < 24) {
9270 k[o++] = static_cast<char>(0x60 | N); // text(N) — 1-byte head
9271 } else {
9272 k[o++] = static_cast<char>(0x78); // text, 1-byte length follows
9273 k[o++] = static_cast<char>(N);
9274 }
9275 for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) k[o++] = s[i];
9276 return k;
9277}
9278
9279template <typename W, typename Tup, size_t... I>
9280void append_cbor_tuple_(W &out, const Tup &in, std::index_sequence<I...>);
9281
9282template <typename W, typename T> void append_cbor(W &out, const T &in) {
9283 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::nullptr_t>) {
9284 json_put(out, static_cast<char>(0xf6)); // null
9285 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailBool<T>) {
9286 json_put(out, static_cast<char>(in ? 0xf5 : 0xf4)); // true / false
9287 } else if constexpr (std::is_enum_v<T>) {
9288 if constexpr (JsonDetailStringEnum<T>)
9289 append_cbor(out, std::string_view(qbuem_enum_to_string(in))); // text
9290 else
9291 append_cbor(out, static_cast<std::underlying_type_t<T>>(in)); // integer
9292 } else if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<T>) {
9293 if constexpr (std::is_unsigned_v<T>) {
9294 cbor_head(out, 0, static_cast<uint64_t>(in));
9295 } else {
9296 const int64_t v = static_cast<int64_t>(in);
9297 if (v < 0) cbor_head(out, 1, static_cast<uint64_t>(-1 - v)); // negative
9298 else cbor_head(out, 0, static_cast<uint64_t>(v));
9299 }
9300 } else if constexpr (std::is_floating_point_v<T>) {
9301 // IEEE-754 double, big-endian (major 7, additional info 27). Assemble the
9302 // 9-byte item in a stack buffer and flush it in one bulk write.
9303 const double d = static_cast<double>(in);
9304 uint64_t bits;
9305 std::memcpy(&bits, &d, 8);
9306 bits = __builtin_bswap64(bits); // host (LE) → CBOR big-endian
9307 char b[9];
9308 b[0] = static_cast<char>(0xfb);
9309 std::memcpy(b + 1, &bits, 8);
9310 json_write(out, b, 9);
9311 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::string> ||
9312 std::is_same_v<T, std::string_view>) {
9313 cbor_head(out, 3, in.size()); // text string
9314 json_write(out, in.data(), in.size());
9315 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, const char *>) {
9316 const std::string_view sv(in ? in : "");
9317 cbor_head(out, 3, sv.size());
9318 json_write(out, sv.data(), sv.size());
9319 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailOptional<T>) {
9320 if (!in.has_value()) json_put(out, static_cast<char>(0xf6));
9321 else append_cbor(out, *in);
9322 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailSeq<T> || JsonDetailSet<T>) {
9323 if constexpr (requires { in.size(); }) {
9324 cbor_head(out, 4, in.size()); // definite-length array
9325 for (const auto &item : in) append_cbor(out, item);
9326 } else {
9327 json_put(out, static_cast<char>(0x9f)); // indefinite-length array
9328 for (const auto &item : in) append_cbor(out, item);
9329 json_put(out, static_cast<char>(0xff)); // break
9330 }
9331 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailMap<T>) {
9332 cbor_head(out, 5, in.size());
9333 for (const auto &[k, val] : in) { append_cbor(out, k); append_cbor(out, val); }
9334 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailFixedArr<T>) {
9335 constexpr size_t N = std::tuple_size_v<T>;
9336 cbor_head(out, 4, N);
9337 for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) append_cbor(out, in[i]);
9338 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailTuple<T>) {
9339 constexpr size_t N = std::tuple_size_v<T>;
9340 cbor_head(out, 4, N);
9341 append_cbor_tuple_(out, in, std::make_index_sequence<N>{});
9342 } else if constexpr (HasQbuemJsonAppendCbor<T, W>) {
9343 qbuem_json_append_cbor(out, in); // nested struct (generated by the macro)
9344 } else if constexpr (ReflectableAggregate<T>) {
9345 // Macro-free aggregate: definite-length map of reflected fields, each entry a
9346 // text key (the field name) + the encoded value.
9347 cbor_head(out, 5, refl::field_count<T>());
9348 refl::for_each_field(in, [&](::std::string_view _nm, const auto &_f) {
9349 append_cbor(out, _nm);
9350 append_cbor(out, _f);
9351 });
9352 } else {
9353 static_assert(sizeof(T) == 0,
9354 "qbuem::cbor::encode / append_cbor: no serialization for T. "
9355 "Use QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS(Type, field...).");
9356 }
9357}
9358
9359template <typename W, typename Tup, size_t... I>
9360void append_cbor_tuple_(W &out, const Tup &in, std::index_sequence<I...>) {
9361 (append_cbor(out, std::get<I>(in)), ...);
9362}
9363
9364template <typename T> void append_cbor(std::string &out, const T &in) {
9365 append_cbor<std::string, T>(out, in);
9366}
9367
9368// ── CBOR decode ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
9369// Type-driven reader: the target C++ type dictates which CBOR data item is
9370// expected (the inverse of append_cbor). Mirrors the from_json dispatch order so
9371// any QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS struct round-trips JSON ⇄ CBOR through one field list.
9372// Reads anything cbor-x / any RFC 8949 encoder emits: definite OR indefinite
9373// arrays/maps, half/single/double floats, smallest-int encodings. Strings are
9374// zero-copy views into the input buffer. Every advance is bounds-checked, so a
9375// truncated or hostile payload throws parse_error rather than reading OOB.
9376
9377// Sentinel returned by read_*_header() for an indefinite-length item (0x9f/0xbf).
9378inline constexpr size_t kCborIndef = static_cast<size_t>(-1);
9379
9380inline int &nexus_depth() noexcept; // defined below; shared recursion counter
9381// Bounds CBOR nesting to the same depth as the typed JSON path (fuzz safety:
9382// a recursive schema fed deeply-nested arrays/maps would otherwise blow the
9383// native stack). Only the array/map/optional/struct branches construct it.
9384struct CborDepthGuard {
9385 CborDepthGuard() {
9386 if (++nexus_depth() > 1024) {
9387 --nexus_depth();
9388 throw ::std::runtime_error("CBOR: input nesting too deep");
9389 }
9390 }
9391 ~CborDepthGuard() { --nexus_depth(); }
9392};
9393
9394// IEEE-754 binary16 → double (CBOR major 7 / 0xf9).
9395QBUEM_INLINE double cbor_half_to_double(uint16_t h) noexcept {
9396 const uint16_t exp = (h >> 10) & 0x1f;
9397 const uint16_t mant = h & 0x3ff;
9398 double val;
9399 if (exp == 0)
9400 val = ::std::ldexp(static_cast<double>(mant), -24);
9401 else if (exp != 31)
9402 val = ::std::ldexp(static_cast<double>(mant + 1024), exp - 25);
9403 else
9404 val = (mant == 0) ? ::std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()
9405 : ::std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
9406 return (h & 0x8000) ? -val : val;
9407}
9408
9409struct CborReader {
9410 const uint8_t *p;
9411 const uint8_t *begin;
9412 const uint8_t *end;
9413
9414 CborReader(const char *data, size_t n) noexcept
9415 : p(reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(data)), begin(p), end(p + n) {}
9416
9417 [[noreturn]] void fail(const char *msg) const {
9418 throw_parse_error(
9419 msg, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(p),
9420 ::std::string_view(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(begin),
9421 static_cast<size_t>(end - begin)));
9422 }
9423 // Guarantee at least n more bytes; otherwise the payload is truncated.
9424 QBUEM_INLINE void need(size_t n) const {
9425 if (__builtin_expect(static_cast<size_t>(end - p) < n, 0))
9426 fail("CBOR: truncated input");
9427 }
9428
9429 // Read an initial byte + its finite argument; sets mt to the major type.
9430 // Rejects additional-info 28..31 (reserved / indefinite — handled by the
9431 // header readers, never as a plain argument).
9432 //
9433 // Hot/cold split: the overwhelmingly common case is a value < 24 packed into
9434 // the initial byte (every small int, every short key length, every small
9435 // count). That path stays inline and ~5 instructions; the 1/2/4/8-byte
9436 // argument assembly is moved out-of-line so it never bloats the caller and the
9437 // inliner can fold this into the per-field decode loop.
9438 QBUEM_INLINE uint64_t read_head(uint8_t &mt) {
9439 need(1);
9440 const uint8_t ib = *p++;
9441 mt = static_cast<uint8_t>(ib >> 5);
9442 const uint8_t ai = ib & 31;
9443 if (__builtin_expect(ai < 24, 1)) return ai;
9444 return read_head_big(ai);
9445 }
9446 // Cold path: additional-info 24..27 (1/2/4/8 big-endian arg bytes).
9447 uint64_t read_head_big(uint8_t ai) {
9448 if (ai == 24) { need(1); return *p++; }
9449 if (ai == 25) { need(2); uint64_t v = (uint64_t(p[0]) << 8) | p[1]; p += 2; return v; }
9450 if (ai == 26) {
9451 need(4); uint32_t v; std::memcpy(&v, p, 4); p += 4;
9452 return __builtin_bswap32(v);
9453 }
9454 if (ai == 27) {
9455 need(8); uint64_t v; std::memcpy(&v, p, 8); p += 8;
9456 return __builtin_bswap64(v);
9457 }
9458 fail("CBOR: reserved/indefinite additional-info");
9459 }
9460
9461 bool read_bool() {
9462 need(1);
9463 const uint8_t ib = *p;
9464 if (ib == 0xf5) { ++p; return true; }
9465 if (ib == 0xf4) { ++p; return false; }
9466 fail("CBOR: expected bool");
9467 }
9468 bool try_read_null() {
9469 need(1);
9470 // Treat both null (0xf6) and undefined (0xf7) as "absent".
9471 if (*p == 0xf6 || *p == 0xf7) { ++p; return true; }
9472 return false;
9473 }
9474 void read_null() { if (!try_read_null()) fail("CBOR: expected null"); }
9475
9476 QBUEM_INLINE double read_float() {
9477 need(1);
9478 const uint8_t ib = *p;
9479 if (__builtin_expect(ib == 0xfb, 1)) { // double — the common encoding
9480 need(9); ++p; uint64_t b; ::std::memcpy(&b, p, 8); p += 8;
9481 b = __builtin_bswap64(b);
9482 double d; ::std::memcpy(&d, &b, 8); return d;
9483 }
9484 if (ib == 0xfa) {
9485 need(5); ++p; uint32_t b; ::std::memcpy(&b, p, 4); p += 4;
9486 b = __builtin_bswap32(b);
9487 float f; ::std::memcpy(&f, &b, 4); return static_cast<double>(f);
9488 }
9489 if (ib == 0xf9) {
9490 need(3); ++p; uint16_t h = static_cast<uint16_t>((uint16_t(p[0]) << 8) | p[1]);
9491 p += 2; return cbor_half_to_double(h);
9492 }
9493 // Lenient: accept an integer where a float is expected (cbor-x emits whole
9494 // numbers as ints), so {score: 3} decodes into a double field.
9495 uint8_t mt; uint64_t arg = read_head(mt);
9496 if (mt == 0) return static_cast<double>(arg);
9497 if (mt == 1) return -1.0 - static_cast<double>(arg);
9498 fail("CBOR: expected float or integer");
9499 }
9500
9501 QBUEM_INLINE ::std::string_view read_text() {
9502 uint8_t mt; uint64_t n = read_head(mt);
9503 if (__builtin_expect(mt != 3, 0)) fail("CBOR: expected text string");
9504 need(static_cast<size_t>(n));
9505 const char *s = reinterpret_cast<const char *>(p);
9506 p += n;
9507 return ::std::string_view(s, static_cast<size_t>(n));
9508 }
9509
9510 // Open an array/map. Returns the entry count, or kCborIndef for 0x9f/0xbf.
9511 QBUEM_INLINE size_t read_array_header() {
9512 need(1);
9513 if (__builtin_expect(*p == 0x9f, 0)) { ++p; return kCborIndef; }
9514 uint8_t mt; uint64_t n = read_head(mt);
9515 if (__builtin_expect(mt != 4, 0)) fail("CBOR: expected array");
9516 return static_cast<size_t>(n);
9517 }
9518 QBUEM_INLINE size_t read_map_header() {
9519 need(1);
9520 if (__builtin_expect(*p == 0xbf, 0)) { ++p; return kCborIndef; }
9521 uint8_t mt; uint64_t n = read_head(mt);
9522 if (__builtin_expect(mt != 5, 0)) fail("CBOR: expected map");
9523 return static_cast<size_t>(n);
9524 }
9525 // Non-destructive: is the next item a 1-byte-head text string whose bytes
9526 // equal `name` (a compile-time field name)? Powers the positional decode fast
9527 // path — it confirms the expected next key WITHOUT the hash + switch dispatch.
9528 // A long key (>= 24 B, 2-byte head) or any mismatch returns false, so the
9529 // caller falls back to the general hash loop. The compare is a FULL byte
9530 // compare, so it is itself a complete anti-spoof check, independent of the
9531 // hash. Does not advance p (the entry stays available for the slow path).
9532 template <std::size_t M>
9533 QBUEM_INLINE bool peek_key_eq(const char (&name)[M]) const {
9534 constexpr std::size_t L = M - 1; // field name length (excl. NUL)
9535 if constexpr (L == 0 || L >= 24) return false;
9536 if (static_cast<std::size_t>(end - p) < 1 + L) return false;
9537 if (static_cast<uint8_t>(p[0]) != static_cast<uint8_t>(0x60 | L)) return false;
9538 return __builtin_memcmp(p + 1, name, L) == 0;
9539 }
9540 // Advance past a confirmed 1-byte-head text key of length L (after a true
9541 // peek_key_eq — bounds already validated there).
9542 QBUEM_INLINE void skip_short_key(std::size_t L) { p += 1 + L; }
9543
9544 // For indefinite items: true while more entries remain (i.e. not at break).
9545 QBUEM_INLINE bool peek_break() { need(1); return *p == 0xff; }
9546 void consume_break() {
9547 need(1);
9548 if (*p != 0xff) fail("CBOR: expected break");
9549 ++p;
9550 }
9551};
9552
9553// Skip exactly one complete CBOR data item (used for unknown map keys and
9554// over-long fixed-size targets). Recursion is depth-bounded via CborDepthGuard.
9555inline void cbor_skip(CborReader &cr) {
9556 cr.need(1);
9557 const uint8_t ib = *cr.p;
9558 const uint8_t mt = static_cast<uint8_t>(ib >> 5);
9559 const uint8_t ai = ib & 31;
9560 if (ai == 31 && mt >= 2 && mt <= 5) { // indefinite array/map/byte/text string
9561 ++cr.p;
9562 CborDepthGuard g;
9563 while (!cr.peek_break()) {
9564 cbor_skip(cr);
9565 if (mt == 5) cbor_skip(cr); // map: skip the value too
9566 }
9567 cr.consume_break();
9568 return;
9569 }
9570 uint8_t m; uint64_t arg = cr.read_head(m);
9571 switch (m) {
9572 case 0: case 1: case 7: break; // int / float / simple — arg already consumed
9573 case 2: case 3: // byte / text string payload
9574 cr.need(static_cast<size_t>(arg));
9575 cr.p += arg;
9576 break;
9577 case 4: { CborDepthGuard g; for (uint64_t i = 0; i < arg; ++i) cbor_skip(cr); break; }
9578 case 5: { CborDepthGuard g; for (uint64_t i = 0; i < arg; ++i) { cbor_skip(cr); cbor_skip(cr); } break; }
9579 default: cr.fail("CBOR: unsupported major type");
9580 }
9581}
9582
9583template <typename T> void from_cbor(CborReader &cr, T &out);
9584
9585// ADL hook generated by QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS (decodes a CBOR map into the struct).
9586template <typename T>
9587concept HasQbuemJsonReadCbor =
9588 requires(CborReader &cr, T &t) { qbuem_json_read_cbor(cr, t); };
9589
9590template <typename T, size_t... I>
9591void from_cbor_tuple_(CborReader &cr, T &out, std::index_sequence<I...>) {
9592 (from_cbor(cr, std::get<I>(out)), ...);
9593}
9594
9595template <typename T> void from_cbor(CborReader &cr, T &out) {
9596 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::nullptr_t>) {
9597 cr.read_null();
9598 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailBool<T>) {
9599 out = cr.read_bool();
9600 } else if constexpr (std::is_enum_v<T>) {
9601 if constexpr (JsonDetailStringEnum<T>) {
9602 T tmp{};
9603 if (!qbuem_enum_from_string(cr.read_text(), tmp))
9604 cr.fail("CBOR: unknown enum string");
9605 out = tmp;
9606 } else {
9607 std::underlying_type_t<T> u{};
9608 from_cbor(cr, u);
9609 out = static_cast<T>(u);
9610 }
9611 } else if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<T>) {
9612 uint8_t mt; uint64_t arg = cr.read_head(mt);
9613 if (mt == 0) out = static_cast<T>(arg); // unsigned: exact
9614 else if (mt == 1) out = static_cast<T>(-1 - static_cast<int64_t>(arg));
9615 else cr.fail("CBOR: expected integer");
9616 } else if constexpr (std::is_floating_point_v<T>) {
9617 out = static_cast<T>(cr.read_float());
9618 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, std::string>) {
9619 out.assign(cr.read_text());
9620 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailOptional<T>) {
9621 if (cr.try_read_null()) { out = std::nullopt; return; }
9622 CborDepthGuard g;
9623 typename T::value_type inner{};
9624 from_cbor(cr, inner);
9625 out = std::move(inner);
9626 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailSeq<T> || JsonDetailSet<T>) {
9627 CborDepthGuard g;
9628 out.clear();
9629 const size_t n = cr.read_array_header();
9630 auto take = [&] {
9631 typename T::value_type item{};
9632 from_cbor(cr, item);
9633 if constexpr (JsonDetailSeq<T>) out.push_back(std::move(item));
9634 else out.insert(std::move(item));
9635 };
9636 if (n == kCborIndef) { while (!cr.peek_break()) take(); cr.consume_break(); }
9637 else {
9638 // Definite length is known — reserve up front to skip the growth reallocs.
9639 // Cap by the remaining bytes (every element is ≥ 1 byte) so a hostile huge
9640 // count can't drive a giant allocation.
9641 if constexpr (requires { out.reserve(n); }) {
9642 const size_t cap = static_cast<size_t>(cr.end - cr.p);
9643 out.reserve(n < cap ? n : cap);
9644 }
9645 for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) take();
9646 }
9647 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailMap<T>) {
9648 CborDepthGuard g;
9649 out.clear();
9650 const size_t n = cr.read_map_header();
9651 auto take = [&] {
9652 std::string k(cr.read_text());
9653 typename T::mapped_type item{};
9654 from_cbor(cr, item);
9655 out.emplace(std::move(k), std::move(item));
9656 };
9657 if (n == kCborIndef) { while (!cr.peek_break()) take(); cr.consume_break(); }
9658 else { for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) take(); }
9659 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailFixedArr<T>) {
9660 CborDepthGuard g;
9661 constexpr size_t N = std::tuple_size_v<T>;
9662 const size_t n = cr.read_array_header();
9663 if (n == kCborIndef) {
9664 size_t i = 0;
9665 while (!cr.peek_break()) {
9666 if (i < N) from_cbor(cr, out[i++]); else cbor_skip(cr);
9667 }
9668 cr.consume_break();
9669 } else {
9670 for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
9671 if (i < N) from_cbor(cr, out[i]); else cbor_skip(cr);
9672 }
9673 }
9674 } else if constexpr (JsonDetailTuple<T>) {
9675 CborDepthGuard g;
9676 constexpr size_t N = std::tuple_size_v<T>;
9677 const size_t n = cr.read_array_header();
9678 from_cbor_tuple_(cr, out, std::make_index_sequence<N>{});
9679 // Drain any extra elements an oversized encoder may have written.
9680 if (n == kCborIndef) { while (!cr.peek_break()) cbor_skip(cr); cr.consume_break(); }
9681 else { for (size_t i = N; i < n; ++i) cbor_skip(cr); }
9682 } else if constexpr (HasQbuemJsonReadCbor<T>) {
9683 CborDepthGuard g;
9684 qbuem_json_read_cbor(cr, out); // nested struct (generated by the macro)
9685 } else if constexpr (ReflectableAggregate<T>) {
9686 // Macro-free aggregate: read a map and match each text key against the
9687 // reflected field names; unknown keys are skipped.
9688 CborDepthGuard g;
9689 const size_t n = cr.read_map_header();
9690 const bool indef = (n == kCborIndef);
9691 for (size_t i = 0; indef ? !cr.peek_break() : (i < n); ++i) {
9692 const std::string_view key = cr.read_text();
9693 bool matched = false;
9694 refl::for_each_field(out, [&](std::string_view nm, auto &f) {
9695 if (!matched && nm == key) { matched = true; from_cbor(cr, f); }
9696 });
9697 if (!matched) cbor_skip(cr);
9698 }
9699 if (indef) cr.consume_break();
9700 } else {
9701 static_assert(sizeof(T) == 0,
9702 "qbuem::cbor::decode / from_cbor: no deserialization for T. "
9703 "Use QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS(Type, field...).");
9704 }
9705}
9706
9707// Verify an incoming CBOR map key against a compile-time field name, AFTER its
9708// hash already matched the field's switch case. The hash is collision-prone, so
9709// a verify is mandatory (defends against an attacker routing a forged key into
9710// the wrong field). But for names ≤ 8 bytes, fast_key_hash IS the raw
9711// little-endian bytes, so "equal hash + equal length" already proves the bytes
9712// are identical — a single length compare is a *complete* defense and skips the
9713// memcmp on every field. Longer names (9+ bytes, where the hash folds/FNVs and
9714// can genuinely collide) fall back to a full byte compare.
9715template <std::size_t M>
9716QBUEM_INLINE bool cbor_key_matches(std::string_view key, const char (&name)[M]) {
9717 constexpr std::size_t L = M - 1; // exclude NUL
9718 if constexpr (L <= 8) return key.size() == L;
9719 else return key == std::string_view(name, L);
9720}
9721
9722// ── Per-field helpers for QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS
9723
9724template <typename T>
9725inline void from_json_field(const Value &obj, const char *key, T &field) {
9726 auto opt = obj.find(key);
9727 if (!opt)
9728 return;
9729 if constexpr (is_specialization_of<T, std::optional>::value) {
9730 from_json(*opt, field);
9731 } else {
9732 if (!opt->is_null())
9733 from_json(*opt, field);
9734 }
9735}
9736
9737template <typename T>
9738inline void to_json_field(Value &obj, const char *key, const T &val) {
9739 obj.insert_json(key, to_json_str(val));
9740}

9803// ── Field spec normalization (rename) ────────────────────────────────────────
9804// A field listed in QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS may be either a bare member name, which
9805// uses its own identifier as the JSON/CBOR key, or `(member, "jsonKey")` to map
9806// it to a different wire key (rename — e.g. snake_case C++ ↔ camelCase JSON, or a
9807// reserved word). The two helpers below extract the C++ member token and the
9808// key string-literal from either form. Skipping a field needs no syntax: omit
9809// it from the list and it is neither serialized nor read.
9810//
9811// QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(score) → score QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(score) → "score"
9812// QBUEM_FIELD_CPP((score, "pts")) → score QBUEM_FIELD_KEY((score, "pts")) → "pts"
9813#define QBUEM_DETAIL_FIELD_FST(a, ...) a
9814#define QBUEM_DETAIL_FIELD_SND(a, b) b
9815// QBUEM_DETAIL_IS_PAREN(x): 1 if x is parenthesized, else 0.
9816#define QBUEM_DETAIL_CHECK_N(x, n, ...) n
9817#define QBUEM_DETAIL_CHECK(...) QBUEM_DETAIL_EXPAND(QBUEM_DETAIL_CHECK_N(__VA_ARGS__, 0,))
9818#define QBUEM_DETAIL_PROBE_PAREN(...) ~, 1,
9819#define QBUEM_DETAIL_IS_PAREN(x) QBUEM_DETAIL_CHECK(QBUEM_DETAIL_PROBE_PAREN x)
9820#define QBUEM_DETAIL_IIF(cond) QBUEM_DETAIL_CONCAT2(QBUEM_DETAIL_IIF_, cond)
9821#define QBUEM_DETAIL_IIF_0(t, f) f
9822#define QBUEM_DETAIL_IIF_1(t, f) t
9823
9824#define QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(F) \
9825 QBUEM_DETAIL_IIF(QBUEM_DETAIL_IS_PAREN(F)) \
9826 (QBUEM_FIELD_CPP_P, QBUEM_FIELD_CPP_B)(F)
9827#define QBUEM_FIELD_CPP_B(n) n
9828#define QBUEM_FIELD_CPP_P(t) QBUEM_DETAIL_FIELD_FST t
9829
9830#define QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(F) \
9831 QBUEM_DETAIL_IIF(QBUEM_DETAIL_IS_PAREN(F)) \
9832 (QBUEM_FIELD_KEY_P, QBUEM_FIELD_KEY_B)(F)
9833#define QBUEM_FIELD_KEY_B(n) #n
9834#define QBUEM_FIELD_KEY_P(t) QBUEM_DETAIL_FIELD_SND t
9835
9836// ============================================================================
9837// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS — one-line struct serialization/deserialization
9838// ============================================================================
9839
9840#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_READ(f) \
9841 ::qbuem::json::detail::from_json_field(v, QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f), \
9842 obj.QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(f));
9843#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_WRITE(f) \
9844 ::qbuem::json::detail::to_json_field(v, QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f), \
9845 obj.QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(f));
9846#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_PULSE(f) \
9847 case ::qbuem::json::detail::fast_key_hash_ce(QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f)): \
9848 /* Verify the actual key bytes — the hash is collision-prone, so without \
9849 this an untrusted key could be routed into the wrong field (spoofing / \
9850 type confusion). One short compare per object key. */ \
9851 if (_key == ::std::string_view(QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f), \
9852 sizeof(QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f)) - 1)) \
9853 ::qbuem::json::detail::from_json_direct(p, end, obj.QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(f)); \
9854 else \
9855 ::qbuem::json::detail::skip_direct(p, end); \
9856 break;
9857
9858// QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_FW — FastWriter path: zero std::string overhead
9859#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_FW(f) \
9860 { \
9861 static constexpr char _bj_kf[] = "\"" QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f) "\":"; \
9862 _bj_fw.write(_bj_kf, sizeof(_bj_kf) - 1); \
9863 } \
9864 ::qbuem::json::detail::append_json(_bj_fw, obj.QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(f)); \
9865 _bj_fw.put(',');
9866
9867// QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_CBOR — one CBOR map entry: text key + value
9868#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_CBOR(f) \
9869 { \
9870 static constexpr auto _bck = \
9871 ::qbuem::json::detail::make_cbor_key(QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f)); \
9872 ::qbuem::json::detail::json_write(_bj_w, _bck.data(), _bck.size()); \
9873 } \
9874 ::qbuem::json::detail::append_cbor(_bj_w, obj.QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(f));
9875
9876// QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_READ — one switch case routing a CBOR map key to its
9877// field. The hash is collision-prone, so the key bytes are verified before the
9878// field is filled (same spoofing defence as the JSON nexus_pulse path); an
9879// unmatched key has its value skipped wholesale.
9880#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_READ(f) \
9881 case ::qbuem::json::detail::fast_key_hash_ce(QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f)): \
9882 if (::qbuem::json::detail::cbor_key_matches(_key, QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f))) \
9883 ::qbuem::json::detail::from_cbor(_cr, obj.QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(f)); \
9884 else \
9885 ::qbuem::json::detail::cbor_skip(_cr); \
9886 break;
9887
9888// QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_FAST — one step of the positional fast path. While the
9889// map's keys arrive in struct-declaration order (the common case — our own
9890// encoder, and most others, preserve field order), each field is confirmed with
9891// a single non-destructive byte compare and decoded directly: no hash, no switch
9892// indirect branch, no separate verify. The first key that does NOT match the
9893// expected field flips _bfast off, leaving that (and every later) entry to the
9894// general hash-dispatch loop below — so reordered / foreign / partial maps stay
9895// correct, just without the fast path.
9896#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_FAST(f) \
9897 if (_bfast && (_bindef ? !_cr.peek_break() : (_bi < _bn)) && \
9898 _cr.peek_key_eq(QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f))) { \
9899 _cr.skip_short_key(sizeof(QBUEM_FIELD_KEY(f)) - 1); \
9900 ::qbuem::json::detail::from_cbor(_cr, obj.QBUEM_FIELD_CPP(f)); \
9901 ++_bi; \
9902 } else { \
9903 _bfast = false; \
9904 }
9905
9906#define QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS(Type, ...) \
9907 /* Fast dispatch on pre-computed key hash — primary hot path */ \
9908 inline void nexus_pulse_h(uint64_t _h, ::std::string_view _key, \
9909 const char *&p, const char *end, Type &obj) { \
9910 switch (_h) { \
9911 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_PULSE, __VA_ARGS__) \
9912 default: \
9913 ::qbuem::json::detail::skip_direct(p, end); \
9914 break; \
9915 } \
9916 } \
9917 /* Backward-compat wrapper: hashes the key then dispatches via nexus_pulse_h */\
9918 inline void nexus_pulse(::std::string_view key, const char *&p, \
9919 const char *end, Type &obj) { \
9920 nexus_pulse_h(::qbuem::json::detail::fast_key_hash(key), key, p, end, \
9921 obj); \
9922 } \
9923 inline void from_qbuem_json(const ::qbuem::json::Value &v, Type &obj) { \
9924 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_READ, __VA_ARGS__) \
9925 } \
9926 inline void to_qbuem_json(::qbuem::json::Value &v, const Type &obj) { \
9927 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_WRITE, __VA_ARGS__) \
9928 } \
9929 /* FastWriter serialization — zero std::string overhead */ \
9930 inline void qbuem_json_append_fw(::qbuem::json::detail::FastWriter &_bj_fw, \
9931 const Type &obj) { \
9932 _bj_fw.put('{'); \
9933 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_FW, __VA_ARGS__) \
9934 _bj_fw.set_last('}'); \
9935 } \
9936 inline void qbuem_json_append_fw(std::string &_bj_s, const Type &obj) { \
9937 ::qbuem::json::detail::FastWriter _bj_fw(_bj_s); /* uses spare cap */ \
9938 qbuem_json_append_fw(_bj_fw, obj); \
9939 } \
9940 inline void append_qbuem_json(std::string &out, const Type &obj) { \
9941 qbuem_json_append_fw(out, obj); \
9942 } \
9943 /* CBOR serialization — DEFINITE-length map of the registered fields. The \
9944 field count is known at compile time, so a definite header (0xA0|N for \
9945 N<24, one byte) beats an indefinite map (0xBF … 0xFF): it drops the \
9946 trailing break byte and lets the decoder run a counted loop instead of a \
9947 per-entry break check. Decoders still accept either form. */ \
9948 template <typename _W> \
9949 inline void qbuem_json_append_cbor(_W &_bj_w, const Type &obj) { \
9950 ::qbuem::json::detail::cbor_head( \
9951 _bj_w, 5, QBUEM_DETAIL_COUNT(__VA_ARGS__)); /* map(N) */ \
9952 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_CBOR, __VA_ARGS__) \
9953 } \
9954 /* CBOR deserialization — reads a map (definite or indefinite), dispatching \
9955 each text key to its field; unknown keys are skipped. Templated on the \
9956 reader (always CborReader) purely so it is instantiated lazily — only \
9957 structs actually decoded pay the from_cbor type-check, matching the \
9958 append_cbor template above. */ \
9959 template <typename _R> \
9960 inline void qbuem_json_read_cbor(_R &_cr, Type &obj) { \
9961 const ::std::size_t _bn = _cr.read_map_header(); \
9962 const bool _bindef = (_bn == ::qbuem::json::detail::kCborIndef); \
9963 ::std::size_t _bi = 0; \
9964 bool _bfast = true; \
9965 /* Positional fast path: consume the in-order prefix with direct key \
9966 compares (no hash / switch); bails to the loop below on first mismatch. */\
9967 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_FAST, __VA_ARGS__) \
9968 (void)_bfast; \
9969 /* General path: remaining entries (reordered / unknown / foreign maps). */\
9970 for (; _bindef ? !_cr.peek_break() : (_bi < _bn); ++_bi) { \
9971 const ::std::string_view _key = _cr.read_text(); \
9972 switch (::qbuem::json::detail::fast_key_hash(_key)) { \
9973 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_READ, __VA_ARGS__) \
9974 default: \
9975 ::qbuem::json::detail::cbor_skip(_cr); \
9976 break; \
9977 } \
9978 } \
9979 if (_bindef) _cr.consume_break(); \
9980 }
9981
9982// ============================================================================
9983// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS_TPL — register a CLASS TEMPLATE once for ALL instantiations
9984// ============================================================================
9985//
9986// Same ADL surface as QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS (DOM read/write, Nexus fuse, FastWriter,
9987// CBOR encode/decode), but emitted as function TEMPLATES so ADL resolves them
9988// for any instantiation — no need to register each concrete type. Pass the
9989// template-parameter list and the dependent type each WRAPPED IN PARENTHESES (so
9990// their internal commas survive as one macro argument), then the field names:
9991//
9992// template <typename T> struct Box { T v; int tag; };
9993// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS_TPL((typename T), (Box<T>), v, tag)
9994//
9995// template <typename A, typename B> struct Pair { A a; B b; };
9996// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS_TPL((typename A, typename B), (Pair<A, B>), a, b)
9997//
9998// Must be invoked at namespace scope in the same namespace as the template (ADL).
9999// Do NOT also register a concrete instantiation of the same template with
10000// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS — the two would be an ambiguous overload set.
10001//
10002// NB: this mirrors QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS function-for-function (only the template
10003// heads and the type spelling differ — every per-field detail macro is shared).
10004// Keep the two in sync if the generated function set changes.
10005#define QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS_TPL(TParams, Type, ...) \
10006 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams> \
10007 inline void nexus_pulse_h(uint64_t _h, ::std::string_view _key, \
10008 const char *&p, const char *end, \
10009 QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10010 switch (_h) { \
10011 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_PULSE, __VA_ARGS__) \
10012 default: \
10013 ::qbuem::json::detail::skip_direct(p, end); \
10014 break; \
10015 } \
10016 } \
10017 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams> \
10018 inline void nexus_pulse(::std::string_view key, const char *&p, \
10019 const char *end, QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10020 nexus_pulse_h(::qbuem::json::detail::fast_key_hash(key), key, p, end, \
10021 obj); \
10022 } \
10023 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams> \
10024 inline void from_qbuem_json(const ::qbuem::json::Value &v, \
10025 QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10026 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_READ, __VA_ARGS__) \
10027 } \
10028 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams> \
10029 inline void to_qbuem_json(::qbuem::json::Value &v, \
10030 const QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10031 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_WRITE, __VA_ARGS__) \
10032 } \
10033 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams> \
10034 inline void qbuem_json_append_fw(::qbuem::json::detail::FastWriter &_bj_fw, \
10035 const QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10036 _bj_fw.put('{'); \
10037 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_FW, __VA_ARGS__) \
10038 _bj_fw.set_last('}'); \
10039 } \
10040 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams> \
10041 inline void qbuem_json_append_fw(std::string &_bj_s, \
10042 const QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10043 ::qbuem::json::detail::FastWriter _bj_fw(_bj_s); \
10044 qbuem_json_append_fw(_bj_fw, obj); \
10045 } \
10046 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams> \
10047 inline void append_qbuem_json(std::string &out, \
10048 const QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10049 qbuem_json_append_fw(out, obj); \
10050 } \
10051 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams, typename _W> \
10052 inline void qbuem_json_append_cbor(_W &_bj_w, \
10053 const QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10054 ::qbuem::json::detail::cbor_head( \
10055 _bj_w, 5, QBUEM_DETAIL_COUNT(__VA_ARGS__)); /* map(N) */ \
10056 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_APPEND_CBOR, __VA_ARGS__) \
10057 } \
10058 template <QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN TParams, typename _R> \
10059 inline void qbuem_json_read_cbor(_R &_cr, QBUEM_DETAIL_UNPAREN Type &obj) { \
10060 const ::std::size_t _bn = _cr.read_map_header(); \
10061 const bool _bindef = (_bn == ::qbuem::json::detail::kCborIndef); \
10062 ::std::size_t _bi = 0; \
10063 bool _bfast = true; \
10064 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_FAST, __VA_ARGS__) \
10065 (void)_bfast; \
10066 for (; _bindef ? !_cr.peek_break() : (_bi < _bn); ++_bi) { \
10067 const ::std::string_view _key = _cr.read_text(); \
10068 switch (::qbuem::json::detail::fast_key_hash(_key)) { \
10069 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_CBOR_READ, __VA_ARGS__) \
10070 default: \
10071 ::qbuem::json::detail::cbor_skip(_cr); \
10072 break; \
10073 } \
10074 } \
10075 if (_bindef) _cr.consume_break(); \
10076 }

10078// ============================================================================
10079// QBUEM_JSON_ENUM — serialize an enum as its value name (string) everywhere
10080// ============================================================================
10081//
10082// Without this, an enum serializes as its underlying integer (works out of the
10083// box). With it, the enum round-trips as the value name across every engine
10084// (DOM, fuse, CBOR). Invoke at the enum's namespace scope (ADL), like
10085// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS:
10086//
10087// enum class Color { Red, Green, Blue };
10088// QBUEM_JSON_ENUM(Color, Red, Green, Blue)
10089//
10090// Unknown strings: on read they leave the field unchanged (DOM) / throw
10091// (CBOR / strict fuse). Names are the C++ enumerator identifiers; for custom
10092// wire strings, write the two hooks by hand (qbuem_enum_to_string /
10093// qbuem_enum_from_string).
10094#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_ENUM_TO(A) case _qb_enum_t::A: return #A;
10095#define QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_ENUM_FROM(A) \
10096 if (_qb_s == ::std::string_view(#A)) { _qb_e = _qb_enum_t::A; return true; }
10097
10098#define QBUEM_JSON_ENUM(EnumType, ...) \
10099 inline ::std::string_view qbuem_enum_to_string(EnumType _qb_v) noexcept { \
10100 using _qb_enum_t = EnumType; \
10101 switch (_qb_v) { \
10102 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_ENUM_TO, __VA_ARGS__) \
10103 } \
10104 return {}; \
10105 } \
10106 inline bool qbuem_enum_from_string(::std::string_view _qb_s, \
10107 EnumType &_qb_e) noexcept { \
10108 using _qb_enum_t = EnumType; \
10109 QBUEM_FOR_EACH(QBUEM_JSON_DETAIL_ENUM_FROM, __VA_ARGS__) \
10110 return false; \
10111 }

10148using parse_error = json::parse_error; // thrown by parse*/read/fuse; offset()/line()/column()
10149
10150// format_error(e, source) — render a parse_error against its original source as a
10151// human-readable, multi-line message: the failing line plus a caret under the
10152// column. `source` must be the same buffer that was parsed; if the error carries
10153// no line info (e.g. a binary/CBOR error) or `source` is empty, returns e.what().
10154//
10155// try { qbuem::read<T>(json); }
10156// catch (const qbuem::parse_error& e) { std::cerr << qbuem::format_error(e, json) << '\n'; }
10157//
10158// Invalid JSON at line 3 column 14 (byte 42)
10159// "score": 3.5.7,
10160// ^
10161inline ::std::string format_error(const parse_error &e,
10162 ::std::string_view source) {
10163 ::std::string out = e.what();
10164 const ::std::size_t line = e.line();
10165 if (line == 0 || source.empty()) return out; // no positional context
10166
10167 // Locate the [start, stop) byte range of the offending line.
10168 ::std::size_t start = 0;
10169 for (::std::size_t cur = 1; cur < line; ++cur) {
10170 const ::std::size_t nl = source.find('\n', start);
10171 if (nl == ::std::string_view::npos) { start = source.size(); break; }
10172 start = nl + 1;
10173 }
10174 ::std::size_t stop = source.find('\n', start);
10175 if (stop == ::std::string_view::npos) stop = source.size();
10176 if (stop > start && source[stop - 1] == '\r') --stop; // trim CR of CRLF
10177 ::std::string_view text = source.substr(start, stop - start);
10178
10179 // 0-based caret column within the line; clamp into the (possibly windowed) line.
10180 ::std::size_t caret = e.column() ? e.column() - 1 : 0;
10181
10182 // Window very long lines so a minified blob doesn't dump everything: keep ~100
10183 // bytes around the caret, marking elision with a leading "…".
10184 constexpr ::std::size_t kWindow = 100;
10185 ::std::string prefix;
10186 if (text.size() > kWindow && caret > 40) {
10187 const ::std::size_t from = caret - 40;
10188 text = text.substr(from, kWindow);
10189 caret -= from;
10190 prefix = "…";
10191 } else if (text.size() > kWindow) {
10192 text = text.substr(0, kWindow);
10193 }
10194 if (caret > text.size()) caret = text.size();
10195
10196 out += '\n';
10197 out += " ";
10198 out += prefix;
10199 out.append(text.data(), text.size());
10200 out += "\n ";
10201 out.append(prefix.size() + caret, ' ');
10202 out += '^';
10203 return out;
10204}

10208// ── parse* lifetime contract ────────────────────────────────────────────────
10209// parse/parse_reuse/parse_strict are ZERO-COPY: the returned Value (and the
10210// Document) holds a non-owning view of `json`. The input buffer MUST outlive
10211// the Document and every Value derived from it — nothing is copied. To make
10212// the most common misuse a COMPILE error instead of a silent use-after-free,
10213// the rvalue-`std::string` overloads are deleted, so e.g.
10214// auto v = qbuem::parse(doc, get_config_json()); // ERROR: deleted overload
10215// will not compile. Pass an lvalue you keep alive (or a string literal), e.g.
10216// std::string text = get_config_json(); auto v = qbuem::parse(doc, text);
10217// If you need an owning value, use read<T>()/fuse<T>() (they copy into T).
10218//
10219// Thread-safety / aliasing:
10220// • A Document owns mutable parse state; one Document is single-threaded. Do
10221// NOT parse into, mutate, or destroy the same Document from two threads.
10222// • Every Value/SafeValue from a Document ALIASES that Document's tape and the
10223// input buffer — they are lightweight handles, not copies. After a read-only
10224// parse you MAY hand those handles to multiple threads that only READ
10225// concurrently (no data race: the tape is immutable once parsed). As soon as
10226// ANY thread mutates (insert/erase/operator[]=/merge_patch) or re-parses the
10227// Document, all concurrent access must stop — mutation rewrites shared state.
10228// • Distinct Documents share nothing and are fully independent across threads.
10229inline Value parse(Document &doc, ::std::string_view json) {
10230 return json::parse_reuse(doc, json);
10231}
10232inline Value parse(Document &doc, const char *json) {
10233 return json::parse_reuse(doc, ::std::string_view(json));
10234}
10235Value parse(Document &, const ::std::string &&) = delete;
10236
10237inline Value parse_reuse(Document &doc, ::std::string_view json) {
10238 return json::parse_reuse(doc, json);
10239}
10240inline Value parse_reuse(Document &doc, const char *json) {
10241 return json::parse_reuse(doc, ::std::string_view(json));
10242}
10243Value parse_reuse(Document &, const ::std::string &&) = delete;
10244
10245inline Value parse_strict(Document &doc, ::std::string_view json) {
10246 json::rfc8259::validate(json);
10247 return json::parse_reuse(doc, json);
10248}
10249inline Value parse_strict(Document &doc, const char *json) {
10250 return parse_strict(doc, ::std::string_view(json));
10251}
10252Value parse_strict(Document &, const ::std::string &&) = delete;
