10899// ── Canonical JSON ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
10900// qbuem::canonicalize(json) → a deterministic serialization: the SAME logical
10901// document always produces the SAME bytes, so it can be hashed, signed, or
10902// content-addressed. Follows the RFC 8785 (JCS) structure: object keys sorted
10903// lexicographically, no insignificant whitespace, shortest numeric forms,
10904// minimal string escaping, -0 normalized to 0.
10905//
10906// Scope (honest about the two places it diverges from byte-exact RFC 8785):
10907// • keys are ordered by Unicode code point (UTF-8 byte order); RFC 8785 uses
10908// UTF-16 order, which differs only for keys containing supplementary-plane
10909// (non-BMP) characters.
10910// • numbers use the library's shortest round-trip format, which matches the
10911// RFC 8785 ECMAScript form across the common range; very large/small
10912// magnitudes may differ in exponential notation (e.g. "1E21" vs "1e+21").
10913// For in-toolchain hashing/dedup this is fully deterministic; for cross-impl
10914// RFC 8785 signing, account for the two notes above.
10915
10916namespace json::detail {
10917// Transcode UTF-8 → UTF-16 code units, for RFC 8785 §3.2.3 key ordering (JCS
10918// sorts member names by UTF-16 code units, which differs from UTF-8/code-point
10919// order only for supplementary-plane characters — those use surrogate pairs).
10920inline ::std::u16string canon_utf8_to_utf16_(::std::string_view s) {
10921 ::std::u16string out;
10922 ::std::size_t i = 0;
10923 while (i < s.size()) {
10924 unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i]);
10925 uint32_t cp; int len;
10926 if (c < 0x80) { cp = c; len = 1; }
10927 else if ((c >> 5) == 0x6) { cp = c & 0x1F; len = 2; }
10928 else if ((c >> 4) == 0xE) { cp = c & 0x0F; len = 3; }
10929 else { cp = c & 0x07; len = 4; }
10930 for (int k = 1; k < len && i + static_cast<::std::size_t>(k) < s.size(); ++k)
10931 cp = (cp << 6) | (static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i + k]) & 0x3F);
10932 i += static_cast<::std::size_t>(len);
10933 if (cp < 0x10000) out += static_cast<char16_t>(cp);
10934 else {
10935 cp -= 0x10000;
10936 out += static_cast<char16_t>(0xD800 + (cp >> 10));
10937 out += static_cast<char16_t>(0xDC00 + (cp & 0x3FF));
10938 }
10939 }
10940 return out;
10941}
10942
10943// Format a double as RFC 8785 / ECMAScript Number::toString (shortest round-trip,
10944// with the ECMAScript exponent rules: 'e+NN' / 'e-NN', integers without a point).
10945inline ::std::string canon_number_(double d) {
10946 if (d == 0.0) return "0";
10947 ::std::string s = to_json_str(d); // shortest decimal (Schubfach), maybe with E/.
10948 bool neg = false; ::std::size_t i = 0;
10949 if (!s.empty() && s[0] == '-') { neg = true; i = 1; }
10950 ::std::size_t ep = s.find_first_of("eE", i);
10951 ::std::string mant = (ep == ::std::string::npos) ? s.substr(i) : s.substr(i, ep - i);
10952 int exp10 = (ep == ::std::string::npos) ? 0 : ::std::atoi(s.c_str() + ep + 1);
10953 ::std::size_t dot = mant.find('.');
10954 ::std::string ipart = (dot == ::std::string::npos) ? mant : mant.substr(0, dot);
10955 ::std::string fpart = (dot == ::std::string::npos) ? ::std::string() : mant.substr(dot + 1);
10956 ::std::string digits = ipart + fpart;
10957 int point = static_cast<int>(ipart.size()) + exp10; // decimal point pos in `digits`
10958 ::std::size_t lead = 0;
10959 while (lead + 1 < digits.size() && digits[lead] == '0') { ++lead; --point; }
10960 digits.erase(0, lead);
10961 ::std::size_t tlen = digits.size();
10962 while (tlen > 1 && digits[tlen - 1] == '0') --tlen;
10963 digits.resize(tlen);
10964 const int k = static_cast<int>(digits.size());
10965 const int n = point;
10966 ::std::string out;
10967 if (neg) out += '-';
10968 if (k <= n && n <= 21) { out += digits; out.append(static_cast<::std::size_t>(n - k), '0'); }
10969 else if (0 < n && n <= 21) { out += digits.substr(0, static_cast<::std::size_t>(n)); out += '.'; out += digits.substr(static_cast<::std::size_t>(n)); }
10970 else if (-6 < n && n <= 0) { out += "0."; out.append(static_cast<::std::size_t>(-n), '0'); out += digits; }
10971 else {
10972 out += digits[0];
10973 if (k > 1) { out += '.'; out += digits.substr(1); }
10974 out += 'e';
10975 int e = n - 1;
10976 out += (e >= 0) ? '+' : '-';
10977 out += ::std::to_string(e >= 0 ? e : -e);
10978 }
10979 return out;
10980}
10981
10982inline void canon_emit_(const json::Value &v, ::std::string &out) {
10983 if (v.is_object()) {
10984 ::std::vector<::std::pair<::std::u16string, ::std::pair<::std::string, json::Value>>> items;
10985 for (const auto &[k, val] : v.items()) {
10986 ::std::string dk = ::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(k);
10987 // Transcode BEFORE moving dk — argument evaluation order is unspecified, so
10988 // computing the UTF-16 sort key and std::move(dk) in one call would risk
10989 // transcoding a moved-from (empty) string.
10990 ::std::u16string u16 = canon_utf8_to_utf16_(dk);
10991 items.emplace_back(::std::move(u16), ::std::make_pair(::std::move(dk), val));
10992 }
10993 ::std::sort(items.begin(), items.end(),
10994 [](const auto &a, const auto &b) { return a.first < b.first; });
10995 out += '{';
10996 for (::std::size_t i = 0; i < items.size(); ++i) {
10997 if (i) out += ',';
10998 out += to_json_str(items[i].second.first); // canonical (minimal) key escaping
10999 out += ':';
11000 canon_emit_(items[i].second.second, out);
11001 }
11002 out += '}';
11003 } else if (v.is_array()) {
11004 out += '[';
11005 bool first = true;
11006 for (const auto &e : v.elements()) {
11007 if (!first) out += ',';
11008 first = false;
11009 canon_emit_(e, out);
11010 }
11011 out += ']';
11012 } else if (v.is_string()) {
11013 out += to_json_str(v.decoded()); // decode then re-escape minimally
11014 } else if (v.is_bool()) {
11015 out += v.as<bool>() ? "true" : "false";
11016 } else if (v.is_int()) {
11017 out += to_json_str(v.as<int64_t>());
11018 } else if (v.is_double()) {
11019 out += canon_number_(v.as<double>()); // RFC 8785 / ECMAScript Number::toString
11020 } else {
11021 out += "null";
11022 }
11023}
11024} // namespace json::detail
11025
11026// Parse `json` and return its canonical form. Uses STRICT parsing (RFC 8259 +
11027// well-formed UTF-8) — a canonical form is only meaningful for valid input, and
11028// the signing/hashing use case must reject malformed data rather than silently
11029// canonicalize a best-effort interpretation. Throws qbuem::parse_error otherwise.
11030// canonicalize_to(buf, json) — APPEND the canonical form of `json` to `buf`,
11031// reusing its existing capacity (the caller owns the buffer). Same strict parsing
11032// and output as canonicalize(); throws qbuem::parse_error on malformed input.
11033inline void canonicalize_to(::std::string &buf, ::std::string_view json) {
11034 Document doc;
11035 Value root = parse_strict(doc, json);
11036 buf.reserve(buf.size() + json.size());
11037 json::detail::canon_emit_(root, buf);
11038}
11039[[nodiscard]] inline ::std::string canonicalize(::std::string_view json) {
11040 ::std::string out;
11041 canonicalize_to(out, json);
11042 return out;
11043}
11044
11045// ── SAX-style event visitor ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
11046// qbuem::visit(value, handler) walks a parsed Value depth-first and emits an
11047// event for each node to `handler`, so you can transcode / inspect / fold JSON
11048// without navigating the DOM by hand. This is an event walk over the (proven,
11049// fuzzed) tape parser — not a separate streaming parser; for data larger than
11050// RAM use NDJSON (read_lines).
11051//
11052// Derive a handler from qbuem::sax_handler and override only the events you care
11053// about; the rest default to no-ops. Dispatch is static (no virtuals → zero
11054// overhead). Every handler method returns bool — return false to ABORT the walk
11055// early (visit then returns false). String/key values are the RAW on-the-wire
11056// slice (escaped, zero-copy), matching Value::as<std::string_view>(); decode with
11057// the value's own escapes if you need the logical text.
11058struct sax_handler {
11059 bool start_object() { return true; }
11060 bool end_object(::std::size_t /*member_count*/) { return true; }
11061 bool start_array() { return true; }
11062 bool end_array(::std::size_t /*element_count*/) { return true; }
11063 bool key(::std::string_view /*raw*/) { return true; }
11064 bool string(::std::string_view /*raw*/) { return true; }
11065 bool integer(int64_t) { return true; }
11066 bool real(double) { return true; }
11067 bool boolean(bool) { return true; }
11068 bool null() { return true; }
11069};
11070
11071// Walk `v`, dispatching events to `h`. Returns false iff a handler aborted.
11072// Recursion depth is bounded: `v` comes from the tape parser, which rejects input
11073// nested deeper than kMaxDepth (1024), so this walk cannot overflow the stack on
11074// adversarial input — the depth cap is enforced at parse time, not here.
11075template <typename H>
11076bool visit(const Value &v, H &h) {
11077 if (v.is_object()) {
11078 if (!h.start_object()) return false;
11079 ::std::size_t n = 0;
11080 for (const auto &[k, val] : v.items()) {
11081 if (!h.key(k)) return false;
11082 if (!visit(val, h)) return false;
11083 ++n;
11084 }
11085 return h.end_object(n);
11086 } else if (v.is_array()) {
11087 if (!h.start_array()) return false;
11088 ::std::size_t n = 0;
11089 for (const auto &e : v.elements()) {
11090 if (!visit(e, h)) return false;
11091 ++n;
11092 }
11093 return h.end_array(n);
11094 } else if (v.is_string()) {
11095 return h.string(v.template as<::std::string_view>());
11096 } else if (v.is_int()) {
11097 return h.integer(v.template as<int64_t>());
11098 } else if (v.is_double()) {
11099 return h.real(v.template as<double>());
11100 } else if (v.is_bool()) {
11101 return h.boolean(v.template as<bool>());
11102 } else {
11103 return h.null();
11104 }
11105}
11106
11107// Parse `json` then visit it — the "stream events from text" one-liner. Throws
11108// qbuem::parse_error on invalid input. Returns false iff a handler aborted.
11109template <typename H>
11110bool sax_parse(::std::string_view json, H &h) {
11111 Document doc;
11112 Value root = parse(doc, json);
11113 return visit(root, h);
11114}
11115
11116// ── RFC 6902 JSON Patch — functional applier + diff generation ───────────────
11117// qbuem::apply_patch(doc, patch) applies a JSON Patch and returns the new
11118// document as a string; qbuem::diff(from, to) computes the patch that takes one
11119// to the other. Unlike the in-place Value::patch() (overlay-based), this applier
11120// is purely functional — each op parses the current document and rebuilds it with
11121// the edit applied, so multi-op patches, array-index removal, pointer-token
11122// unescaping, and whole-document replacement all behave correctly.
11123
11124namespace json::detail {
11125
11126inline bool value_equal(const Value &a, const Value &b); // defined below (diff)
11127
11128inline void p6902_push_(::std::string &out, bool &first, ::std::string_view j) {
11129 if (!first) out += ',';
11130 first = false;
11131 out.append(j);
11132}
11133
11134// Split a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into decoded reference tokens.
11135inline ::std::vector<::std::string> p6902_tokens_(::std::string_view path) {
11136 ::std::vector<::std::string> toks;
11137 if (path.empty()) return toks; // whole document
11138 ::std::size_t i = (path[0] == '/') ? 1 : 0;
11139 ::std::string cur;
11140 for (; i <= path.size(); ++i) {
11141 if (i == path.size() || path[i] == '/') {
11142 toks.push_back(cur);
11143 cur.clear();
11144 } else if (path[i] == '~' && i + 1 < path.size()) {
11145 cur += (path[i + 1] == '0') ? '~' : (path[i + 1] == '1' ? '/' : path[i + 1]);
11146 ++i;
11147 } else {
11148 cur += path[i];
11149 }
11150 }
11151 return toks;
11152}
11153
11154// op: 0=add, 1=remove, 2=replace. Rebuild `v` to JSON with the node at
11155// tokens[ti..] edited; `nv` is the new value's JSON (for add/replace). Returns
11156// nullopt if the path does not resolve (RFC 6902 failure).
11157inline ::std::optional<::std::string>
11158p6902_edit_(const Value &v, const ::std::vector<::std::string> &toks,
11159 ::std::size_t ti, int op, ::std::string_view nv) {
11160 if (ti == toks.size()) {
11161 if (op == 1) return ::std::nullopt; // remove whole document — unsupported
11162 return ::std::string(nv); // add/replace whole document
11163 }
11164 const ::std::string &tok = toks[ti];
11165 const bool last = (ti + 1 == toks.size());
11166 if (v.is_object()) {
11167 ::std::string out = "{";
11168 bool first = true, found = false;
11169 for (const auto &[rawk, child] : v.items()) {
11170 if (::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(rawk) == tok) {
11171 found = true;
11172 if (last && op == 1) continue; // remove: drop this member
11173 ::std::string mv;
11174 if (last) {
11175 mv.assign(nv); // add/replace existing key
11176 } else {
11177 auto sub = p6902_edit_(child, toks, ti + 1, op, nv);
11178 if (!sub) return ::std::nullopt;
11179 mv = ::std::move(*sub);
11180 }
11181 if (!first) out += ',';
11182 first = false;
11183 out += '"';
11184 out.append(rawk);
11185 out += "\":";
11186 out += mv;
11187 } else {
11188 if (!first) out += ',';
11189 first = false;
11190 out += '"';
11191 out.append(rawk);
11192 out += "\":";
11193 out += child.dump();
11194 }
11195 }
11196 if (last && op == 0 && !found) { // add a new member
11197 if (!first) out += ',';
11198 first = false;
11199 out += to_json_str(tok);
11200 out += ':';
11201 out.append(nv);
11202 found = true;
11203 }
11204 if (!found) return ::std::nullopt; // replace/remove on a missing key, or
11205 // descend into a missing parent
11206 out += '}';
11207 return out;
11208 }
11209 if (v.is_array()) {
11210 const ::std::size_t n = v.size();
11211 const bool dash = (tok == "-");
11212 ::std::size_t idx = 0;
11213 if (!dash) {
11214 const char *b = tok.data(), *e = b + tok.size();
11215 auto [p, ec] = ::std::from_chars(b, e, idx);
11216 if (ec != ::std::errc{} || p != e) return ::std::nullopt;
11217 }
11218 ::std::string out = "[";
11219 bool first = true;
11220 if (!last) {
11221 if (dash || idx >= n) return ::std::nullopt;
11222 for (::std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
11223 if (i == idx) {
11224 auto sub = p6902_edit_(v[i], toks, ti + 1, op, nv);
11225 if (!sub) return ::std::nullopt;
11226 p6902_push_(out, first, *sub);
11227 } else {
11228 p6902_push_(out, first, v[i].dump());
11229 }
11230 }
11231 } else if (op == 0) { // add/insert
11232 const ::std::size_t at = dash ? n : idx;
11233 if (at > n) return ::std::nullopt;
11234 for (::std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
11235 if (i == at) p6902_push_(out, first, nv);
11236 p6902_push_(out, first, v[i].dump());
11237 }
11238 if (at == n) p6902_push_(out, first, nv);
11239 } else { // remove / replace at index
11240 if (dash || idx >= n) return ::std::nullopt;
11241 for (::std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
11242 if (i == idx) {
11243 if (op == 1) continue; // remove
11244 p6902_push_(out, first, nv); // replace
11245 } else {
11246 p6902_push_(out, first, v[i].dump());
11247 }
11248 }
11249 }
11250 out += ']';
11251 return out;
11252 }
11253 return ::std::nullopt; // cannot descend into a scalar
11254}
11255
11256// Read the JSON of the value at `path` in already-parsed `root` (for move/copy/
11257// test sources). nullopt if absent.
11258inline ::std::optional<::std::string>
11259p6902_value_at_(const Value &root, ::std::string_view path) {
11260 Value v = root;
11261 for (const auto &tok : p6902_tokens_(path)) {
11262 if (v.is_object()) {
11263 auto m = v.find(tok); // NB: matches raw key bytes
11264 if (!m) {
11265 // fall back to a decoded-key scan for escaped keys
11266 bool hit = false;
11267 for (const auto &[rk, cv] : v.items())
11268 if (::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(rk) == tok) { v = cv; hit = true; break; }
11269 if (!hit) return ::std::nullopt;
11270 } else {
11271 v = *m;
11272 }
11273 } else if (v.is_array()) {
11274 ::std::size_t idx = 0;
11275 const char *b = tok.data(), *e = b + tok.size();
11276 auto [p, ec] = ::std::from_chars(b, e, idx);
11277 if (ec != ::std::errc{} || p != e || idx >= v.size()) return ::std::nullopt;
11278 v = v[idx];
11279 } else {
11280 return ::std::nullopt;
11281 }
11282 }
11283 return v.dump();
11284}
11285
11286// Apply one RFC 6902 op to `doc_json`, returning the new document JSON.
11287inline ::std::optional<::std::string>
11288p6902_apply_one_(::std::string_view doc_json, const Value &op_obj) {
11289 if (!op_obj.is_object()) return ::std::nullopt;
11290 const ::std::string op = op_obj["op"] | "";
11291 const ::std::string path = op_obj["path"] | "";
11292 if (op.empty() || (!path.empty() && path[0] != '/')) return ::std::nullopt;
11293 Document doc;
11294 Value root = ::qbuem::parse(doc, doc_json);
11295 const auto toks = p6902_tokens_(path);
11296 if (op == "add" || op == "replace") {
11297 Value val = op_obj["value"];
11298 if (!val.is_valid()) return ::std::nullopt;
11299 return p6902_edit_(root, toks, 0, op == "add" ? 0 : 2, val.dump());
11300 }
11301 if (op == "remove") {
11302 return p6902_edit_(root, toks, 0, 1, "");
11303 }
11304 if (op == "copy" || op == "move") {
11305 const ::std::string from = op_obj["from"] | "";
11306 if (from.empty() && (op_obj["from"] | "x") == "x") return ::std::nullopt;
11307 auto src = p6902_value_at_(root, from);
11308 if (!src) return ::std::nullopt;
11309 if (op == "move") {
11310 auto removed = p6902_edit_(root, p6902_tokens_(from), 0, 1, "");
11311 if (!removed) return ::std::nullopt;
11312 Document d2;
11313 Value r2 = ::qbuem::parse(d2, *removed);
11314 return p6902_edit_(r2, toks, 0, 0, *src);
11315 }
11316 return p6902_edit_(root, toks, 0, 0, *src);
11317 }
11318 if (op == "test") {
11319 Value val = op_obj["value"];
11320 auto cur = p6902_value_at_(root, path);
11321 if (!cur || !val.is_valid()) return ::std::nullopt;
11322 Document da, db;
11323 Value a = ::qbuem::parse(da, *cur);
11324 if (!value_equal(a, val)) return ::std::nullopt;
11325 return ::std::string(doc_json); // test passes — document unchanged
11326 }
11327 return ::std::nullopt; // unknown op
11328}
11329} // namespace json::detail
11330
11331// Apply a whole RFC 6902 patch to `doc_json`. Throws qbuem::parse_error on
11332// malformed JSON; throws std::runtime_error if any op fails (per RFC 6902, a
11333// patch is all-or-nothing).
11334//
11335// Complexity: O(ops × docsize) — the functional applier reparses and rebuilds
11336// the whole document once per op, so a P-op patch over an N-byte document is
11337// O(P·N). This trades speed for correctness (multi-op patches, array-index
11338// removal, and pointer unescaping all round-trip); for a one-shot edit of a huge
11339// document, prefer the in-place Value::patch().
11340//
11341// apply_patch_to(buf, doc, patch) APPENDS the patched document to `buf` (the
11342// caller owns the buffer); apply_patch() is the convenience that returns a fresh
11343// string.
11344inline void apply_patch_to(::std::string &buf, ::std::string_view doc_json,
11345 ::std::string_view patch_json) {
11346 Document pdoc;
11347 Value patch = parse(pdoc, patch_json);
11348 if (!patch.is_array())
11349 throw ::std::runtime_error("apply_patch: patch must be a JSON array");
11350 ::std::string cur(doc_json);
11351 for (const Value &op : patch.elements()) {
11352 auto next = json::detail::p6902_apply_one_(cur, op);
11353 if (!next)
11354 throw ::std::runtime_error("apply_patch: operation failed (bad path or op)");
11355 cur = ::std::move(*next); // settle: the next op sees this op's effect
11356 }
11357 buf += cur;
11358}
11359[[nodiscard]] inline ::std::string apply_patch(::std::string_view doc_json,
11360 ::std::string_view patch_json) {
11361 ::std::string out;
11362 apply_patch_to(out, doc_json, patch_json);
11363 return out;
11364}
11365
11366// ── JSON diff (RFC 6902 patch generation) ────────────────────────────────────
11367// qbuem::diff(from, to) computes a JSON Patch (RFC 6902) that, applied to `from`,
11368// yields `to` — for sending only the delta (real-time state sync). The inverse of
11369// apply_patch. Numbers compare by value (1 == 1.0), strings by decoded text.
11370// Arrays diff element-wise (a length decrease emits one whole-array replace).
11371
11372// Deep value equality: numbers by numeric value, strings by decoded text.
11373// Find a member of `obj` whose key equals the (decoded) `raw_key`. Fast path is
11374// a raw byte match (the common case — both docs escape keys the same way); the
11375// slow path compares decoded keys so two spellings of the same key (e.g. "a" vs
11376// "a") are treated as equal.
11377namespace json::detail {
11378inline ::std::optional<Value> find_by_decoded_key_(const Value &obj,
11379 ::std::string_view raw_key) {
11380 if (auto m = obj.find(raw_key)) return m;
11381 const ::std::string want = ::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(raw_key);
11382 for (const auto &[rk, v] : obj.items())
11383 if (::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(rk) == want) return v;
11384 return ::std::nullopt;
11385}
11386
11387inline bool value_equal(const Value &a, const Value &b) {
11388 if (a.is_object() && b.is_object()) {
11389 ::std::size_t na = 0, nb = 0;
11390 for (const auto &[k, va] : a.items()) {
11391 ++na;
11392 auto ob = find_by_decoded_key_(b, k);
11393 if (!ob || !value_equal(va, *ob)) return false;
11394 }
11395 for (const auto &kv : b.items()) { (void)kv; ++nb; }
11396 return na == nb;
11397 }
11398 if (a.is_array() && b.is_array()) {
11399 if (a.size() != b.size()) return false;
11400 for (::std::size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i)
11401 if (!value_equal(a[i], b[i])) return false;
11402 return true;
11403 }
11404 if (a.is_string() && b.is_string()) return a.decoded() == b.decoded();
11405 // Integers compare exactly (a double compare would equate e.g. 2^53 and
11406 // 2^53+1); only mixed/real numbers fall back to a double compare so 1 == 1.0.
11407 if (a.is_int() && b.is_int())
11408 return a.template as<int64_t>() == b.template as<int64_t>();
11409 if (a.is_number() && b.is_number())
11410 return a.template as<double>() == b.template as<double>();
11411 if (a.is_bool() && b.is_bool())
11412 return a.template as<bool>() == b.template as<bool>();
11413 if (a.is_null() && b.is_null()) return true;
11414 return false; // differing type
11415}
11416
11417inline ::std::string diff_jptr_escape_(::std::string_view k) {
11418 ::std::string s;
11419 s.reserve(k.size());
11420 for (char c : k) {
11421 if (c == '~') s += "~0";
11422 else if (c == '/') s += "~1";
11423 else s += c;
11424 }
11425 return s;
11426}
11427inline void diff_op_(::std::string &out, bool &first, const char *op,
11428 const ::std::string &path) {
11429 if (!first) out += ',';
11430 first = false;
11431 out += R"({"op":")";
11432 out += op;
11433 out += R"(","path":)";
11434 out += to_json_str(path);
11435 out += '}';
11436}
11437inline void diff_op_value_(::std::string &out, bool &first, const char *op,
11438 const ::std::string &path, const Value &v) {
11439 if (!first) out += ',';
11440 first = false;
11441 out += R"({"op":")";
11442 out += op;
11443 out += R"(","path":)";
11444 out += to_json_str(path);
11445 out += R"(,"value":)";
11446 out += v.dump();
11447 out += '}';
11448}
11449inline void diff_emit_(const Value &from, const Value &to,
11450 const ::std::string &path, ::std::string &out,
11451 bool &first) {
11452 if (value_equal(from, to)) return;
11453 if (from.is_object() && to.is_object()) {
11454 for (const auto &[k, fv] : from.items()) {
11455 (void)fv;
11456 if (!find_by_decoded_key_(to, k)) // key removed (match by decoded name)
11457 diff_op_(out, first, "remove",
11458 path + "/" +
11459 diff_jptr_escape_(::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(k)));
11460 }
11461 for (const auto &[k, tv] : to.items()) {
11462 const ::std::string p =
11463 path + "/" + diff_jptr_escape_(::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(k));
11464 auto fv = find_by_decoded_key_(from, k);
11465 if (!fv) diff_op_value_(out, first, "add", p, tv);
11466 else diff_emit_(*fv, tv, p, out, first);
11467 }
11468 } else if (from.is_array() && to.is_array()) {
11469 const ::std::size_t la = from.size(), lb = to.size();
11470 if (lb < la) {
11471 diff_op_value_(out, first, "replace", path, to); // shrink → whole-array
11472 } else {
11473 for (::std::size_t i = 0; i < la; ++i)
11474 diff_emit_(from[i], to[i], path + "/" + ::std::to_string(i), out, first);
11475 for (::std::size_t i = la; i < lb; ++i)
11476 diff_op_value_(out, first, "add", path + "/-", to[i]);
11477 }
11478 } else {
11479 diff_op_value_(out, first, "replace", path, to);
11480 }
11481}
11482} // namespace json::detail
11483
11484// diff_to(buf, from, to) — APPEND the RFC 6902 patch (a JSON array) taking
11485// parsed `from` to `to` onto `buf`, reusing its capacity (the caller owns the
11486// buffer). diff() is the convenience that returns a fresh string.
11487inline void diff_to(::std::string &buf, const Value &from, const Value &to) {
11488 buf += '[';
11489 bool first = true;
11490 json::detail::diff_emit_(from, to, ::std::string(), buf, first);
11491 buf += ']';
11492}
11493// Parse both JSON strings, then diff them onto `buf`. Throws on invalid input.
11494inline void diff_to(::std::string &buf, ::std::string_view from_json,
11495 ::std::string_view to_json) {
11496 Document fdoc, tdoc;
11497 Value f = parse(fdoc, from_json);
11498 Value t = parse(tdoc, to_json);
11499 diff_to(buf, f, t);
11500}
11501// Returns an RFC 6902 patch (JSON array string) taking parsed `from` to `to`.
11502[[nodiscard]] inline ::std::string diff(const Value &from, const Value &to) {
11503 ::std::string out;
11504 diff_to(out, from, to);
11505 return out;
11506}
11507// Parse both JSON strings and diff them. Throws on invalid input.
11508[[nodiscard]] inline ::std::string diff(::std::string_view from_json,
11509 ::std::string_view to_json) {
11510 ::std::string out;
11511 diff_to(out, from_json, to_json);
11512 return out;
11513}
11514
11515// ── JSONPath (RFC 9535) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
11516// qbuem::query(root, "$.store.book[?@.price<10].title") returns every Value the
11517// query selects, in document order. Supported:
11518// - segments: root `$`, member access (`.name` / `['name']` / `["name"]`),
11519// array index incl. negative (`[0]`, `[-1]`), wildcard (`.*` / `[*]`),
11520// recursive descent (`..`), slices (`[start:end:step]`), unions
11521// (`[0, 2, 'k']`).
11522// - filter selectors `[?<expr>]` (RFC 9535 §2.3.5): comparisons (`==` `!=` `<`
11523// `<=` `>` `>=`), existence tests (a bare relative/absolute query is true iff
11524// it selects ≥1 node), the logical operators `&&` `||` `!` with parentheses,
11525// literals (numbers, `'...'`/`"..."` strings, `true`, `false`, `null`),
11526// singular queries (`@.a.b`, `$.x[0]`) as comparison operands, and the
11527// non-regex functions `length()`, `count()`, `value()`.
11528//
11529// NOT supported, by design: the I-Regexp functions `match()` and `search()` —
11530// they require a regular-expression engine, which has no place in a single-header
11531// zero-dependency library; a query using either throws qbuem::parse_error. Pre-
11532// filter with your own regex if you need them.
11533//
11534// A syntactically malformed query throws qbuem::parse_error; a valid query that
11535// matches nothing returns an empty vector. Returned Values view into the same
11536// document as `root`, so that document must outlive them.
11537namespace json::detail::jsonpath {
11538
11539struct FilterExpr; // filter-expression AST root (shared_ptr-referenced)
11540struct JpSegment; // a path segment (referenced from a filter-query)
11541
11542struct JpSelector {
11543 enum class Kind { Name, Wildcard, Index, Slice, Filter };
11544 Kind kind;
11545 ::std::string name; // Kind::Name
11546 int64_t index = 0; // Kind::Index
11547 int64_t s_start = 0, s_end = 0, s_step = 1; // Kind::Slice
11548 bool has_start = false, has_end = false;
11549 ::std::shared_ptr<FilterExpr> filter; // Kind::Filter
11550};
11551struct JpSegment {
11552 bool descendant = false; // leading `..`
11553 ::std::vector<JpSelector> selectors; // union of ≥1
11554};
11555
11556// ── Filter-expression AST (RFC 9535 §2.3.5) ──────────────────────────────────
11557// Singular query (`@`/`$` + only name/index steps): selects ≤1 node, usable as a
11558// comparison operand.
11559struct SingularQuery {
11560 bool from_root = false; // `$` vs `@`
11561 struct Step { bool is_index; ::std::string name; int64_t index; };
11562 ::std::vector<Step> steps;
11563};
11564// Filter query (`@`/`$` + arbitrary segments): used in existence tests and as the
11565// argument to count()/value(); may select any number of nodes.
11566struct FilterQuery {
11567 bool from_root = false;
11568 ::std::vector<JpSegment> segs;
11569};
11570// A comparison operand or function argument.
11571struct Comparable {
11572 enum class T { Null, Bool, Int, Dbl, Str, Singular, Length, Count, Value } t;
11573 bool b = false;
11574 int64_t i = 0;
11575 double d = 0;
11576 ::std::string s; // Str literal
11577 ::std::shared_ptr<SingularQuery> sq; // Singular
11578 ::std::shared_ptr<Comparable> len_arg; // Length(arg)
11579 ::std::shared_ptr<FilterQuery> fq; // Count(query) / Value(query)
11580};
11581// A logical-expression node.
11582struct FilterExpr {
11583 enum class T { Or, And, Not, Cmp, Exists } t;
11584 ::std::vector<FilterExpr> kids; // Or/And operands, or Not's one child
11585 Comparable lhs, rhs; // Cmp
11586 int op = 0; // Cmp op: 0..5 == != < <= > >=
11587 ::std::shared_ptr<FilterQuery> exists; // Exists
11588};
11589
11590struct JpParser {
11591 const char *p;
11592 const char *begin;
11593 const char *end;
11594 size_t fdepth = 0; // filter-expression recursion depth (DoS guard)
11595
11596 // Every level of filter nesting (parentheses, `!`, and nested `[?...]`) passes
11597 // through parse_unary exactly once; cap the depth so a pathologically nested
11598 // query string can't overflow the stack (mirrors the tape parser's kMaxDepth).
11599 static constexpr size_t kFilterMaxDepth = 512;
11600 struct DepthGuard {
11601 size_t &d;
11602 explicit DepthGuard(size_t &x) : d(x) { ++d; }
11603 ~DepthGuard() { --d; }
11604 };
11605
11606 [[noreturn]] void fail(const char *msg) const {
11607 ::qbuem::json::throw_parse_error(
11608 msg, p, ::std::string_view(begin, static_cast<size_t>(end - begin)));
11609 }
11610 void ws() { while (p < end && (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t' || *p == '\n' || *p == '\r')) ++p; }
11611
11612 // Parse a quoted name selector ('...' or "...") per RFC 9535 §2.3.1.1: the JSON
11613 // string grammar including \uXXXX (and surrogate pairs). Returns the decoded
11614 // UTF-8 name. Rejects unescaped control characters, invalid escapes, and a
11615 // backslash-escaped non-matching quote (\" is only legal inside "...", \' only
11616 // inside '...').
11617 ::std::string parse_quoted(char q) {
11618 ::std::string out;
11619 ++p; // opening quote
11620 auto hex4 = [&]() -> uint32_t {
11621 uint32_t v = 0;
11622 for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
11623 if (p >= end) fail("JSONPath: unterminated \\u escape");
11624 char h = *p++;
11625 uint32_t d;
11626 if (h >= '0' && h <= '9') d = static_cast<uint32_t>(h - '0');
11627 else if (h >= 'a' && h <= 'f') d = static_cast<uint32_t>(h - 'a' + 10);
11628 else if (h >= 'A' && h <= 'F') d = static_cast<uint32_t>(h - 'A' + 10);
11629 else { fail("JSONPath: invalid hex digit in \\u escape"); }
11630 v = (v << 4) | d;
11631 }
11632 return v;
11633 };
11634 auto emit_cp = [&](uint32_t cp) {
11635 if (cp <= 0x7F) out += static_cast<char>(cp);
11636 else if (cp <= 0x7FF) {
11637 out += static_cast<char>(0xC0 | (cp >> 6));
11638 out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));
11639 } else if (cp <= 0xFFFF) {
11640 out += static_cast<char>(0xE0 | (cp >> 12));
11641 out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F));
11642 out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));
11643 } else {
11644 out += static_cast<char>(0xF0 | (cp >> 18));
11645 out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F));
11646 out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F));
11647 out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));
11648 }
11649 };
11650 while (p < end && *p != q) {
11651 unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(*p++);
11652 if (c == '\\') {
11653 if (p >= end) fail("JSONPath: unterminated escape");
11654 char e = *p++;
11655 switch (e) {
11656 case 'b': out += '\b'; break;
11657 case 'f': out += '\f'; break;
11658 case 'n': out += '\n'; break;
11659 case 'r': out += '\r'; break;
11660 case 't': out += '\t'; break;
11661 case '/': out += '/'; break;
11662 case '\\': out += '\\'; break;
11663 case 'u': {
11664 uint32_t cp = hex4();
11665 if (cp >= 0xD800 && cp <= 0xDBFF) { // high surrogate: a low MUST follow
11666 if (!(p + 1 < end && p[0] == '\\' && p[1] == 'u'))
11667 fail("JSONPath: lone high surrogate in \\u escape");
11668 p += 2;
11669 uint32_t lo = hex4();
11670 if (lo < 0xDC00 || lo > 0xDFFF)
11671 fail("JSONPath: high surrogate not followed by a low surrogate");
11672 cp = 0x10000 + ((cp - 0xD800) << 10) + (lo - 0xDC00);
11673 } else if (cp >= 0xDC00 && cp <= 0xDFFF) {
11674 fail("JSONPath: lone low surrogate in \\u escape");
11675 }
11676 emit_cp(cp);
11677 break;
11678 }
11679 default:
11680 if (e == q) out += q; // \" inside "...", or \' inside '...'
11681 else fail("JSONPath: invalid escape in string selector");
11682 break;
11683 }
11684 } else if (c <= 0x1F) {
11685 fail("JSONPath: unescaped control character in string selector");
11686 } else {
11687 out += static_cast<char>(c);
11688 }
11689 }
11690 if (p >= end) fail("JSONPath: unterminated string");
11691 ++p; // closing quote
11692 return out;
11693 }
11694
11695 // Parse an optionally-signed integer; returns it and whether any digit was read.
11696 // RFC 9535 §2.3.3/§2.3.4 `int`: optional '-' then a single 0 or a non-zero
11697 // leading digit run. No '+', no leading zeros, no '-0'. The value must be in
11698 // the I-JSON range ±(2^53 − 1). Returns false (without consuming) otherwise.
11699 bool parse_int(int64_t &out) {
11700 ws();
11701 const char *s = p;
11702 const bool neg = (p < end && *p == '-');
11703 if (neg) ++p;
11704 if (p >= end || *p < '0' || *p > '9') { p = s; return false; } // need a digit
11705 const char *num = p;
11706 if (*p == '0') {
11707 ++p;
11708 if (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') { p = s; return false; } // "01"
11709 if (neg) { p = s; return false; } // "-0"
11710 } else {
11711 while (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') ++p;
11712 }
11713 int64_t mag;
11714 auto [ptr, ec] = ::std::from_chars(num, p, mag);
11715 (void)ptr;
11716 if (ec != ::std::errc{}) { p = s; return false; } // overflow
11717 constexpr int64_t kMax = 9007199254740991LL; // 2^53 − 1
11718 if (mag > kMax) { p = s; return false; }
11719 out = neg ? -mag : mag;
11720 return true;
11721 }
11722
11723 // Parse one selector inside `[...]` (already past `[`, positioned at selector).
11724 JpSelector parse_bracket_selector() {
11725 ws();
11726 if (p >= end) fail("JSONPath: unexpected end of selector");
11727 if (*p == '?') return parse_filter_selector();
11728 if (*p == '*') { ++p; return {JpSelector::Kind::Wildcard, {}, 0, 0, 0, 1, false, false, {}}; }
11729 if (*p == '\'' || *p == '"') {
11730 JpSelector s; s.kind = JpSelector::Kind::Name; s.name = parse_quoted(*p); return s;
11731 }
11732 // index or slice: [int] [: [int] [: [int]]]
11733 JpSelector s;
11734 int64_t a;
11735 bool has_a = parse_int(a);
11736 ws();
11737 if (p < end && *p == ':') {
11738 s.kind = JpSelector::Kind::Slice;
11739 s.has_start = has_a; if (has_a) s.s_start = a;
11740 ++p; // ':'
11741 int64_t b;
11742 if (parse_int(b)) { s.has_end = true; s.s_end = b; }
11743 ws();
11744 if (p < end && *p == ':') {
11745 ++p;
11746 int64_t st;
11747 if (parse_int(st)) s.s_step = st;
11748 }
11749 return s;
11750 }
11751 if (!has_a) fail("JSONPath: expected name, index, slice, or '*'");
11752 s.kind = JpSelector::Kind::Index; s.index = a; return s;
11753 }
11754
11755 // Parse exactly one segment (`.name` / `..name` / `[selectors]` / `.*` / `..*`)
11756 // if one starts at the current position; returns false (without consuming) if
11757 // the next token cannot begin a segment. Shared by parse() and filter-queries.
11758 bool parse_one_segment(JpSegment &seg) {
11759 ws();
11760 if (p >= end) return false;
11761 if (*p == '.' && p + 1 < end && p[1] == '.') {
11762 seg.descendant = true;
11763 p += 2;
11764 // `..` may be followed by a name, `*`, or `[selectors]`.
11765 if (p < end && *p == '[') {
11766 ++p;
11767 parse_bracket_list(seg);
11768 } else if (p < end && *p == '*') {
11769 ++p; seg.selectors.push_back({JpSelector::Kind::Wildcard, {}, 0, 0, 0, 1, false, false, {}});
11770 } else {
11771 JpSelector s; s.kind = JpSelector::Kind::Name; s.name = parse_member_name();
11772 if (s.name.empty()) fail("JSONPath: expected member name after '..'");
11773 seg.selectors.push_back(std::move(s));
11774 }
11775 return true;
11776 }
11777 if (*p == '.') {
11778 ++p;
11779 if (p < end && *p == '*') { ++p; seg.selectors.push_back({JpSelector::Kind::Wildcard, {}, 0, 0, 0, 1, false, false, {}}); }
11780 else {
11781 JpSelector s; s.kind = JpSelector::Kind::Name; s.name = parse_member_name();
11782 if (s.name.empty()) fail("JSONPath: expected member name after '.'");
11783 seg.selectors.push_back(std::move(s));
11784 }
11785 return true;
11786 }
11787 if (*p == '[') {
11788 ++p;
11789 parse_bracket_list(seg);
11790 return true;
11791 }
11792 return false;
11793 }
11794
11795 ::std::vector<JpSegment> parse() {
11796 ::std::vector<JpSegment> segs;
11797 // RFC 9535: a query has NO leading whitespace (whitespace is only allowed
11798 // *between* segments) and NO trailing whitespace.
11799 if (p >= end || *p != '$')
11800 fail("JSONPath: query must start with '$' (no leading whitespace)");
11801 ++p;
11802 while (true) {
11803 const char *ws_start = p;
11804 ws();
11805 if (p >= end) {
11806 if (p != ws_start) fail("JSONPath: trailing whitespace");
11807 break;
11808 }
11809 JpSegment seg;
11810 if (!parse_one_segment(seg)) fail("JSONPath: expected '.', '..', or '['");
11811 segs.push_back(std::move(seg));
11812 }
11813 return segs;
11814 }
11815
11816 // Parse a comma-separated selector list, consuming the closing `]`.
11817 void parse_bracket_list(JpSegment &seg) {
11818 while (true) {
11819 seg.selectors.push_back(parse_bracket_selector());
11820 ws();
11821 if (p < end && *p == ',') { ++p; continue; }
11822 if (p < end && *p == ']') { ++p; return; }
11823 fail("JSONPath: expected ',' or ']' in selector list");
11824 }
11825 }
11826
11827 // Dotted member name (unquoted): a run of name chars. Stops at structural and
11828 // filter-operator characters so `@.price<10` reads the name as `price`.
11829 ::std::string parse_member_name() {
11830 const char *s = p;
11831 // RFC 9535 member-name-shorthand name-first = ALPHA / "_" / non-ASCII (no
11832 // digit, no `*`, no operator). The remaining name-chars are read with a
11833 // lenient terminator set (so e.g. `content-type` works as an extension).
11834 if (p >= end) return {};
11835 unsigned char f0 = static_cast<unsigned char>(*p);
11836 if (!((f0 >= 'A' && f0 <= 'Z') || (f0 >= 'a' && f0 <= 'z') || f0 == '_' || f0 >= 0x80))
11837 return {};
11838 ++p;
11839 while (p < end) {
11840 char c = *p;
11841 if (c == '.' || c == '[' || c == ']' || c == ' ' || c == '\t' ||
11842 c == '\n' || c == '\r' || c == ',' || c == '=' || c == '!' ||
11843 c == '<' || c == '>' || c == '&' || c == '|' || c == '(' ||
11844 c == ')')
11845 break;
11846 ++p;
11847 }
11848 return ::std::string(s, static_cast<size_t>(p - s));
11849 }
11850
11851 // ── Filter-expression parsing (RFC 9535 §2.3.5) ────────────────────────────
11852 void expect_char(char ch, const char *msg) {
11853 ws();
11854 if (p >= end || *p != ch) fail(msg);
11855 ++p;
11856 }
11857
11858 // `[?<logical-expr>]` — the `?` is current; the closing `]` is left for the
11859 // surrounding bracket-list to consume.
11860 JpSelector parse_filter_selector() {
11861 ++p; // '?'
11862 JpSelector s;
11863 s.kind = JpSelector::Kind::Filter;
11864 s.filter = ::std::make_shared<FilterExpr>(parse_logical_or());
11865 return s;
11866 }
11867
11868 FilterExpr parse_logical_or() {
11869 FilterExpr first = parse_logical_and();
11870 ws();
11871 if (!(p + 1 < end && p[0] == '|' && p[1] == '|')) return first;
11872 FilterExpr node;
11873 node.t = FilterExpr::T::Or;
11874 node.kids.push_back(::std::move(first));
11875 while (p + 1 < end && p[0] == '|' && p[1] == '|') {
11876 p += 2;
11877 node.kids.push_back(parse_logical_and());
11878 ws();
11879 }
11880 return node;
11881 }
11882
11883 FilterExpr parse_logical_and() {
11884 FilterExpr first = parse_unary();
11885 ws();
11886 if (!(p + 1 < end && p[0] == '&' && p[1] == '&')) return first;
11887 FilterExpr node;
11888 node.t = FilterExpr::T::And;
11889 node.kids.push_back(::std::move(first));
11890 while (p + 1 < end && p[0] == '&' && p[1] == '&') {
11891 p += 2;
11892 node.kids.push_back(parse_unary());
11893 ws();
11894 }
11895 return node;
11896 }
11897
11898 FilterExpr parse_unary() {
11899 DepthGuard guard(fdepth);
11900 if (fdepth > kFilterMaxDepth) fail("JSONPath: filter expression nested too deeply");
11901 ws();
11902 if (p < end && *p == '!' && !(p + 1 < end && p[1] == '=')) {
11903 ++p;
11904 FilterExpr node;
11905 node.t = FilterExpr::T::Not;
11906 node.kids.push_back(parse_unary());
11907 return node;
11908 }
11909 return parse_primary();
11910 }
11911
11912 FilterExpr parse_primary() {
11913 ws();
11914 if (p >= end) fail("JSONPath: expected a filter expression");
11915 if (*p == '(') {
11916 ++p;
11917 FilterExpr e = parse_logical_or();
11918 expect_char(')', "JSONPath: expected ')' in filter expression");
11919 return e;
11920 }
11921 // A query (`@`/`$`) is either a singular-query comparison operand or a
11922 // filter-query existence test; everything else (literal/function) must be the
11923 // left operand of a comparison.
11924 if (*p == '@' || *p == '$') {
11925 FilterQuery fq = parse_filter_query();
11926 const int op = parse_comp_op();
11927 if (op < 0) { // existence test
11928 FilterExpr e;
11929 e.t = FilterExpr::T::Exists;
11930 e.exists = ::std::make_shared<FilterQuery>(::std::move(fq));
11931 return e;
11932 }
11933 FilterExpr e;
11934 e.t = FilterExpr::T::Cmp;
11935 e.op = op;
11936 if (!filter_query_to_singular(fq, e.lhs))
11937 fail("JSONPath: left side of a comparison must be a singular query");
11938 e.rhs = parse_comparable();
11939 return e;
11940 }
11941 Comparable lhs = parse_comparable();
11942 const int op = parse_comp_op();
11943 if (op < 0)
11944 fail("JSONPath: expected a comparison operator (a bare literal is not a "
11945 "valid filter test)");
11946 FilterExpr e;
11947 e.t = FilterExpr::T::Cmp;
11948 e.op = op;
11949 e.lhs = ::std::move(lhs);
11950 e.rhs = parse_comparable();
11951 return e;
11952 }
11953
11954 // Comparison operator → 0..5 (== != < <= > >=), or -1 if none is present.
11955 int parse_comp_op() {
11956 ws();
11957 if (p + 1 < end) {
11958 if (p[0] == '=' && p[1] == '=') { p += 2; return 0; }
11959 if (p[0] == '!' && p[1] == '=') { p += 2; return 1; }
11960 if (p[0] == '<' && p[1] == '=') { p += 2; return 3; }
11961 if (p[0] == '>' && p[1] == '=') { p += 2; return 5; }
11962 }
11963 if (p < end && *p == '<') { ++p; return 2; }
11964 if (p < end && *p == '>') { ++p; return 4; }
11965 return -1;
11966 }
11967
11968 Comparable parse_comparable() {
11969 ws();
11970 if (p >= end) fail("JSONPath: expected a value in filter expression");
11971 const char c = *p;
11972 if (c == '@' || c == '$') {
11973 Comparable cv;
11974 cv.t = Comparable::T::Singular;
11975 cv.sq = ::std::make_shared<SingularQuery>(parse_singular_query());
11976 return cv;
11977 }
11978 if (c == '\'' || c == '"') {
11979 Comparable cv;
11980 cv.t = Comparable::T::Str;
11981 cv.s = parse_quoted(c);
11982 return cv;
11983 }
11984 if (c == '-' || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')) return parse_number_comparable();
11985 // identifier: keyword literal (true/false/null) or function call
11986 const char *s = p;
11987 while (p < end && ((*p >= 'a' && *p <= 'z') || (*p >= 'A' && *p <= 'Z') ||
11988 (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9') || *p == '_'))
11989 ++p;
11990 ::std::string id(s, static_cast<size_t>(p - s));
11991 if (id == "true") { Comparable cv; cv.t = Comparable::T::Bool; cv.b = true; return cv; }
11992 if (id == "false") { Comparable cv; cv.t = Comparable::T::Bool; cv.b = false; return cv; }
11993 if (id == "null") { Comparable cv; cv.t = Comparable::T::Null; return cv; }
11994 // RFC 9535 function-expr: the name is immediately followed by '(' — NO
11995 // whitespace between the function name and the opening parenthesis.
11996 if (p < end && *p == '(') {
11997 ++p;
11998 if (id == "length") {
11999 Comparable cv; cv.t = Comparable::T::Length;
12000 cv.len_arg = ::std::make_shared<Comparable>(parse_comparable());
12001 expect_char(')', "JSONPath: expected ')' after length() argument");
12002 return cv;
12003 }
12004 if (id == "count") {
12005 Comparable cv; cv.t = Comparable::T::Count;
12006 cv.fq = ::std::make_shared<FilterQuery>(parse_filter_query());
12007 expect_char(')', "JSONPath: expected ')' after count() argument");
12008 return cv;
12009 }
12010 if (id == "value") {
12011 Comparable cv; cv.t = Comparable::T::Value;
12012 cv.fq = ::std::make_shared<FilterQuery>(parse_filter_query());
12013 expect_char(')', "JSONPath: expected ')' after value() argument");
12014 return cv;
12015 }
12016 if (id == "match" || id == "search")
12017 fail("JSONPath: match()/search() (I-Regexp) are not supported");
12018 fail("JSONPath: unknown function in filter expression");
12019 }
12020 fail("JSONPath: unexpected token in filter expression");
12021 }
12022
12023 // A singular query: `@`/`$` then only single name/index steps (no wildcard,
12024 // descent, slice, union, or filter). Selects at most one node.
12025 SingularQuery parse_singular_query() {
12026 SingularQuery q;
12027 ws();
12028 if (p < end && *p == '$') { q.from_root = true; ++p; }
12029 else if (p < end && *p == '@') { ++p; }
12030 else fail("JSONPath: a query must start with '@' or '$'");
12031 while (true) {
12032 ws(); // RFC 9535: whitespace is allowed between segments of a query
12033 if (p < end && *p == '.' && !(p + 1 < end && p[1] == '.')) {
12034 ++p;
12035 SingularQuery::Step st; st.is_index = false; st.index = 0;
12036 st.name = parse_member_name();
12037 if (st.name.empty()) fail("JSONPath: expected member name in singular query");
12038 q.steps.push_back(::std::move(st));
12039 } else if (p < end && *p == '[') {
12040 ++p; ws();
12041 SingularQuery::Step st;
12042 if (p < end && (*p == '\'' || *p == '"')) {
12043 st.is_index = false; st.index = 0; st.name = parse_quoted(*p);
12044 } else {
12045 int64_t idx;
12046 if (!parse_int(idx))
12047 fail("JSONPath: singular query brackets accept only a name or index");
12048 st.is_index = true; st.index = idx;
12049 }
12050 expect_char(']', "JSONPath: expected ']' in singular query");
12051 q.steps.push_back(::std::move(st));
12052 } else {
12053 break;
12054 }
12055 }
12056 return q;
12057 }
12058
12059 // A filter query: `@`/`$` then arbitrary segments. May select many nodes.
12060 FilterQuery parse_filter_query() {
12061 FilterQuery q;
12062 ws();
12063 if (p < end && *p == '$') { q.from_root = true; ++p; }
12064 else if (p < end && *p == '@') { ++p; }
12065 else fail("JSONPath: a query must start with '@' or '$'");
12066 JpSegment seg;
12067 while (parse_one_segment(seg)) {
12068 q.segs.push_back(::std::move(seg));
12069 seg = JpSegment{};
12070 }
12071 return q;
12072 }
12073
12074 // RFC 9535 §2.3.5.2.1 number: (int / "-0") [frac] [exp]. int = "0" / (["-"]
12075 // [1-9][0-9]*). Strictly rejects leading zeros, a missing fractional digit
12076 // ("1."), and a missing exponent digit ("1e").
12077 Comparable parse_number_comparable() {
12078 const char *s = p;
12079 if (p < end && *p == '-') ++p;
12080 if (p >= end || *p < '0' || *p > '9') fail("JSONPath: invalid number literal");
12081 if (*p == '0') ++p; // lone 0 (or -0)
12082 else while (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') ++p;
12083 if (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') fail("JSONPath: leading zero in number");
12084 bool is_dbl = false;
12085 if (p < end && *p == '.') {
12086 is_dbl = true; ++p;
12087 if (p >= end || *p < '0' || *p > '9') fail("JSONPath: no digit after '.'");
12088 while (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') ++p;
12089 }
12090 if (p < end && (*p == 'e' || *p == 'E')) {
12091 is_dbl = true; ++p;
12092 if (p < end && (*p == '+' || *p == '-')) ++p;
12093 if (p >= end || *p < '0' || *p > '9') fail("JSONPath: no digit in exponent");
12094 while (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') ++p;
12095 }
12096 Comparable cv;
12097 if (is_dbl) {
12098 cv.t = Comparable::T::Dbl;
12099 cv.d = ::std::strtod(::std::string(s, static_cast<size_t>(p - s)).c_str(), nullptr);
12100 } else {
12101 int64_t v;
12102 auto [ptr, ec] = ::std::from_chars(s, p, v);
12103 (void)ptr;
12104 if (ec != ::std::errc{}) { // out of int64 range → fall back to double
12105 cv.t = Comparable::T::Dbl;
12106 cv.d = ::std::strtod(::std::string(s, static_cast<size_t>(p - s)).c_str(), nullptr);
12107 } else {
12108 cv.t = Comparable::T::Int; cv.i = v;
12109 }
12110 }
12111 return cv;
12112 }
12113
12114 // Reinterpret a parsed filter-query as a singular query (name/index steps
12115 // only); false if any segment is descendant, a union, or a non-name/index
12116 // selector.
12117 bool filter_query_to_singular(const FilterQuery &fq, Comparable &out) {
12118 auto sq = ::std::make_shared<SingularQuery>();
12119 sq->from_root = fq.from_root;
12120 for (const JpSegment &seg : fq.segs) {
12121 if (seg.descendant || seg.selectors.size() != 1) return false;
12122 const JpSelector &s = seg.selectors[0];
12123 if (s.kind == JpSelector::Kind::Name) {
12124 sq->steps.push_back({false, s.name, 0});
12125 } else if (s.kind == JpSelector::Kind::Index) {
12126 sq->steps.push_back({true, ::std::string(), s.index});
12127 } else {
12128 return false;
12129 }
12130 }
12131 out.t = Comparable::T::Singular;
12132 out.sq = ::std::move(sq);
12133 return true;
12134 }
12135};
12136
12137// Mutually-recursive evaluator: a filter selector evaluates a filter expression,
12138// whose existence tests / count() / value() run sub-queries (apply_segments),
12139// which may themselves apply more filter selectors.
12140inline ::std::vector<Value> apply_segments(const Value &start,
12141 const ::std::vector<JpSegment> &segs,
12142 const Value &root);
12143inline bool filter_eval(const FilterExpr &e, const Value &cur, const Value &root);
12144
12145// Recursion is bounded by the parser's kMaxDepth (1024) — `v` views a parsed
12146// tape, which cannot be nested deeper than the parser allowed, so `$..` over
12147// adversarial input can't overflow the stack.
12148inline void jp_collect_descendants(const Value &v, ::std::vector<Value> &out) {
12149 out.push_back(v);
12150 if (v.is_object()) {
12151 for (const auto &[k, val] : v.items()) { (void)k; jp_collect_descendants(val, out); }
12152 } else if (v.is_array()) {
12153 for (const auto &e : v.elements()) jp_collect_descendants(e, out);
12154 }
12155}
12156
12157inline void jp_apply_selector(const Value &v, const JpSelector &s,
12158 const Value &root, ::std::vector<Value> &out) {
12159 using K = JpSelector::Kind;
12160 if (s.kind == K::Filter) {
12161 // RFC 9535: a filter selector selects array elements and object member values
12162 // for which the expression tests true (current node `@` = each child).
12163 if (v.is_array()) {
12164 for (const auto &e : v.elements())
12165 if (filter_eval(*s.filter, e, root)) out.push_back(e);
12166 } else if (v.is_object()) {
12167 for (const auto &[k, val] : v.items()) { (void)k; if (filter_eval(*s.filter, val, root)) out.push_back(val); }
12168 }
12169 return;
12170 }
12171 if (s.kind == K::Name) {
12172 if (v.is_object()) {
12173 // Fast path: raw on-the-wire byte match (the common case).
12174 Value m = v[std::string_view(s.name)];
12175 if (m.is_valid()) { out.push_back(m); return; }
12176 // Slow path: the member's key may be escaped on the wire (control chars,
12177 // \uXXXX, surrogate pairs), so its raw bytes differ from the decoded
12178 // selector name. Compare decoded keys.
12179 for (const auto &[rk, val] : v.items())
12180 if (::qbuem::json::detail::json_unescape(rk) == s.name) { out.push_back(val); return; }
12181 }
12182 } else if (s.kind == K::Wildcard) {
12183 if (v.is_object()) { for (const auto &[k, val] : v.items()) { (void)k; out.push_back(val); } }
12184 else if (v.is_array()) { for (const auto &e : v.elements()) out.push_back(e); }
12185 } else if (s.kind == K::Index) {
12186 if (v.is_array()) {
12187 const int64_t n = static_cast<int64_t>(v.size());
12188 int64_t i = s.index < 0 ? n + s.index : s.index;
12189 if (i >= 0 && i < n) { Value e = v[static_cast<size_t>(i)]; if (e.is_valid()) out.push_back(e); }
12190 }
12191 } else { // Slice
12192 if (!v.is_array()) return;
12193 const int64_t n = static_cast<int64_t>(v.size());
12194 const int64_t step = s.s_step;
12195 if (step == 0) return; // RFC: step 0 selects nothing
12196 auto norm = [n](int64_t i) { return i >= 0 ? i : n + i; };
12197 if (step > 0) {
12198 int64_t lo = s.has_start ? norm(s.s_start) : 0;
12199 int64_t hi = s.has_end ? norm(s.s_end) : n;
12200 lo = lo < 0 ? 0 : (lo > n ? n : lo);
12201 hi = hi < 0 ? 0 : (hi > n ? n : hi);
12202 for (int64_t i = lo; i < hi; i += step) { Value e = v[static_cast<size_t>(i)]; if (e.is_valid()) out.push_back(e); }
12203 } else {
12204 int64_t up = s.has_start ? norm(s.s_start) : n - 1;
12205 int64_t lo = s.has_end ? norm(s.s_end) : -n - 1;
12206 up = up < -1 ? -1 : (up > n - 1 ? n - 1 : up);
12207 lo = lo < -1 ? -1 : (lo > n - 1 ? n - 1 : lo);
12208 for (int64_t i = up; i > lo; i += step) { Value e = v[static_cast<size_t>(i)]; if (e.is_valid()) out.push_back(e); }
12209 }
12210 }
12211}
12212
12213// Run a query's segments from `start`, threading the absolute `$` root through so
12214// nested filter selectors can evaluate `$`-rooted sub-queries.
12215inline ::std::vector<Value> apply_segments(const Value &start,
12216 const ::std::vector<JpSegment> &segs,
12217 const Value &root) {
12218 ::std::vector<Value> nodes;
12219 if (start.is_valid()) nodes.push_back(start);
12220 for (const JpSegment &seg : segs) {
12221 ::std::vector<Value> next;
12222 for (const Value &node : nodes) {
12223 if (seg.descendant) {
12224 ::std::vector<Value> desc;
12225 jp_collect_descendants(node, desc);
12226 for (const Value &d : desc)
12227 for (const JpSelector &s : seg.selectors) jp_apply_selector(d, s, root, next);
12228 } else {
12229 for (const JpSelector &s : seg.selectors) jp_apply_selector(node, s, root, next);
12230 }
12231 }
12232 nodes = ::std::move(next);
12233 }
12234 return nodes;
12235}
12236
12237// ── Filter evaluation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12238// A comparison operand's runtime value. Scalars normalise to a primitive kind;
12239// arrays/objects stay a Node (deep-equality compare); a query that selects
12240// nothing is Nothing (distinct from JSON null, per RFC 9535).
12241struct CmpVal {
12242 enum class K { Nothing, Null, Bool, Int, Dbl, Str, Node } k = K::Nothing;
12243 bool b = false;
12244 int64_t i = 0;
12245 double d = 0;
12246 ::std::string s;
12247 Value node;
12248};
12249
12250inline CmpVal cmpval_from_node(const Value &n) {
12251 CmpVal v;
12252 if (!n.is_valid()) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Nothing; return v; }
12253 if (n.is_null()) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Null; return v; }
12254 if (n.is_bool()) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Bool; v.b = n.template as<bool>(); return v; }
12255 if (n.is_int()) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Int; v.i = n.template as<int64_t>(); return v; }
12256 if (n.is_number()) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Dbl; v.d = n.template as<double>(); return v; }
12257 if (n.is_string()) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Str; v.s = n.decoded(); return v; }
12258 v.k = CmpVal::K::Node; v.node = n; // array / object
12259 return v;
12260}
12261
12262// Resolve a singular query (name/index steps only) to its one node, or an invalid
12263// Value (= Nothing) if any step misses.
12264inline Value resolve_singular(const SingularQuery &q, const Value &cur,
12265 const Value &root) {
12266 Value v = q.from_root ? root : cur;
12267 for (const auto &st : q.steps) {
12268 if (!v.is_valid()) return Value{};
12269 if (st.is_index) {
12270 if (!v.is_array()) return Value{};
12271 const int64_t n = static_cast<int64_t>(v.size());
12272 const int64_t idx = st.index < 0 ? n + st.index : st.index;
12273 if (idx < 0 || idx >= n) return Value{};
12274 v = v[static_cast<size_t>(idx)];
12275 } else {
12276 if (!v.is_object()) return Value{};
12277 v = v[::std::string_view(st.name)];
12278 }
12279 }
12280 return v;
12281}
12282
12283// length() per RFC 9535 §2.4.4: array elements / object members / string Unicode
12284// scalar values; -1 (→ Nothing) for anything else.
12285inline int64_t jp_node_length(const Value &n) {
12286 if (n.is_array()) return static_cast<int64_t>(n.size());
12287 if (n.is_object()) { int64_t c = 0; for (const auto &kv : n.items()) { (void)kv; ++c; } return c; }
12288 return -1;
12289}
12290inline int64_t utf8_scalar_count(::std::string_view s) {
12291 int64_t n = 0;
12292 for (unsigned char c : s) if ((c & 0xC0) != 0x80) ++n; // skip 10xxxxxx continuations
12293 return n;
12294}
12295
12296inline CmpVal eval_comparable(const Comparable &c, const Value &cur,
12297 const Value &root) {
12298 CmpVal v;
12299 switch (c.t) {
12300 case Comparable::T::Null: v.k = CmpVal::K::Null; return v;
12301 case Comparable::T::Bool: v.k = CmpVal::K::Bool; v.b = c.b; return v;
12302 case Comparable::T::Int: v.k = CmpVal::K::Int; v.i = c.i; return v;
12303 case Comparable::T::Dbl: v.k = CmpVal::K::Dbl; v.d = c.d; return v;
12304 case Comparable::T::Str: v.k = CmpVal::K::Str; v.s = c.s; return v;
12305 case Comparable::T::Singular:
12306 return cmpval_from_node(resolve_singular(*c.sq, cur, root));
12307 case Comparable::T::Count:
12308 v.k = CmpVal::K::Int;
12309 v.i = static_cast<int64_t>(
12310 apply_segments(c.fq->from_root ? root : cur, c.fq->segs, root).size());
12311 return v;
12312 case Comparable::T::Value: {
12313 auto nodes = apply_segments(c.fq->from_root ? root : cur, c.fq->segs, root);
12314 if (nodes.size() == 1) return cmpval_from_node(nodes[0]);
12315 v.k = CmpVal::K::Nothing; // empty or multiple → Nothing
12316 return v;
12317 }
12318 case Comparable::T::Length: {
12319 CmpVal a = eval_comparable(*c.len_arg, cur, root);
12320 if (a.k == CmpVal::K::Str) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Int; v.i = utf8_scalar_count(a.s); return v; }
12321 if (a.k == CmpVal::K::Node) {
12322 const int64_t len = jp_node_length(a.node);
12323 if (len >= 0) { v.k = CmpVal::K::Int; v.i = len; return v; }
12324 }
12325 v.k = CmpVal::K::Nothing; // length of a non-string/array/object → Nothing
12326 return v;
12327 }
12328 }
12329 v.k = CmpVal::K::Nothing;
12330 return v;
12331}
12332
12333inline bool cmpval_is_num(const CmpVal &v) {
12334 return v.k == CmpVal::K::Int || v.k == CmpVal::K::Dbl;
12335}
12336inline double cmpval_as_dbl(const CmpVal &v) {
12337 return v.k == CmpVal::K::Int ? static_cast<double>(v.i) : v.d;
12338}
12339
12340inline bool cmp_eq(const CmpVal &a, const CmpVal &b) {
12341 if (a.k == CmpVal::K::Nothing || b.k == CmpVal::K::Nothing)
12342 return a.k == CmpVal::K::Nothing && b.k == CmpVal::K::Nothing;
12343 if (cmpval_is_num(a) && cmpval_is_num(b)) {
12344 if (a.k == CmpVal::K::Int && b.k == CmpVal::K::Int) return a.i == b.i;
12345 return cmpval_as_dbl(a) == cmpval_as_dbl(b);
12346 }
12347 if (a.k != b.k) return false; // different non-numeric types are never equal
12348 switch (a.k) {
12349 case CmpVal::K::Null: return true;
12350 case CmpVal::K::Bool: return a.b == b.b;
12351 case CmpVal::K::Str: return a.s == b.s;
12352 case CmpVal::K::Node: return value_equal(a.node, b.node);
12353 default: return false;
12354 }
12355}
12356// Ordering is defined only for number/number and string/string (UTF-8 byte order
12357// == Unicode code-point order); every other operand pairing yields false.
12358inline bool cmp_lt(const CmpVal &a, const CmpVal &b) {
12359 if (cmpval_is_num(a) && cmpval_is_num(b)) {
12360 if (a.k == CmpVal::K::Int && b.k == CmpVal::K::Int) return a.i < b.i;
12361 return cmpval_as_dbl(a) < cmpval_as_dbl(b);
12362 }
12363 if (a.k == CmpVal::K::Str && b.k == CmpVal::K::Str) return a.s < b.s;
12364 return false;
12365}
12366inline bool cmp_apply(int op, const CmpVal &a, const CmpVal &b) {
12367 switch (op) {
12368 case 0: return cmp_eq(a, b); // ==
12369 case 1: return !cmp_eq(a, b); // !=
12370 case 2: return cmp_lt(a, b); // <
12371 case 3: return cmp_lt(a, b) || cmp_eq(a, b); // <=
12372 case 4: return cmp_lt(b, a); // >
12373 case 5: return cmp_lt(b, a) || cmp_eq(a, b); // >=
12374 default: return false;
12375 }
12376}
12377
12378inline bool filter_eval(const FilterExpr &e, const Value &cur, const Value &root) {
12379 switch (e.t) {
12380 case FilterExpr::T::Or:
12381 for (const FilterExpr &k : e.kids) if (filter_eval(k, cur, root)) return true;
12382 return false;
12383 case FilterExpr::T::And:
12384 for (const FilterExpr &k : e.kids) if (!filter_eval(k, cur, root)) return false;
12385 return true;
12386 case FilterExpr::T::Not:
12387 return !filter_eval(e.kids[0], cur, root);
12388 case FilterExpr::T::Exists:
12389 return !apply_segments(e.exists->from_root ? root : cur, e.exists->segs, root).empty();
12390 case FilterExpr::T::Cmp:
12391 return cmp_apply(e.op, eval_comparable(e.lhs, cur, root),
12392 eval_comparable(e.rhs, cur, root));
12393 }
12394 return false;
12395}
12396
12397} // namespace json::detail::jsonpath
12398
12399[[nodiscard]] inline ::std::vector<Value> query(const Value &root,
12400 ::std::string_view path) {
12401 using namespace json::detail::jsonpath;
12402 JpParser parser{path.data(), path.data(), path.data() + path.size()};
12403 const ::std::vector<JpSegment> segs = parser.parse();
12404 return apply_segments(root, segs, root);
12405}
12406
12407// jsonpath(root, path) — the RFC 9535 spelling, an exact alias for query(root,
12408// path). Returns every Value the path selects, in document order; the Values view
12409// into the same document as `root`, which must outlive them. (There is no
12410// string-input overload: it would parse into a temporary Document and return
12411// dangling views — parse the text yourself, then call jsonpath/query.)
12412[[nodiscard]] inline ::std::vector<Value> jsonpath(const Value &root,
12413 ::std::string_view path) {
12414 return query(root, path);
12415}
12416
12417// ── NDJSON / JSON Lines ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12418// Newline-delimited JSON: one JSON value per line (jsonlines.org / ndjson-spec).
12419// The dominant format for logs, ML datasets, and streamed LLM output. Records
12420// are decoded one at a time, so a multi-GB document is processed in bounded
12421// memory. Blank lines are skipped; a trailing '\r' (CRLF) is trimmed. A record
12422// that fails to parse throws qbuem::parse_error whose line()/column() are
12423// relative to that record.
12424
12425// True for a line that is empty or only ASCII whitespace.
12426namespace json::detail {
12427inline bool ndjson_blank_(::std::string_view s) noexcept {
12428 for (char c : s)
12429 if (static_cast<unsigned char>(c) > ' ') return false;
12430 return true;
12431}
12432} // namespace json::detail
12433
12434// read_lines<T>(text, fn) — invoke fn(T&&) for each record, in order. fn may be
12435// any callable taking a T by value/rvalue. Bounded memory: one Document and one
12436// T are reused across the whole stream.
12437template <typename T, typename F>
12438void read_lines(::std::string_view text, F &&fn) {
12439 Document doc; // reused across lines (no per-record tape allocation)
12440 ::std::size_t pos = 0;
12441 const ::std::size_t n = text.size();
12442 while (pos < n) {
12443 ::std::size_t nl = text.find('\n', pos);
12444 ::std::size_t stop = (nl == ::std::string_view::npos) ? n : nl;
12445 ::std::string_view line = text.substr(pos, stop - pos);
12446 if (!line.empty() && line.back() == '\r') line.remove_suffix(1);
12447 if (!json::detail::ndjson_blank_(line)) {
12448 Value root = json::parse_reuse(doc, line);
12449 T obj{};
12450 json::detail::from_json(root, obj);
12451 fn(static_cast<T &&>(obj));
12452 }
12453 pos = (nl == ::std::string_view::npos) ? n : nl + 1;
12454 }
12455}
12456
12457// read_lines<T>(text) — collect every record into a vector.
12458template <typename T>
12459[[nodiscard]] ::std::vector<T> read_lines(::std::string_view text) {
12460 ::std::vector<T> out;
12461 read_lines<T>(text, [&](T &&v) { out.push_back(static_cast<T &&>(v)); });
12462 return out;
12463}
12464
12465// write_lines(buf, range) — append each element of `range` as one NDJSON record
12466// (compact JSON + '\n') to buf, reusing its capacity. range is any iterable of a
12467// serializable T.
12468template <typename Range>
12469void write_lines(::std::string &buf, const Range &range) {
12470 for (const auto &item : range) {
12471 ::qbuem::json::detail::append_json(buf, item);
12472 buf += '\n';
12473 }
12474}
12475
12476template <typename Range>
12477[[nodiscard]] ::std::string write_lines(const Range &range) {
12478 ::std::string buf;
12479 write_lines(buf, range);
12480 return buf;
12481}
12482
12483// ── CBOR binary serialization (RFC 8949) ─────────────────────────────────────
12484// cbor::encode(obj) → compact, self-describing binary that decodes in any
12485// language (e.g. the JS `cbor-x` library) without a shared schema. Reuses the
12486// QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS field list — register a field once and it serializes to both
12487// JSON and CBOR. Bytes are returned in a std::string (a byte container here).
12488namespace cbor {
12489
12490template <typename T> void encode_to(::std::string &buf, const T &obj) {
12491 // Route through FastWriter (1 KB stack buffer, flushes to the string only when
12492 // full or on destruction) — the same zero-per-append-overhead path the JSON
12493 // serializer uses. The scope ends the writer, flushing the tail into `buf`.
12494 ::qbuem::json::detail::FastWriter w(buf);
12495 ::qbuem::json::detail::append_cbor(w, obj);
12496}
12497
12498template <typename T> [[nodiscard]] ::std::string encode(const T &obj) {
12499 ::std::string buf;
12500 { ::qbuem::json::detail::FastWriter w(buf);
12501 ::qbuem::json::detail::append_cbor(w, obj); }
12502 return buf;
12503}
12504
12505// decode<T>(bytes) → T. Inverse of encode: reads the CBOR data item into a T
12506// (any QBUEM_JSON_FIELDS struct or supported STL type). Throws qbuem::parse_error
12507// on a truncated, malformed, or type-mismatched payload — never reads out of
12508// bounds, so it is safe on untrusted network input. Trailing bytes after the
12509// top-level item are ignored (framed-message friendly).
12510template <typename T> [[nodiscard]] T decode(::std::string_view bytes) {
12511 ::qbuem::json::detail::CborReader cr(bytes.data(), bytes.size());
12512 T obj{};
12513 ::qbuem::json::detail::from_cbor(cr, obj);
12514 return obj;
12515}
12516
12517template <typename T>
12518[[nodiscard]] T decode(const ::std::uint8_t *data, ::std::size_t n) {
12519 return decode<T>(::std::string_view(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(data), n));
12520}
12521
12522// decode_into(bytes, obj) — fill an existing object (reuses its heap capacity).
12523template <typename T> void decode_into(::std::string_view bytes, T &obj) {
12524 ::qbuem::json::detail::CborReader cr(bytes.data(), bytes.size());
12525 ::qbuem::json::detail::from_cbor(cr, obj);
12526}
12527
12528} // namespace cbor

12530} // namespace qbuem
